3128.text: I understand more than the ancients, because I keep thy precepts.

3129.text: I have refrained my feet from every evil way, that I might keep thy word.

3130.text: I have not departed from thy judgments: for thou hast taught me.

3131.text: How sweet are thy words unto my taste! yea, sweeter than honey to my mouth!

3132.text: Through thy precepts I get understanding: therefore I hate every false way.

3133.text: Thy word is a lamp unto my feet, and a light unto my path.

3134.text: I have sworn, and I will perform it, that I will keep thy righteous judgments.

3135.text: I am afflicted very much: quicken me, O Lord, according unto thy word.

3136.text: Accept, I beseech thee, the freewill offerings of my mouth, O Lord, and teach me thy judgments.

3137.text: My soul is continually in my hand: yet do I not forget thy law.

3138.text: The wicked have laid a snare for me: yet I erred not from thy precepts.

3139.text: Thy testimonies have I taken as an heritage for ever: for they are the rejoicing of my heart.

3140.text: I have inclined mine heart to perform thy statutes alway, even unto the end.

3141.text: I hate vain thoughts: but thy law do I love.

3142.text: Thou art my hiding place and my shield: I hope in thy word.

3143.text: Depart from me, ye evildoers: for I will keep the commandments of my God.

3144.text: Uphold me according unto thy word, that I may live: and let me not be ashamed of my hope.

3145.text: Hold thou me up, and I shall be safe: and I will have respect unto thy statutes continually.

3146.text: Thou hast trodden down all them that err from thy statutes: for their deceit is falsehood.

3147.text: Thou puttest away all the wicked of the earth like dross: therefore I love thy testimonies.

3148.text: My flesh trembleth for fear of thee; and I am afraid of thy judgments.

3149.text: I have done judgment and justice: leave me not to mine oppressors.

3150.text: Be surety for thy servant for good: let not the proud oppress me.

3151.text: Mine eyes fail for thy salvation, and for the word of thy righteousness.

3152.text: Deal with thy servant according unto thy mercy, and teach me thy statutes.

3153.text: I am thy servant; give me understanding, that I may know thy testimonies.

3154.text: It is time for thee, Lord, to work: for they have made void thy law.

3155.text: Therefore I love thy commandments above gold; yea, above fine gold.

3156.text: Therefore I esteem all thy precepts concerning all things to be right; and I hate every false way.

3157.text: Thy testimonies are wonderful: therefore doth my soul keep them.

3158.text: The entrance of thy words giveth light; it giveth understanding unto the simple.

3159.text: I opened my mouth, and panted: for I longed for thy commandments.

3160.text: Look thou upon me, and be merciful unto me, as thou usest to do unto those that love thy name.

3161.text: Order my steps in thy word: and let not any iniquity have dominion over me.

3162.text: Deliver me from the oppression of man: so will I keep thy precepts.

3163.text: Make thy face to shine upon thy servant; and teach me thy statutes.

3164.text: Rivers of waters run down mine eyes, because they keep not thy law.

3165.text: Righteous art thou, O Lord, and upright are thy judgments.

3166.text: Thy testimonies that thou hast commanded are righteous and very faithful.

3167.text: My zeal hath consumed me, because mine enemies have forgotten thy words.

3168.text: Thy word is very pure: therefore thy servant loveth it.

3169.text: I am small and despised: yet do not I forget thy precepts.

3170.text: Thy righteousness is an everlasting righteousness, and thy law is the truth.

3171.text: Trouble and anguish have taken hold on me: yet thy commandments are my delights.

3172.text: The righteousness of thy testimonies is everlasting: give me understanding, and I shall live.

3173.text: I cried with my whole heart; hear me, O Lord: I will keep thy statutes.

3174.text: I cried unto thee; save me, and I shall keep thy testimonies.

3175.text: I prevented the dawning of the morning, and cried: I hoped in thy word.

3176.text: Mine eyes prevent the night watches, that I might meditate in thy word.

3177.text: Hear my voice according unto thy lovingkindness: O Lord, quicken me according to thy judgment.

3178.text: They draw nigh that follow after mischief: they are far from thy law.

3179.text: Thou art near, O Lord; and all thy commandments are truth.

3180.text: Concerning thy testimonies, I have known of old that thou hast founded them for ever.

3181.text: Consider mine affliction, and deliver me: for I do not forget thy law.

3182.text: Plead my cause, and deliver me: quicken me according to thy word.

3183.text: Salvation is far from the wicked: for they seek not thy statutes.

3184.text: Great are thy tender mercies, O Lord: quicken me according to thy judgments.

3185.text: Many are my persecutors and mine enemies; yet do I not decline from thy testimonies.

3186.text: I beheld the transgressors, and was grieved; because they kept not thy word.

3187.text: Consider how I love thy precepts: quicken me, O Lord, according to thy lovingkindness.

3188.text: Thy word is true from the beginning: and every one of thy righteous judgments endureth for ever.

3189.text: Princes have persecuted me without a cause: but my heart standeth in awe of thy word.

3190.text: I rejoice at thy word, as one that findeth great spoil.

3191.text: I hate and abhor lying: but thy law do I love.

3192.text: Seven times a day do I praise thee because of thy righteous judgments.

3193.text: Great peace have they which love thy law: and nothing shall offend them.

3194.text: Lord, I have hoped for thy salvation, and done thy commandments.

3195.text: My soul hath kept thy testimonies; and I love them exceedingly.

3196.text: I have kept thy precepts and thy testimonies: for all my ways are before thee.

3197.text: Let my cry come near before thee, O Lord: give me understanding according to thy word.

3198.text: Let my supplication come before thee: deliver me according to thy word.

3199.text: My lips shall utter praise, when thou hast taught me thy statutes.

3200.text: My tongue shall speak of thy word: for all thy commandments are righteousness.

3201.text: Let thine hand help me; for I have chosen thy precepts.

3202.text: I have longed for thy salvation, O Lord; and thy law is my delight.

3203.text: Let my soul live, and it shall praise thee; and let thy judgments help me.

3204.text: I have gone astray like a lost sheep; seek thy servant; for I do not forget thy commandments.

3205.text: In my distress I cried unto the Lord, and he heard me.

3206.text: Deliver my soul, O Lord, from lying lips, and from a deceitful tongue.

3207.text: What shall be given unto thee? or what shall be done unto thee, thou false tongue?

3208.text: Sharp arrows of the mighty, with coals of juniper.

3209.text: Woe is me, that I sojourn in Mesech, that I dwell in the tents of Kedar!

3210.text: My soul hath long dwelt with him that hateth peace.

3211.text: I am for peace: but when I speak, they are for war.

3212.text: I will lift up mine eyes unto the hills, from whence cometh my help.

3213.text: My help cometh from the Lord, which made heaven and earth.

3214.text: He will not suffer thy foot to be moved: he that keepeth thee will not slumber.

3215.text: Behold, he that keepeth Israel shall neither slumber nor sleep.

3216.text: The Lord is thy keeper: the Lord is thy shade upon thy right hand.

3217.text: The sun shall not smite thee by day, nor the moon by night.

3218.text: The Lord shall preserve thee from all evil: he shall preserve thy soul.

3219.text: The Lord shall preserve thy going out and thy coming in from this time forth, and even for evermore.

3220.text: I was glad when they said unto me, Let us go into the house of the Lord.

3221.text: Our feet shall stand within thy gates, O Jerusalem.

3222.text: Jerusalem is builded as a city that is compact together:

3223.text: Whither the tribes go up, the tribes of the Lord, unto the testimony of Israel, to give thanks unto the name of the Lord.

3224.text: For there are set thrones of judgment, the thrones of the house of David.

3225.text: Pray for the peace of Jerusalem: they shall prosper that love thee.

3226.text: Peace be within thy walls, and prosperity within thy palaces.

3227.text: For my brethren and companions’ sakes, I will now say, Peace be within thee.

3228.text: Because of the house of the Lord our God I will seek thy good.

3229.text: Unto thee lift I up mine eyes, O thou that dwellest in the heavens.

3230.text: Behold, as the eyes of servants look unto the hand of their masters, and as the eyes of a maiden unto the hand of her mistress; so our eyes wait upon the Lord our God, until that he have mercy upon us.

3231.text: Have mercy upon us, O Lord, have mercy upon us: for we are exceedingly filled with contempt.

3232.text: Our soul is exceedingly filled with the scorning of those that are at ease, and with the contempt of the proud.

3233.text: If it had not been the Lord who was on our side, now may Israel say;

3234.text: If it had not been the Lord who was on our side, when men rose up against us:

3235.text: Then they had swallowed us up quick, when their wrath was kindled against us:

3236.text: Then the waters had overwhelmed us, the stream had gone over our soul:

3237.text: Then the proud waters had gone over our soul.

3238.text: Blessed be the Lord, who hath not given us as a prey to their teeth.

3239.text: Our soul is escaped as a bird out of the snare of the fowlers: the snare is broken, and we are escaped.

3240.text: Our help is in the name of the Lord, who made heaven and earth.

3241.text: They that trust in the Lord shall be as mount Zion, which cannot be removed, but abideth for ever.

3242.text: As the mountains are round about Jerusalem, so the Lord is round about his people from henceforth even for ever.

3243.text: For the rod of the wicked shall not rest upon the lot of the righteous; lest the righteous put forth their hands unto iniquity.

3244.text: Do good, O Lord, unto those that be good, and to them that are upright in their hearts.

3245.text: As for such as turn aside unto their crooked ways, the Lord shall lead them forth with the workers of iniquity: but peace shall be upon Israel.

3246.text: When the Lord turned again the captivity of Zion, we were like them that dream.

3247.text: Then was our mouth filled with laughter, and our tongue with singing: then said they among the heathen, The Lord hath done great things for them.

3248.text: The Lord hath done great things for us; whereof we are glad.

3249.text: Turn again our captivity, O Lord, as the streams in the south.

3250.text: They that sow in tears shall reap in joy.

3251.text: He that goeth forth and weepeth, bearing precious seed, shall doubtless come again with rejoicing, bringing his sheaves with him.

3252.text: Except the Lord build the house, they labour in vain that build it: except the Lord keep the city, the watchman waketh but in vain.

3253.text: It is vain for you to rise up early, to sit up late, to eat the bread of sorrows: for so he giveth his beloved sleep.

3254.text: Lo, children are an heritage of the Lord: and the fruit of the womb is his reward.

3255.text: As arrows are in the hand of a mighty man; so are children of the youth.

3256.text: Happy is the man that hath his quiver full of them: they shall not be ashamed, but they shall speak with the enemies in the gate.

3257.text: Blessed is every one that feareth the Lord; that walketh in his ways.

3258.text: For thou shalt eat the labour of thine hands: happy shalt thou be, and it shall be well with thee.

3259.text: Thy wife shall be as a fruitful vine by the sides of thine house: thy children like olive plants round about thy table.

3260.text: Behold, that thus shall the man be blessed that feareth the Lord.

3261.text: The Lord shall bless thee out of Zion: and thou shalt see the good of Jerusalem all the days of thy life.

3262.text: Yea, thou shalt see thy children’s children, and peace upon Israel.

3263.text: Many a time have they afflicted me from my youth, may Israel now say:

3264.text: Many a time have they afflicted me from my youth: yet they have not prevailed against me.

3265.text: The plowers plowed upon my back: they made long their furrows.

3266.text: The Lord is righteous: he hath cut asunder the cords of the wicked.

3267.text: Let them all be confounded and turned back that hate Zion.

3268.text: Let them be as the grass upon the housetops, which withereth afore it groweth up:

3269.text: Wherewith the mower filleth not his hand; nor he that bindeth sheaves his bosom.

3270.text: Neither do they which go by say, The blessing of the Lord be upon you: we bless you in the name of the Lord.

3271.text: Out of the depths have I cried unto thee, O Lord.

3272.text: Lord, hear my voice: let thine ears be attentive to the voice of my supplications.

3273.text: If thou, Lord, shouldest mark iniquities, O Lord, who shall stand?

3274.text: But there is forgiveness with thee, that thou mayest be feared.

3275.text: I wait for the Lord, my soul doth wait, and in his word do I hope.

3276.text: My soul waiteth for the Lord more than they that watch for the morning: I say, more than they that watch for the morning.

3277.text: Let Israel hope in the Lord: for with the Lord there is mercy, and with him is plenteous redemption.

3278.text: And he shall redeem Israel from all his iniquities.

3279.text: Lord, my heart is not haughty, nor mine eyes lofty: neither do I exercise myself in great matters, or in things too high for me.

3280.text: Surely I have behaved and quieted myself, as a child that is weaned of his mother: my soul is even as a weaned child.

3281.text: Let Israel hope in the Lord from henceforth and for ever.

3282.text: Lord, remember David, and all his afflictions:

3283.text: How he sware unto the Lord, and vowed unto the mighty God of Jacob;

3284.text: Surely I will not come into the tabernacle of my house, nor go up into my bed;

3285.text: I will not give sleep to mine eyes, or slumber to mine eyelids,

3286.text: Until I find out a place for the Lord, an habitation for the mighty God of Jacob.

3287.text: Lo, we heard of it at Ephratah: we found it in the fields of the wood.

3288.text: We will go into his tabernacles: we will worship at his footstool.

3289.text: Arise, O Lord, into thy rest; thou, and the ark of thy strength.

3290.text: Let thy priests be clothed with righteousness; and let thy saints shout for joy.

3291.text: For thy servant David’s sake turn not away the face of thine anointed.

3292.text: The Lord hath sworn in truth unto David; he will not turn from it; Of the fruit of thy body will I set upon thy throne.

3293.text: If thy children will keep my covenant and my testimony that I shall teach them, their children shall also sit upon thy throne for evermore.

3294.text: For the Lord hath chosen Zion; he hath desired it for his habitation.

3295.text: This is my rest for ever: here will I dwell; for I have desired it.

3296.text: I will abundantly bless her provision: I will satisfy her poor with bread.

3297.text: I will also clothe her priests with salvation: and her saints shall shout aloud for joy.

3298.text: There will I make the horn of David to bud: I have ordained a lamp for mine anointed.

3299.text: His enemies will I clothe with shame: but upon himself shall his crown flourish.

3300.text: Behold, how good and how pleasant it is for brethren to dwell together in unity!

3301.text: It is like the precious ointment upon the head, that ran down upon the beard, even Aaron’s beard: that went down to the skirts of his garments;

3302.text: As the dew of Hermon, and as the dew that descended upon the mountains of Zion: for there the Lord commanded the blessing, even life for evermore.

3303.text: Behold, bless ye the Lord, all ye servants of the Lord, which by night stand in the house of the Lord.

3304.text: Lift up your hands in the sanctuary, and bless the Lord.

3305.text: The Lord that made heaven and earth bless thee out of Zion.

3306.text: Praise ye the Lord. Praise ye the name of the Lord; praise him, O ye servants of the Lord.

3307.text: Ye that stand in the house of the Lord, in the courts of the house of our God,

3308.text: Praise the Lord; for the Lord is good: sing praises unto his name; for it is pleasant.

3309.text: For the Lord hath chosen Jacob unto himself, and Israel for his peculiar treasure.

3310.text: For I know that the Lord is great, and that our Lord is above all gods.

3311.text: Whatsoever the Lord pleased, that did he in heaven, and in earth, in the seas, and all deep places.

3312.text: He causeth the vapours to ascend from the ends of the earth; he maketh lightnings for the rain; he bringeth the wind out of his treasuries.

3313.text: Who smote the firstborn of Egypt, both of man and beast.

3314.text: Who sent tokens and wonders into the midst of thee, O Egypt, upon Pharaoh, and upon all his servants.

3315.text: Who smote great nations, and slew mighty kings;

3316.text: Sihon king of the Amorites, and Og king of Bashan, and all the kingdoms of Canaan:

3317.text: And gave their land for an heritage, an heritage unto Israel his people.

3318.text: Thy name, O Lord, endureth for ever; and thy memorial, O Lord, throughout all generations.

3319.text: For the Lord will judge his people, and he will repent himself concerning his servants.

3320.text: The idols of the heathen are silver and gold, the work of men’s hands.

3321.text: They have mouths, but they speak not; eyes have they, but they see not;

3322.text: They have ears, but they hear not; neither is there any breath in their mouths.

3323.text: They that make them are like unto them: so is every one that trusteth in them.

3324.text: Bless the Lord, O house of Israel: bless the Lord, O house of Aaron:

3325.text: Bless the Lord, O house of Levi: ye that fear the Lord, bless the Lord.

3326.text: Blessed be the Lord out of Zion, which dwelleth at Jerusalem. Praise ye the Lord.

3327.text: O give thanks unto the Lord; for he is good: for his mercy endureth for ever.

3328.text: O give thanks unto the God of gods: for his mercy endureth for ever.

3329.text: O give thanks to the Lord of lords: for his mercy endureth for ever.

3330.text: To him who alone doeth great wonders: for his mercy endureth for ever.

3331.text: To him that by wisdom made the heavens: for his mercy endureth for ever.

3332.text: To him that stretched out the earth above the waters: for his mercy endureth for ever.

3333.text: To him that made great lights: for his mercy endureth for ever:

3334.text: The sun to rule by day: for his mercy endureth for ever:

3335.text: The moon and stars to rule by night: for his mercy endureth for ever.

3336.text: To him that smote Egypt in their firstborn: for his mercy endureth for ever:

3337.text: And brought out Israel from among them: for his mercy endureth for ever:

3338.text: With a strong hand, and with a stretched out arm: for his mercy endureth for ever.

3339.text: To him which divided the Red sea into parts: for his mercy endureth for ever:

3340.text: And made Israel to pass through the midst of it: for his mercy endureth for ever:

3341.text: But overthrew Pharaoh and his host in the Red sea: for his mercy endureth for ever.

3342.text: To him which led his people through the wilderness: for his mercy endureth for ever.

3343.text: To him which smote great kings: for his mercy endureth for ever:

3344.text: And slew famous kings: for his mercy endureth for ever:

3345.text: Sihon king of the Amorites: for his mercy endureth for ever:

3346.text: And Og the king of Bashan: for his mercy endureth for ever:

3347.text: And gave their land for an heritage: for his mercy endureth for ever:

3348.text: Even an heritage unto Israel his servant: for his mercy endureth for ever.

3349.text: Who remembered us in our low estate: for his mercy endureth for ever:

3350.text: And hath redeemed us from our enemies: for his mercy endureth for ever.

3351.text: Who giveth food to all flesh: for his mercy endureth for ever.

3352.text: O give thanks unto the God of heaven: for his mercy endureth for ever.

3353.text: By the rivers of Babylon, there we sat down, yea, we wept, when we remembered Zion.

3354.text: We hanged our harps upon the willows in the midst thereof.

3355.text: For there they that carried us away captive required of us a song; and they that wasted us required of us mirth, saying, Sing us one of the songs of Zion.

3356.text: How shall we sing the Lord’s song in a strange land?

3357.text: If I forget thee, O Jerusalem, let my right hand forget her cunning.

3358.text: If I do not remember thee, let my tongue cleave to the roof of my mouth; if I prefer not Jerusalem above my chief joy.

3359.text: Remember, O Lord, the children of Edom in the day of Jerusalem; who said, Rase it, rase it, even to the foundation thereof.

3360.text: O daughter of Babylon, who art to be destroyed; happy shall he be, that rewardeth thee as thou hast served us.

3361.text: Happy shall he be, that taketh and dasheth thy little ones against the stones.

3362.text: I will praise thee with my whole heart: before the gods will I sing praise unto thee.

3363.text: I will worship toward thy holy temple, and praise thy name for thy lovingkindness and for thy truth: for thou hast magnified thy word above all thy name.

3364.text: In the day when I cried thou answeredst me, and strengthenedst me with strength in my soul.

3365.text: All the kings of the earth shall praise thee, O Lord, when they hear the words of thy mouth.

3366.text: Yea, they shall sing in the ways of the Lord: for great is the glory of the Lord.

3367.text: Though the Lord be high, yet hath he respect unto the lowly: but the proud he knoweth afar off.

3368.text: Though I walk in the midst of trouble, thou wilt revive me: thou shalt stretch forth thine hand against the wrath of mine enemies, and thy right hand shall save me.

3369.text: The Lord will perfect that which concerneth me: thy mercy, O Lord, endureth for ever: forsake not the works of thine own hands.

3370.text: O Lord, thou hast searched me, and known me.

3371.text: Thou knowest my downsitting and mine uprising, thou understandest my thought afar off.

3372.text: Thou compassest my path and my lying down, and art acquainted with all my ways.

3373.text: For there is not a word in my tongue, but, lo, O Lord, thou knowest it altogether.

3374.text: Thou hast beset me behind and before, and laid thine hand upon me.

3375.text: Such knowledge is too wonderful for me; it is high, I cannot attain unto it.

3376.text: Whither shall I go from thy spirit? or whither shall I flee from thy presence?

3377.text: If I ascend up into heaven, thou art there: if I make my bed in hell, behold, thou art there.

3378.text: If I take the wings of the morning, and dwell in the uttermost parts of the sea;

3379.text: Even there shall thy hand lead me, and thy right hand shall hold me.

3380.text: If I say, Surely the darkness shall cover me; even the night shall be light about me.

3381.text: Yea, the darkness hideth not from thee; but the night shineth as the day: the darkness and the light are both alike to thee.

3382.text: For thou hast possessed my reins: thou hast covered me in my mother’s womb.

3383.text: I will praise thee; for I am fearfully and wonderfully made: marvellous are thy works; and that my soul knoweth right well.

3384.text: My substance was not hid from thee, when I was made in secret, and curiously wrought in the lowest parts of the earth.

3385.text: Thine eyes did see my substance, yet being unperfect; and in thy book all my members were written, which in continuance were fashioned, when as yet there was none of them.

3386.text: How precious also are thy thoughts unto me, O God! how great is the sum of them!

3387.text: If I should count them, they are more in number than the sand: when I awake, I am still with thee.

3388.text: Surely thou wilt slay the wicked, O God: depart from me therefore, ye bloody men.

3389.text: For they speak against thee wickedly, and thine enemies take thy name in vain.

3390.text: Do not I hate them, O Lord, that hate thee? and am not I grieved with those that rise up against thee?

3391.text: I hate them with perfect hatred: I count them mine enemies.

3392.text: Search me, O God, and know my heart: try me, and know my thoughts:

3393.text: And see if there be any wicked way in me, and lead me in the way everlasting.

3394.text: Deliver me, O Lord, from the evil man: preserve me from the violent man;

3395.text: Which imagine mischiefs in their heart; continually are they gathered together for war.

3396.text: They have sharpened their tongues like a serpent; adders’ poison is under their lips. Selah.

3397.text: Keep me, O Lord, from the hands of the wicked; preserve me from the violent man; who have purposed to overthrow my goings.

3398.text: The proud have hid a snare for me, and cords; they have spread a net by the wayside; they have set gins for me. Selah.

3399.text: I said unto the Lord, Thou art my God: hear the voice of my supplications, O Lord.

3400.text: O God the Lord, the strength of my salvation, thou hast covered my head in the day of battle.

3401.text: Grant not, O Lord, the desires of the wicked: further not his wicked device; lest they exalt themselves. Selah.

3402.text: As for the head of those that compass me about, let the mischief of their own lips cover them.

3403.text: Let burning coals fall upon them: let them be cast into the fire; into deep pits, that they rise not up again.

3404.text: Let not an evil speaker be established in the earth: evil shall hunt the violent man to overthrow him.

3405.text: I know that the Lord will maintain the cause of the afflicted, and the right of the poor.

3406.text: Surely the righteous shall give thanks unto thy name: the upright shall dwell in thy presence.

3407.text: Lord, I cry unto thee: make haste unto me; give ear unto my voice, when I cry unto thee.

3408.text: Let my prayer be set forth before thee as incense; and the lifting up of my hands as the evening sacrifice.

3409.text: Set a watch, O Lord, before my mouth; keep the door of my lips.

3410.text: Incline not my heart to any evil thing, to practise wicked works with men that work iniquity: and let me not eat of their dainties.

3411.text: Let the righteous smite me; it shall be a kindness: and let him reprove me; it shall be an excellent oil, which shall not break my head: for yet my prayer also shall be in their calamities.

3412.text: When their judges are overthrown in stony places, they shall hear my words; for they are sweet.

3413.text: Our bones are scattered at the grave’s mouth, as when one cutteth and cleaveth wood upon the earth.

3414.text: But mine eyes are unto thee, O God the Lord: in thee is my trust; leave not my soul destitute.

3415.text: Keep me from the snares which they have laid for me, and the gins of the workers of iniquity.

3416.text: Let the wicked fall into their own nets, whilst that I withal escape.

3417.text: I cried unto the Lord with my voice; with my voice unto the Lord did I make my supplication.

3418.text: I poured out my complaint before him; I shewed before him my trouble.

3419.text: When my spirit was overwhelmed within me, then thou knewest my path. In the way wherein I walked have they privily laid a snare for me.

3420.text: I looked on my right hand, and beheld, but there was no man that would know me: refuge failed me; no man cared for my soul.

3421.text: I cried unto thee, O Lord: I said, Thou art my refuge and my portion in the land of the living.

3422.text: Attend unto my cry; for I am brought very low: deliver me from my persecutors; for they are stronger than I.

3423.text: Bring my soul out of prison, that I may praise thy name: the righteous shall compass me about; for thou shalt deal bountifully with me.

3424.text: Hear my prayer, O Lord, give ear to my supplications: in thy faithfulness answer me, and in thy righteousness.

3425.text: And enter not into judgment with thy servant: for in thy sight shall no man living be justified.

3426.text: For the enemy hath persecuted my soul; he hath smitten my life down to the ground; he hath made me to dwell in darkness, as those that have been long dead.

3427.text: Therefore is my spirit overwhelmed within me; my heart within me is desolate.

3428.text: I remember the days of old; I meditate on all thy works; I muse on the work of thy hands.

3429.text: I stretch forth my hands unto thee: my soul thirsteth after thee, as a thirsty land. Selah.

3430.text: Hear me speedily, O Lord: my spirit faileth: hide not thy face from me, lest I be like unto them that go down into the pit.

3431.text: Cause me to hear thy lovingkindness in the morning; for in thee do I trust: cause me to know the way wherein I should walk; for I lift up my soul unto thee.

3432.text: Deliver me, O Lord, from mine enemies: I flee unto thee to hide me.

3433.text: Teach me to do thy will; for thou art my God: thy spirit is good; lead me into the land of uprightness.

3434.text: Quicken me, O Lord, for thy name’s sake: for thy righteousness’ sake bring my soul out of trouble.

3435.text: And of thy mercy cut off mine enemies, and destroy all them that afflict my soul: for I am thy servant.

3436.text: Blessed be the Lord my strength, which teacheth my hands to war, and my fingers to fight:

3437.text: My goodness, and my fortress; my high tower, and my deliverer; my shield, and he in whom I trust; who subdueth my people under me.

3438.text: Lord, what is man, that thou takest knowledge of him! or the son of man, that thou makest account of him!

3439.text: Man is like to vanity: his days are as a shadow that passeth away.

3440.text: Bow thy heavens, O Lord, and come down: touch the mountains, and they shall smoke.

3441.text: Cast forth lightning, and scatter them: shoot out thine arrows, and destroy them.

3442.text: Send thine hand from above; rid me, and deliver me out of great waters, from the hand of strange children;

3443.text: Whose mouth speaketh vanity, and their right hand is a right hand of falsehood.

3444.text: I will sing a new song unto thee, O God: upon a psaltery and an instrument of ten strings will I sing praises unto thee.

3445.text: It is he that giveth salvation unto kings: who delivereth David his servant from the hurtful sword.

3446.text: Rid me, and deliver me from the hand of strange children, whose mouth speaketh vanity, and their right hand is a right hand of falsehood:

3447.text: That our sons may be as plants grown up in their youth; that our daughters may be as corner stones, polished after the similitude of a palace:

3448.text: That our garners may be full, affording all manner of store: that our sheep may bring forth thousands and ten thousands in our streets:

3449.text: That our oxen may be strong to labour; that there be no breaking in, nor going out; that there be no complaining in our streets.

3450.text: Happy is that people, that is in such a case: yea, happy is that people, whose God is the Lord.

3451.text: I will extol thee, my God, O king; and I will bless thy name for ever and ever.

3452.text: Every day will I bless thee; and I will praise thy name for ever and ever.

3453.text: Great is the Lord, and greatly to be praised; and his greatness is unsearchable.

3454.text: One generation shall praise thy works to another, and shall declare thy mighty acts.

3455.text: I will speak of the glorious honour of thy majesty, and of thy wondrous works.

3456.text: And men shall speak of the might of thy terrible acts: and I will declare thy greatness.

3457.text: They shall abundantly utter the memory of thy great goodness, and shall sing of thy righteousness.

3458.text: The Lord is gracious, and full of compassion; slow to anger, and of great mercy.

3459.text: The Lord is good to all: and his tender mercies are over all his works.

3460.text: All thy works shall praise thee, O Lord; and thy saints shall bless thee.

3461.text: They shall speak of the glory of thy kingdom, and talk of thy power;

3462.text: To make known to the sons of men his mighty acts, and the glorious majesty of his kingdom.

3463.text: Thy kingdom is an everlasting kingdom, and thy dominion endureth throughout all generations.

3464.text: The Lord upholdeth all that fall, and raiseth up all those that be bowed down.

3465.text: The eyes of all wait upon thee; and thou givest them their meat in due season.

3466.text: Thou openest thine hand, and satisfiest the desire of every living thing.

3467.text: The Lord is righteous in all his ways, and holy in all his works.

3468.text: The Lord is nigh unto all them that call upon him, to all that call upon him in truth.

3469.text: He will fulfil the desire of them that fear him: he also will hear their cry, and will save them.

3470.text: The Lord preserveth all them that love him: but all the wicked will he destroy.

3471.text: My mouth shall speak the praise of the Lord: and let all flesh bless his holy name for ever and ever.

3472.text: Praise ye the Lord. Praise the Lord, O my soul.

3473.text: While I live will I praise the Lord: I will sing praises unto my God while I have any being.

3474.text: Put not your trust in princes, nor in the son of man, in whom there is no help.

3475.text: His breath goeth forth, he returneth to his earth; in that very day his thoughts perish.

3476.text: Happy is he that hath the God of Jacob for his help, whose hope is in the Lord his God:

3477.text: Which made heaven, and earth, the sea, and all that therein is: which keepeth truth for ever:

3478.text: Which executeth judgment for the oppressed: which giveth food to the hungry. The Lord looseth the prisoners:

3479.text: The Lord openeth the eyes of the blind: the Lord raiseth them that are bowed down: the Lord loveth the righteous:

3480.text: The Lord preserveth the strangers; he relieveth the fatherless and widow: but the way of the wicked he turneth upside down.

3481.text: The Lord shall reign for ever, even thy God, O Zion, unto all generations. Praise ye the Lord.

3482.text: Praise ye the Lord: for it is good to sing praises unto our God; for it is pleasant; and praise is comely.

3483.text: The Lord doth build up Jerusalem: he gathereth together the outcasts of Israel.

3484.text: He healeth the broken in heart, and bindeth up their wounds.

3485.text: He telleth the number of the stars; he calleth them all by their names.

3486.text: Great is our Lord, and of great power: his understanding is infinite.

3487.text: The Lord lifteth up the meek: he casteth the wicked down to the ground.

3488.text: Sing unto the Lord with thanksgiving; sing praise upon the harp unto our God:

3489.text: Who covereth the heaven with clouds, who prepareth rain for the earth, who maketh grass to grow upon the mountains.

3490.text: He giveth to the beast his food, and to the young ravens which cry.

3491.text: He delighteth not in the strength of the horse: he taketh not pleasure in the legs of a man.

3492.text: The Lord taketh pleasure in them that fear him, in those that hope in his mercy.

3493.text: Praise the Lord, O Jerusalem; praise thy God, O Zion.

3494.text: For he hath strengthened the bars of thy gates; he hath blessed thy children within thee.

3495.text: He maketh peace in thy borders, and filleth thee with the finest of the wheat.

3496.text: He sendeth forth his commandment upon earth: his word runneth very swiftly.

3497.text: He giveth snow like wool: he scattereth the hoarfrost like ashes.

3498.text: He casteth forth his ice like morsels: who can stand before his cold?

3499.text: He sendeth out his word, and melteth them: he causeth his wind to blow, and the waters flow.

3500.text: He sheweth his word unto Jacob, his statutes and his judgments unto Israel.

3501.text: He hath not dealt so with any nation: and as for his judgments, they have not known them. Praise ye the Lord.

3502.text: Praise ye the Lord. Praise ye the Lord from the heavens: praise him in the heights.

3503.text: Praise ye him, all his angels: praise ye him, all his hosts.

3504.text: Praise ye him, sun and moon: praise him, all ye stars of light.

3505.text: Praise him, ye heavens of heavens, and ye waters that be above the heavens.

3506.text: Let them praise the name of the Lord: for he commanded, and they were created.

3507.text: He hath also stablished them for ever and ever: he hath made a decree which shall not pass.

3508.text: Praise the Lord from the earth, ye dragons, and all deeps:

3509.text: Fire, and hail; snow, and vapour; stormy wind fulfilling his word:

3510.text: Mountains, and all hills; fruitful trees, and all cedars:

3511.text: Beasts, and all cattle; creeping things, and flying fowl:

3512.text: Kings of the earth, and all people; princes, and all judges of the earth:

3513.text: Both young men, and maidens; old men, and children:

3514.text: Let them praise the name of the Lord: for his name alone is excellent; his glory is above the earth and heaven.

3515.text: He also exalteth the horn of his people, the praise of all his saints; even of the children of Israel, a people near unto him. Praise ye the Lord.

3516.text: Praise ye the Lord. Sing unto the Lord a new song, and his praise in the congregation of saints.

3517.text: Let Israel rejoice in him that made him: let the children of Zion be joyful in their King.

3518.text: Let them praise his name in the dance: let them sing praises unto him with the timbrel and harp.

3519.text: For the Lord taketh pleasure in his people: he will beautify the meek with salvation.

3520.text: Let the saints be joyful in glory: let them sing aloud upon their beds.

3521.text: Let the high praises of God be in their mouth, and a twoedged sword in their hand;

3522.text: To execute vengeance upon the heathen, and punishments upon the people;

3523.text: To bind their kings with chains, and their nobles with fetters of iron;

3524.text: To execute upon them the judgment written: this honour have all his saints. Praise ye the Lord.

3525.text: Praise ye the Lord. Praise God in his sanctuary: praise him in the firmament of his power.

3526.text: Praise him for his mighty acts: praise him according to his excellent greatness.

3527.text: Praise him with the sound of the trumpet: praise him with the psaltery and harp.

3528.text: Praise him with the timbrel and dance: praise him with stringed instruments and organs.

3529.text: Praise him upon the loud cymbals: praise him upon the high sounding cymbals.

3530.text: Let every thing that hath breath praise the Lord. Praise ye the Lord.

3531.text: The proverbs of Solomon the son of David, king of Israel;

3532.text: To know wisdom and instruction; to perceive the words of understanding;

3533.text: To receive the instruction of wisdom, justice, and judgment, and equity;

3534.text: To give subtilty to the simple, to the young man knowledge and discretion.

3535.text: A wise man will hear, and will increase learning; and a man of understanding shall attain unto wise counsels:

3536.text: To understand a proverb, and the interpretation; the words of the wise, and their dark sayings.

3537.text: The fear of the Lord is the beginning of knowledge: but fools despise wisdom and instruction.

3538.text: My son, hear the instruction of thy father, and forsake not the law of thy mother:

3539.text: For they shall be an ornament of grace unto thy head, and chains about thy neck.

3540.text: My son, if sinners entice thee, consent thou not.

3541.text: If they say, Come with us, let us lay wait for blood, let us lurk privily for the innocent without cause:

3542.text: Let us swallow them up alive as the grave; and whole, as those that go down into the pit:

3543.text: We shall find all precious substance, we shall fill our houses with spoil:

3544.text: Cast in thy lot among us; let us all have one purse:

3545.text: My son, walk not thou in the way with them; refrain thy foot from their path:

3546.text: For their feet run to evil, and make haste to shed blood.

3547.text: Surely in vain the net is spread in the sight of any bird.

3548.text: And they lay wait for their own blood; they lurk privily for their own lives.

3549.text: So are the ways of every one that is greedy of gain; which taketh away the life of the owners thereof.

3550.text: Wisdom crieth without; she uttereth her voice in the streets:

3551.text: She crieth in the chief place of concourse, in the openings of the gates: in the city she uttereth her words, saying,

3552.text: How long, ye simple ones, will ye love simplicity? and the scorners delight in their scorning, and fools hate knowledge?

3553.text: Turn you at my reproof: behold, I will pour out my spirit unto you, I will make known my words unto you.

3554.text: Because I have called, and ye refused; I have stretched out my hand, and no man regarded;

3555.text: But ye have set at nought all my counsel, and would none of my reproof:

3556.text: I also will laugh at your calamity; I will mock when your fear cometh;

3557.text: When your fear cometh as desolation, and your destruction cometh as a whirlwind; when distress and anguish cometh upon you.

3558.text: Then shall they call upon me, but I will not answer; they shall seek me early, but they shall not find me:

3559.text: For that they hated knowledge, and did not choose the fear of the Lord:

3560.text: They would none of my counsel: they despised all my reproof.

3561.text: Therefore shall they eat of the fruit of their own way, and be filled with their own devices.

3562.text: For the turning away of the simple shall slay them, and the prosperity of fools shall destroy them.

3563.text: But whoso hearkeneth unto me shall dwell safely, and shall be quiet from fear of evil.

3564.text: My son, if thou wilt receive my words, and hide my commandments with thee;

3565.text: So that thou incline thine ear unto wisdom, and apply thine heart to understanding;

3566.text: Yea, if thou criest after knowledge, and liftest up thy voice for understanding;

3567.text: If thou seekest her as silver, and searchest for her as for hid treasures;

3568.text: Then shalt thou understand the fear of the Lord, and find the knowledge of God.

3569.text: For the Lord giveth wisdom: out of his mouth cometh knowledge and understanding.

3570.text: He layeth up sound wisdom for the righteous: he is a buckler to them that walk uprightly.

3571.text: He keepeth the paths of judgment, and preserveth the way of his saints.

3572.text: Then shalt thou understand righteousness, and judgment, and equity; yea, every good path.

3573.text: When wisdom entereth into thine heart, and knowledge is pleasant unto thy soul;

3574.text: Discretion shall preserve thee, understanding shall keep thee:

3575.text: To deliver thee from the way of the evil man, from the man that speaketh froward things;

3576.text: Who leave the paths of uprightness, to walk in the ways of darkness;

3577.text: Who rejoice to do evil, and delight in the frowardness of the wicked;

3578.text: Whose ways are crooked, and they froward in their paths:

3579.text: To deliver thee from the strange woman, even from the stranger which flattereth with her words;

3580.text: Which forsaketh the guide of her youth, and forgetteth the covenant of her God.

3581.text: For her house inclineth unto death, and her paths unto the dead.

3582.text: None that go unto her return again, neither take they hold of the paths of life.

3583.text: That thou mayest walk in the way of good men, and keep the paths of the righteous.

3584.text: For the upright shall dwell in the land, and the perfect shall remain in it.

3585.text: But the wicked shall be cut off from the earth, and the transgressors shall be rooted out of it.

3586.text: My son, forget not my law; but let thine heart keep my commandments:

3587.text: For length of days, and long life, and peace, shall they add to thee.

3588.text: Let not mercy and truth forsake thee: bind them about thy neck; write them upon the table of thine heart:

3589.text: So shalt thou find favour and good understanding in the sight of God and man.

3590.text: Trust in the Lord with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding.

3591.text: In all thy ways acknowledge him, and he shall direct thy paths.

3592.text: Be not wise in thine own eyes: fear the Lord, and depart from evil.

3593.text: It shall be health to thy navel, and marrow to thy bones.

3594.text: Honour the Lord with thy substance, and with the firstfruits of all thine increase:

3595.text: So shall thy barns be filled with plenty, and thy presses shall burst out with new wine.

3596.text: My son, despise not the chastening of the Lord; neither be weary of his correction:

3597.text: For whom the Lord loveth he correcteth; even as a father the son in whom he delighteth.

3598.text: Happy is the man that findeth wisdom, and the man that getteth understanding.

3599.text: For the merchandise of it is better than the merchandise of silver, and the gain thereof than fine gold.

3600.text: She is more precious than rubies: and all the things thou canst desire are not to be compared unto her.

3601.text: Length of days is in her right hand; and in her left hand riches and honour.

3602.text: Her ways are ways of pleasantness, and all her paths are peace.

3603.text: She is a tree of life to them that lay hold upon her: and happy is every one that retaineth her.

3604.text: The Lord by wisdom hath founded the earth; by understanding hath he established the heavens.

3605.text: By his knowledge the depths are broken up, and the clouds drop down the dew.

3606.text: My son, let not them depart from thine eyes: keep sound wisdom and discretion:

3607.text: So shall they be life unto thy soul, and grace to thy neck.

3608.text: Then shalt thou walk in thy way safely, and thy foot shall not stumble.

3609.text: When thou liest down, thou shalt not be afraid: yea, thou shalt lie down, and thy sleep shall be sweet.

3610.text: Be not afraid of sudden fear, neither of the desolation of the wicked, when it cometh.

3611.text: For the Lord shall be thy confidence, and shall keep thy foot from being taken.

3612.text: Withhold not good from them to whom it is due, when it is in the power of thine hand to do it.

3613.text: Say not unto thy neighbour, Go, and come again, and to morrow I will give; when thou hast it by thee.

3614.text: Devise not evil against thy neighbour, seeing he dwelleth securely by thee.

3615.text: Strive not with a man without cause, if he have done thee no harm.

3616.text: Envy thou not the oppressor, and choose none of his ways.

3617.text: For the froward is abomination to the Lord: but his secret is with the righteous.

3618.text: The curse of the Lord is in the house of the wicked: but he blesseth the habitation of the just.

3619.text: Surely he scorneth the scorners: but he giveth grace unto the lowly.

3620.text: The wise shall inherit glory: but shame shall be the promotion of fools.

3621.text: Hear, ye children, the instruction of a father, and attend to know understanding.

3622.text: For I give you good doctrine, forsake ye not my law.

3623.text: For I was my father’s son, tender and only beloved in the sight of my mother.

3624.text: He taught me also, and said unto me, Let thine heart retain my words: keep my commandments, and live.

3625.text: Get wisdom, get understanding: forget it not; neither decline from the words of my mouth.

3626.text: Forsake her not, and she shall preserve thee: love her, and she shall keep thee.

3627.text: Wisdom is the principal thing; therefore get wisdom: and with all thy getting get understanding.

3628.text: Exalt her, and she shall promote thee: she shall bring thee to honour, when thou dost embrace her.

3629.text: She shall give to thine head an ornament of grace: a crown of glory shall she deliver to thee.

3630.text: Hear, O my son, and receive my sayings; and the years of thy life shall be many.

3631.text: I have taught thee in the way of wisdom; I have led thee in right paths.

3632.text: When thou goest, thy steps shall not be straitened; and when thou runnest, thou shalt not stumble.

3633.text: Take fast hold of instruction; let her not go: keep her; for she is thy life.

3634.text: Enter not into the path of the wicked, and go not in the way of evil men.

3635.text: Avoid it, pass not by it, turn from it, and pass away.

3636.text: For they sleep not, except they have done mischief; and their sleep is taken away, unless they cause some to fall.

3637.text: For they eat the bread of wickedness, and drink the wine of violence.

3638.text: But the path of the just is as the shining light, that shineth more and more unto the perfect day.

3639.text: The way of the wicked is as darkness: they know not at what they stumble.

3640.text: My son, attend to my words; incline thine ear unto my sayings.

3641.text: Let them not depart from thine eyes; keep them in the midst of thine heart.

3642.text: For they are life unto those that find them, and health to all their flesh.

3643.text: Keep thy heart with all diligence; for out of it are the issues of life.

3644.text: Put away from thee a froward mouth, and perverse lips put far from thee.

3645.text: Let thine eyes look right on, and let thine eyelids look straight before thee.

3646.text: Ponder the path of thy feet, and let all thy ways be established.

3647.text: Turn not to the right hand nor to the left: remove thy foot from evil.

3648.text: My son, attend unto my wisdom, and bow thine ear to my understanding:

3649.text: That thou mayest regard discretion, and that thy lips may keep knowledge.

3650.text: For the lips of a strange woman drop as an honeycomb, and her mouth is smoother than oil:

3651.text: But her end is bitter as wormwood, sharp as a twoedged sword.

3652.text: Her feet go down to death; her steps take hold on hell.

3653.text: Lest thou shouldest ponder the path of life, her ways are moveable, that thou canst not know them.

3654.text: Hear me now therefore, O ye children, and depart not from the words of my mouth.

3655.text: Remove thy way far from her, and come not nigh the door of her house:

3656.text: Lest thou give thine honour unto others, and thy years unto the cruel:

3657.text: Lest strangers be filled with thy wealth; and thy labours be in the house of a stranger;

3658.text: And thou mourn at the last, when thy flesh and thy body are consumed,

3659.text: And say, How have I hated instruction, and my heart despised reproof;

3660.text: And have not obeyed the voice of my teachers, nor inclined mine ear to them that instructed me!

3661.text: I was almost in all evil in the midst of the congregation and assembly.

3662.text: Drink waters out of thine own cistern, and running waters out of thine own well.

3663.text: Let thy fountains be dispersed abroad, and rivers of waters in the streets.

3664.text: Let them be only thine own, and not strangers’ with thee.

3665.text: Let thy fountain be blessed: and rejoice with the wife of thy youth.

3666.text: Let her be as the loving hind and pleasant roe; let her breasts satisfy thee at all times; and be thou ravished always with her love.

3667.text: And why wilt thou, my son, be ravished with a strange woman, and embrace the bosom of a stranger?

3668.text: For the ways of man are before the eyes of the Lord, and he pondereth all his goings.

3669.text: His own iniquities shall take the wicked himself, and he shall be holden with the cords of his sins.

3670.text: He shall die without instruction; and in the greatness of his folly he shall go astray.

3671.text: My son, if thou be surety for thy friend, if thou hast stricken thy hand with a stranger,

3672.text: Thou art snared with the words of thy mouth, thou art taken with the words of thy mouth.

3673.text: Do this now, my son, and deliver thyself, when thou art come into the hand of thy friend; go, humble thyself, and make sure thy friend.

3674.text: Give not sleep to thine eyes, nor slumber to thine eyelids.

3675.text: Deliver thyself as a roe from the hand of the hunter, and as a bird from the hand of the fowler.

3676.text: Go to the ant, thou sluggard; consider her ways, and be wise:

3677.text: Which having no guide, overseer, or ruler,

3678.text: Provideth her meat in the summer, and gathereth her food in the harvest.

3679.text: How long wilt thou sleep, O sluggard? when wilt thou arise out of thy sleep?

3680.text: Yet a little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to sleep:

3681.text: So shall thy poverty come as one that travelleth, and thy want as an armed man.

3682.text: A naughty person, a wicked man, walketh with a froward mouth.

3683.text: He winketh with his eyes, he speaketh with his feet, he teacheth with his fingers;

3684.text: Frowardness is in his heart, he deviseth mischief continually; he soweth discord.

3685.text: Therefore shall his calamity come suddenly; suddenly shall he be broken without remedy.

3686.text: These six things doth the Lord hate: yea, seven are an abomination unto him:

3687.text: A proud look, a lying tongue, and hands that shed innocent blood,

3688.text: An heart that deviseth wicked imaginations, feet that be swift in running to mischief,

3689.text: A false witness that speaketh lies, and he that soweth discord among brethren.

3690.text: My son, keep thy father’s commandment, and forsake not the law of thy mother:

3691.text: Bind them continually upon thine heart, and tie them about thy neck.

3692.text: When thou goest, it shall lead thee; when thou sleepest, it shall keep thee; and when thou awakest, it shall talk with thee.

3693.text: For the commandment is a lamp; and the law is light; and reproofs of instruction are the way of life:

3694.text: To keep thee from the evil woman, from the flattery of the tongue of a strange woman.

3695.text: Lust not after her beauty in thine heart; neither let her take thee with her eyelids.

3696.text: For by means of a whorish woman a man is brought to a piece of bread: and the adulteress will hunt for the precious life.

3697.text: Can a man take fire in his bosom, and his clothes not be burned?

3698.text: Can one go upon hot coals, and his feet not be burned?

3699.text: So he that goeth in to his neighbour’s wife; whosoever toucheth her shall not be innocent.

3700.text: Men do not despise a thief, if he steal to satisfy his soul when he is hungry;

3701.text: But if he be found, he shall restore sevenfold; he shall give all the substance of his house.

3702.text: But whoso committeth adultery with a woman lacketh understanding: he that doeth it destroyeth his own soul.

3703.text: A wound and dishonour shall he get; and his reproach shall not be wiped away.

3704.text: For jealousy is the rage of a man: therefore he will not spare in the day of vengeance.

3705.text: He will not regard any ransom; neither will he rest content, though thou givest many gifts.

3706.text: My son, keep my words, and lay up my commandments with thee.

3707.text: Keep my commandments, and live; and my law as the apple of thine eye.

3708.text: Bind them upon thy fingers, write them upon the table of thine heart.

3709.text: Say unto wisdom, Thou art my sister; and call understanding thy kinswoman:

3710.text: That they may keep thee from the strange woman, from the stranger which flattereth with her words.

3711.text: For at the window of my house I looked through my casement,

3712.text: And beheld among the simple ones, I discerned among the youths, a young man void of understanding,

3713.text: Passing through the street near her corner; and he went the way to her house,

3714.text: In the twilight, in the evening, in the black and dark night:

3715.text: And, behold, there met him a woman with the attire of an harlot, and subtil of heart.

3716.text: (She is loud and stubborn; her feet abide not in her house:

3717.text: Now is she without, now in the streets, and lieth in wait at every corner.)

3718.text: So she caught him, and kissed him, and with an impudent face said unto him,

3719.text: I have peace offerings with me; this day have I payed my vows.

3720.text: Therefore came I forth to meet thee, diligently to seek thy face, and I have found thee.

3721.text: I have decked my bed with coverings of tapestry, with carved works, with fine linen of Egypt.

3722.text: I have perfumed my bed with myrrh, aloes, and cinnamon.

3723.text: Come, let us take our fill of love until the morning: let us solace ourselves with loves.

3724.text: For the goodman is not at home, he is gone a long journey:

3725.text: He hath taken a bag of money with him, and will come home at the day appointed.

3726.text: With her much fair speech she caused him to yield, with the flattering of her lips she forced him.

3727.text: He goeth after her straightway, as an ox goeth to the slaughter, or as a fool to the correction of the stocks;

3728.text: Till a dart strike through his liver; as a bird hasteth to the snare, and knoweth not that it is for his life.

3729.text: Hearken unto me now therefore, O ye children, and attend to the words of my mouth.

3730.text: Let not thine heart decline to her ways, go not astray in her paths.

3731.text: For she hath cast down many wounded: yea, many strong men have been slain by her.

3732.text: Her house is the way to hell, going down to the chambers of death.

3733.text: Doth not wisdom cry? and understanding put forth her voice?

3734.text: She standeth in the top of high places, by the way in the places of the paths.

3735.text: She crieth at the gates, at the entry of the city, at the coming in at the doors.

3736.text: Unto you, O men, I call; and my voice is to the sons of man.

3737.text: O ye simple, understand wisdom: and, ye fools, be ye of an understanding heart.

3738.text: Hear; for I will speak of excellent things; and the opening of my lips shall be right things.

3739.text: For my mouth shall speak truth; and wickedness is an abomination to my lips.

3740.text: All the words of my mouth are in righteousness; there is nothing froward or perverse in them.

3741.text: They are all plain to him that understandeth, and right to them that find knowledge.

3742.text: Receive my instruction, and not silver; and knowledge rather than choice gold.

3743.text: For wisdom is better than rubies; and all the things that may be desired are not to be compared to it.

3744.text: I wisdom dwell with prudence, and find out knowledge of witty inventions.

3745.text: The fear of the Lord is to hate evil: pride, and arrogancy, and the evil way, and the froward mouth, do I hate.

3746.text: Counsel is mine, and sound wisdom: I am understanding; I have strength.

3747.text: By me kings reign, and princes decree justice.

3748.text: By me princes rule, and nobles, even all the judges of the earth.

3749.text: I love them that love me; and those that seek me early shall find me.

3750.text: Riches and honour are with me; yea, durable riches and righteousness.

3751.text: My fruit is better than gold, yea, than fine gold; and my revenue than choice silver.

3752.text: I lead in the way of righteousness, in the midst of the paths of judgment:

3753.text: That I may cause those that love me to inherit substance; and I will fill their treasures.

3754.text: The Lord possessed me in the beginning of his way, before his works of old.

3755.text: I was set up from everlasting, from the beginning, or ever the earth was.

3756.text: When there were no depths, I was brought forth; when there were no fountains abounding with water.

3757.text: Before the mountains were settled, before the hills was I brought forth:

3758.text: While as yet he had not made the earth, nor the fields, nor the highest part of the dust of the world.

3759.text: When he prepared the heavens, I was there: when he set a compass upon the face of the depth:

3760.text: When he established the clouds above: when he strengthened the fountains of the deep:

3761.text: When he gave to the sea his decree, that the waters should not pass his commandment: when he appointed the foundations of the earth:

3762.text: Then I was by him, as one brought up with him: and I was daily his delight, rejoicing always before him;

3763.text: Rejoicing in the habitable part of his earth; and my delights were with the sons of men.

3764.text: Now therefore hearken unto me, O ye children: for blessed are they that keep my ways.

3765.text: Hear instruction, and be wise, and refuse it not.

3766.text: Blessed is the man that heareth me, watching daily at my gates, waiting at the posts of my doors.

3767.text: For whoso findeth me findeth life, and shall obtain favour of the Lord.

3768.text: But he that sinneth against me wrongeth his own soul: all they that hate me love death.

3769.text: Wisdom hath builded her house, she hath hewn out her seven pillars:

3770.text: She hath killed her beasts; she hath mingled her wine; she hath also furnished her table.

3771.text: She hath sent forth her maidens: she crieth upon the highest places of the city,

3772.text: Whoso is simple, let him turn in hither: as for him that wanteth understanding, she saith to him,

3773.text: Come, eat of my bread, and drink of the wine which I have mingled.

3774.text: Forsake the foolish, and live; and go in the way of understanding.

3775.text: He that reproveth a scorner getteth to himself shame: and he that rebuketh a wicked man getteth himself a blot.

3776.text: Reprove not a scorner, lest he hate thee: rebuke a wise man, and he will love thee.

3777.text: Give instruction to a wise man, and he will be yet wiser: teach a just man, and he will increase in learning.

3778.text: The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom: and the knowledge of the holy is understanding.

3779.text: For by me thy days shall be multiplied, and the years of thy life shall be increased.

3780.text: If thou be wise, thou shalt be wise for thyself: but if thou scornest, thou alone shalt bear it.

3781.text: A foolish woman is clamorous: she is simple, and knoweth nothing.

3782.text: For she sitteth at the door of her house, on a seat in the high places of the city,

3783.text: To call passengers who go right on their ways:

3784.text: Whoso is simple, let him turn in hither: and as for him that wanteth understanding, she saith to him,

3785.text: Stolen waters are sweet, and bread eaten in secret is pleasant.

3786.text: But he knoweth not that the dead are there; and that her guests are in the depths of hell.

3787.text: The proverbs of Solomon. A wise son maketh a glad father: but a foolish son is the heaviness of his mother.

3788.text: Treasures of wickedness profit nothing: but righteousness delivereth from death.

3789.text: The Lord will not suffer the soul of the righteous to famish: but he casteth away the substance of the wicked.

3790.text: He becometh poor that dealeth with a slack hand: but the hand of the diligent maketh rich.

3791.text: He that gathereth in summer is a wise son: but he that sleepeth in harvest is a son that causeth shame.

3792.text: Blessings are upon the head of the just: but violence covereth the mouth of the wicked.

3793.text: The memory of the just is blessed: but the name of the wicked shall rot.

3794.text: The wise in heart will receive commandments: but a prating fool shall fall.

3795.text: He that walketh uprightly walketh surely: but he that perverteth his ways shall be known.

3796.text: He that winketh with the eye causeth sorrow: but a prating fool shall fall.

3797.text: The mouth of a righteous man is a well of life: but violence covereth the mouth of the wicked.

3798.text: Hatred stirreth up strifes: but love covereth all sins.

3799.text: In the lips of him that hath understanding wisdom is found: but a rod is for the back of him that is void of understanding.

3800.text: Wise men lay up knowledge: but the mouth of the foolish is near destruction.

3801.text: The rich man’s wealth is his strong city: the destruction of the poor is their poverty.

3802.text: The labour of the righteous tendeth to life: the fruit of the wicked to sin.

3803.text: He is in the way of life that keepeth instruction: but he that refuseth reproof erreth.

3804.text: He that hideth hatred with lying lips, and he that uttereth a slander, is a fool.

3805.text: In the multitude of words there wanteth not sin: but he that refraineth his lips is wise.

3806.text: The tongue of the just is as choice silver: the heart of the wicked is little worth.

3807.text: The lips of the righteous feed many: but fools die for want of wisdom.

3808.text: The blessing of the Lord, it maketh rich, and he addeth no sorrow with it.

3809.text: It is as sport to a fool to do mischief: but a man of understanding hath wisdom.

3810.text: The fear of the wicked, it shall come upon him: but the desire of the righteous shall be granted.

3811.text: As the whirlwind passeth, so is the wicked no more: but the righteous is an everlasting foundation.

3812.text: As vinegar to the teeth, and as smoke to the eyes, so is the sluggard to them that send him.

3813.text: The fear of the Lord prolongeth days: but the years of the wicked shall be shortened.

3814.text: The hope of the righteous shall be gladness: but the expectation of the wicked shall perish.

3815.text: The way of the Lord is strength to the upright: but destruction shall be to the workers of iniquity.

3816.text: The righteous shall never be removed: but the wicked shall not inhabit the earth.

3817.text: The mouth of the just bringeth forth wisdom: but the froward tongue shall be cut out.

3818.text: The lips of the righteous know what is acceptable: but the mouth of the wicked speaketh frowardness.

3819.text: A false balance is abomination to the Lord: but a just weight is his delight.

3820.text: When pride cometh, then cometh shame: but with the lowly is wisdom.

3821.text: The integrity of the upright shall guide them: but the perverseness of transgressors shall destroy them.

3822.text: Riches profit not in the day of wrath: but righteousness delivereth from death.

3823.text: The righteousness of the perfect shall direct his way: but the wicked shall fall by his own wickedness.

3824.text: The righteousness of the upright shall deliver them: but transgressors shall be taken in their own naughtiness.

3825.text: When a wicked man dieth, his expectation shall perish: and the hope of unjust men perisheth.

3826.text: The righteous is delivered out of trouble, and the wicked cometh in his stead.

3827.text: An hypocrite with his mouth destroyeth his neighbour: but through knowledge shall the just be delivered.

3828.text: When it goeth well with the righteous, the city rejoiceth: and when the wicked perish, there is shouting.

3829.text: By the blessing of the upright the city is exalted: but it is overthrown by the mouth of the wicked.

3830.text: He that is void of wisdom despiseth his neighbour: but a man of understanding holdeth his peace.

3831.text: A talebearer revealeth secrets: but he that is of a faithful spirit concealeth the matter.

3832.text: Where no counsel is, the people fall: but in the multitude of counsellors there is safety.

3833.text: He that is surety for a stranger shall smart for it: and he that hateth suretiship is sure.

3834.text: A gracious woman retaineth honour: and strong men retain riches.

3835.text: The merciful man doeth good to his own soul: but he that is cruel troubleth his own flesh.

3836.text: The wicked worketh a deceitful work: but to him that soweth righteousness shall be a sure reward.

3837.text: As righteousness tendeth to life: so he that pursueth evil pursueth it to his own death.

3838.text: They that are of a froward heart are abomination to the Lord: but such as are upright in their way are his delight.

3839.text: Though hand join in hand, the wicked shall not be unpunished: but the seed of the righteous shall be delivered.

3840.text: As a jewel of gold in a swine’s snout, so is a fair woman which is without discretion.

3841.text: The desire of the righteous is only good: but the expectation of the wicked is wrath.

3842.text: There is that scattereth, and yet increaseth; and there is that withholdeth more than is meet, but it tendeth to poverty.

3843.text: The liberal soul shall be made fat: and he that watereth shall be watered also himself.

3844.text: He that withholdeth corn, the people shall curse him: but blessing shall be upon the head of him that selleth it.

3845.text: He that diligently seeketh good procureth favour: but he that seeketh mischief, it shall come unto him.

3846.text: He that trusteth in his riches shall fall: but the righteous shall flourish as a branch.

3847.text: He that troubleth his own house shall inherit the wind: and the fool shall be servant to the wise of heart.

3848.text: The fruit of the righteous is a tree of life; and he that winneth souls is wise.

3849.text: Behold, the righteous shall be recompensed in the earth: much more the wicked and the sinner.

3850.text: Whoso loveth instruction loveth knowledge: but he that hateth reproof is brutish.

3851.text: A good man obtaineth favour of the Lord: but a man of wicked devices will he condemn.

3852.text: A man shall not be established by wickedness: but the root of the righteous shall not be moved.

3853.text: A virtuous woman is a crown to her husband: but she that maketh ashamed is as rottenness in his bones.

3854.text: The thoughts of the righteous are right: but the counsels of the wicked are deceit.

3855.text: The words of the wicked are to lie in wait for blood: but the mouth of the upright shall deliver them.

3856.text: The wicked are overthrown, and are not: but the house of the righteous shall stand.

3857.text: A man shall be commended according to his wisdom: but he that is of a perverse heart shall be despised.

3858.text: He that is despised, and hath a servant, is better than he that honoureth himself, and lacketh bread.

3859.text: A righteous man regardeth the life of his beast: but the tender mercies of the wicked are cruel.

3860.text: He that tilleth his land shall be satisfied with bread: but he that followeth vain persons is void of understanding.

3861.text: The wicked desireth the net of evil men: but the root of the righteous yieldeth fruit.

3862.text: The wicked is snared by the transgression of his lips: but the just shall come out of trouble.

3863.text: A man shall be satisfied with good by the fruit of his mouth: and the recompence of a man’s hands shall be rendered unto him.

3864.text: The way of a fool is right in his own eyes: but he that hearkeneth unto counsel is wise.

3865.text: A fool’s wrath is presently known: but a prudent man covereth shame.

3866.text: He that speaketh truth sheweth forth righteousness: but a false witness deceit.

3867.text: There is that speaketh like the piercings of a sword: but the tongue of the wise is health.

3868.text: The lip of truth shall be established for ever: but a lying tongue is but for a moment.

3869.text: Deceit is in the heart of them that imagine evil: but to the counsellors of peace is joy.

3870.text: There shall no evil happen to the just: but the wicked shall be filled with mischief.

3871.text: Lying lips are abomination to the Lord: but they that deal truly are his delight.

3872.text: A prudent man concealeth knowledge: but the heart of fools proclaimeth foolishness.

3873.text: The hand of the diligent shall bear rule: but the slothful shall be under tribute.

3874.text: Heaviness in the heart of man maketh it stoop: but a good word maketh it glad.

3875.text: The righteous is more excellent than his neighbour: but the way of the wicked seduceth them.

3876.text: The slothful man roasteth not that which he took in hunting: but the substance of a diligent man is precious.

3877.text: In the way of righteousness is life; and in the pathway thereof there is no death.

3878.text: A wise son heareth his father’s instruction: but a scorner heareth not rebuke.

3879.text: A man shall eat good by the fruit of his mouth: but the soul of the transgressors shall eat violence.

3880.text: He that keepeth his mouth keepeth his life: but he that openeth wide his lips shall have destruction.

3881.text: The soul of the sluggard desireth, and hath nothing: but the soul of the diligent shall be made fat.

3882.text: A righteous man hateth lying: but a wicked man is loathsome, and cometh to shame.

3883.text: Righteousness keepeth him that is upright in the way: but wickedness overthroweth the sinner.

3884.text: There is that maketh himself rich, yet hath nothing: there is that maketh himself poor, yet hath great riches.

3885.text: The ransom of a man’s life are his riches: but the poor heareth not rebuke.

3886.text: The light of the righteous rejoiceth: but the lamp of the wicked shall be put out.

3887.text: Only by pride cometh contention: but with the well advised is wisdom.

3888.text: Wealth gotten by vanity shall be diminished: but he that gathereth by labour shall increase.

3889.text: Hope deferred maketh the heart sick: but when the desire cometh, it is a tree of life.

3890.text: Whoso despiseth the word shall be destroyed: but he that feareth the commandment shall be rewarded.

3891.text: The law of the wise is a fountain of life, to depart from the snares of death.

3892.text: Good understanding giveth favour: but the way of transgressors is hard.

3893.text: Every prudent man dealeth with knowledge: but a fool layeth open his folly.

3894.text: A wicked messenger falleth into mischief: but a faithful ambassador is health.

3895.text: Poverty and shame shall be to him that refuseth instruction: but he that regardeth reproof shall be honoured.

3896.text: The desire accomplished is sweet to the soul: but it is abomination to fools to depart from evil.

3897.text: He that walketh with wise men shall be wise: but a companion of fools shall be destroyed.

3898.text: Evil pursueth sinners: but to the righteous good shall be repayed.

3899.text: A good man leaveth an inheritance to his children’s children: and the wealth of the sinner is laid up for the just.

3900.text: Much food is in the tillage of the poor: but there is that is destroyed for want of judgment.

3901.text: He that spareth his rod hateth his son: but he that loveth him chasteneth him betimes.

3902.text: The righteous eateth to the satisfying of his soul: but the belly of the wicked shall want.

3903.text: Every wise woman buildeth her house: but the foolish plucketh it down with her hands.

3904.text: He that walketh in his uprightness feareth the Lord: but he that is perverse in his ways despiseth him.

3905.text: In the mouth of the foolish is a rod of pride: but the lips of the wise shall preserve them.

3906.text: Where no oxen are, the crib is clean: but much increase is by the strength of the ox.

3907.text: A faithful witness will not lie: but a false witness will utter lies.

3908.text: A scorner seeketh wisdom, and findeth it not: but knowledge is easy unto him that understandeth.

3909.text: Go from the presence of a foolish man, when thou perceivest not in him the lips of knowledge.

3910.text: The wisdom of the prudent is to understand his way: but the folly of fools is deceit.

3911.text: Fools make a mock at sin: but among the righteous there is favour.

3912.text: The heart knoweth his own bitterness; and a stranger doth not intermeddle with his joy.

3913.text: The house of the wicked shall be overthrown: but the tabernacle of the upright shall flourish.

3914.text: There is a way which seemeth right unto a man, but the end thereof are the ways of death.

3915.text: Even in laughter the heart is sorrowful; and the end of that mirth is heaviness.

3916.text: The backslider in heart shall be filled with his own ways: and a good man shall be satisfied from himself.

3917.text: The simple believeth every word: but the prudent man looketh well to his going.

3918.text: A wise man feareth, and departeth from evil: but the fool rageth, and is confident.

3919.text: He that is soon angry dealeth foolishly: and a man of wicked devices is hated.

3920.text: The simple inherit folly: but the prudent are crowned with knowledge.

3921.text: The evil bow before the good; and the wicked at the gates of the righteous.

3922.text: The poor is hated even of his own neighbour: but the rich hath many friends.

3923.text: He that despiseth his neighbour sinneth: but he that hath mercy on the poor, happy is he.

3924.text: Do they not err that devise evil? but mercy and truth shall be to them that devise good.

3925.text: In all labour there is profit: but the talk of the lips tendeth only to penury.

3926.text: The crown of the wise is their riches: but the foolishness of fools is folly.

3927.text: A true witness delivereth souls: but a deceitful witness speaketh lies.

3928.text: In the fear of the Lord is strong confidence: and his children shall have a place of refuge.

3929.text: The fear of the Lord is a fountain of life, to depart from the snares of death.

3930.text: In the multitude of people is the king’s honour: but in the want of people is the destruction of the prince.

3931.text: He that is slow to wrath is of great understanding: but he that is hasty of spirit exalteth folly.

3932.text: A sound heart is the life of the flesh: but envy the rottenness of the bones.

3933.text: He that oppresseth the poor reproacheth his Maker: but he that honoureth him hath mercy on the poor.

3934.text: The wicked is driven away in his wickedness: but the righteous hath hope in his death.

3935.text: Wisdom resteth in the heart of him that hath understanding: but that which is in the midst of fools is made known.

3936.text: Righteousness exalteth a nation: but sin is a reproach to any people.

3937.text: The king’s favour is toward a wise servant: but his wrath is against him that causeth shame.

3938.text: A soft answer turneth away wrath: but grievous words stir up anger.

3939.text: The tongue of the wise useth knowledge aright: but the mouth of fools poureth out foolishness.

3940.text: The eyes of the Lord are in every place, beholding the evil and the good.

3941.text: A wholesome tongue is a tree of life: but perverseness therein is a breach in the spirit.

3942.text: A fool despiseth his father’s instruction: but he that regardeth reproof is prudent.

3943.text: In the house of the righteous is much treasure: but in the revenues of the wicked is trouble.

3944.text: The lips of the wise disperse knowledge: but the heart of the foolish doeth not so.

3945.text: The sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination to the Lord: but the prayer of the upright is his delight.

3946.text: The way of the wicked is an abomination unto the Lord: but he loveth him that followeth after righteousness.

3947.text: Correction is grievous unto him that forsaketh the way: and he that hateth reproof shall die.

3948.text: Hell and destruction are before the Lord: how much more then the hearts of the children of men?

3949.text: A scorner loveth not one that reproveth him: neither will he go unto the wise.

3950.text: A merry heart maketh a cheerful countenance: but by sorrow of the heart the spirit is broken.

3951.text: The heart of him that hath understanding seeketh knowledge: but the mouth of fools feedeth on foolishness.

3952.text: All the days of the afflicted are evil: but he that is of a merry heart hath a continual feast.
