4660.text: Then shall the dust return to the earth as it was: and the spirit shall return unto God who gave it.

4661.text: Vanity of vanities, saith the preacher; all is vanity.

4662.text: And moreover, because the preacher was wise, he still taught the people knowledge; yea, he gave good heed, and sought out, and set in order many proverbs.

4663.text: The preacher sought to find out acceptable words: and that which was written was upright, even words of truth.

4664.text: The words of the wise are as goads, and as nails fastened by the masters of assemblies, which are given from one shepherd.

4665.text: And further, by these, my son, be admonished: of making many books there is no end; and much study is a weariness of the flesh.

4666.text: Let us hear the conclusion of the whole matter: Fear God, and keep his commandments: for this is the whole duty of man.

4667.text: For God shall bring every work into judgment, with every secret thing, whether it be good, or whether it be evil.

4668.text: The song of songs, which is Solomon’s.

4669.text: Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth: for thy love is better than wine.

4670.text: Because of the savour of thy good ointments thy name is as ointment poured forth, therefore do the virgins love thee.

4671.text: Draw me, we will run after thee: the king hath brought me into his chambers: we will be glad and rejoice in thee, we will remember thy love more than wine: the upright love thee.

4672.text: I am black, but comely, O ye daughters of Jerusalem, as the tents of Kedar, as the curtains of Solomon.

4673.text: Look not upon me, because I am black, because the sun hath looked upon me: my mother’s children were angry with me; they made me the keeper of the vineyards; but mine own vineyard have I not kept.

4674.text: Tell me, O thou whom my soul loveth, where thou feedest, where thou makest thy flock to rest at noon: for why should I be as one that turneth aside by the flocks of thy companions?

4675.text: If thou know not, O thou fairest among women, go thy way forth by the footsteps of the flock, and feed thy kids beside the shepherds’ tents.

4676.text: I have compared thee, O my love, to a company of horses in Pharaoh’s chariots.

4677.text: Thy cheeks are comely with rows of jewels, thy neck with chains of gold.

4678.text: We will make thee borders of gold with studs of silver.

4679.text: While the king sitteth at his table, my spikenard sendeth forth the smell thereof.

4680.text: A bundle of myrrh is my wellbeloved unto me; he shall lie all night betwixt my breasts.

4681.text: My beloved is unto me as a cluster of camphire in the vineyards of En–gedi.

4682.text: Behold, thou art fair, my love; behold, thou art fair; thou hast doves’ eyes.

4683.text: Behold, thou art fair, my beloved, yea, pleasant: also our bed is green.

4684.text: The beams of our house are cedar, and our rafters of fir.

4685.text: I am the rose of Sharon, and the lily of the valleys.

4686.text: As the lily among thorns, so is my love among the daughters.

4687.text: As the apple tree among the trees of the wood, so is my beloved among the sons. I sat down under his shadow with great delight, and his fruit was sweet to my taste.

4688.text: He brought me to the banqueting house, and his banner over me was love.

4689.text: Stay me with flagons, comfort me with apples: for I am sick of love.

4690.text: His left hand is under my head, and his right hand doth embrace me.

4691.text: I charge you, O ye daughters of Jerusalem, by the roes, and by the hinds of the field, that ye stir not up, nor awake my love, till he please.

4692.text: The voice of my beloved! behold, he cometh leaping upon the mountains, skipping upon the hills.

4693.text: My beloved is like a roe or a young hart: behold, he standeth behind our wall, he looketh forth at the windows, shewing himself through the lattice.

4694.text: My beloved spake, and said unto me, Rise up, my love, my fair one, and come away.

4695.text: For, lo, the winter is past, the rain is over and gone;

4696.text: The flowers appear on the earth; the time of the singing of birds is come, and the voice of the turtle is heard in our land;

4697.text: The fig tree putteth forth her green figs, and the vines with the tender grape give a good smell. Arise, my love, my fair one, and come away.

4698.text: O my dove, that art in the clefts of the rock, in the secret places of the stairs, let me see thy countenance, let me hear thy voice; for sweet is thy voice, and thy countenance is comely.

4699.text: Take us the foxes, the little foxes, that spoil the vines: for our vines have tender grapes.

4700.text: My beloved is mine, and I am his: he feedeth among the lilies.

4701.text: Until the day break, and the shadows flee away, turn, my beloved, and be thou like a roe or a young hart upon the mountains of Bether.

4702.text: By night on my bed I sought him whom my soul loveth: I sought him, but I found him not.

4703.text: I will rise now, and go about the city in the streets, and in the broad ways I will seek him whom my soul loveth: I sought him, but I found him not.

4704.text: The watchmen that go about the city found me: to whom I said, Saw ye him whom my soul loveth?

4705.text: It was but a little that I passed from them, but I found him whom my soul loveth: I held him, and would not let him go, until I had brought him into my mother’s house, and into the chamber of her that conceived me.

4706.text: I charge you, O ye daughters of Jerusalem, by the roes, and by the hinds of the field, that ye stir not up, nor awake my love, till he please.

4707.text: Who is this that cometh out of the wilderness like pillars of smoke, perfumed with myrrh and frankincense, with all powders of the merchant?

4708.text: Behold his bed, which is Solomon’s; threescore valiant men are about it, of the valiant of Israel.

4709.text: They all hold swords, being expert in war: every man hath his sword upon his thigh because of fear in the night.

4710.text: King Solomon made himself a chariot of the wood of Lebanon.

4711.text: He made the pillars thereof of silver, the bottom thereof of gold, the covering of it of purple, the midst thereof being paved with love, for the daughters of Jerusalem.

4712.text: Go forth, O ye daughters of Zion, and behold king Solomon with the crown wherewith his mother crowned him in the day of his espousals, and in the day of the gladness of his heart.

4713.text: Behold, thou art fair, my love; behold, thou art fair; thou hast doves’ eyes within thy locks: thy hair is as a flock of goats, that appear from mount Gilead.

4714.text: Thy teeth are like a flock of sheep that are even shorn, which came up from the washing; whereof every one bear twins, and none is barren among them.

4715.text: Thy lips are like a thread of scarlet, and thy speech is comely: thy temples are like a piece of a pomegranate within thy locks.

4716.text: Thy neck is like the tower of David builded for an armoury, whereon there hang a thousand bucklers, all shields of mighty men.

4717.text: Thy two breasts are like two young roes that are twins, which feed among the lilies.

4718.text: Until the day break, and the shadows flee away, I will get me to the mountain of myrrh, and to the hill of frankincense.

4719.text: Thou art all fair, my love; there is no spot in thee.

4720.text: Come with me from Lebanon, my spouse, with me from Lebanon: look from the top of Amana, from the top of Shenir and Hermon, from the lions’ dens, from the mountains of the leopards.

4721.text: Thou hast ravished my heart, my sister, my spouse; thou hast ravished my heart with one of thine eyes, with one chain of thy neck.

4722.text: How fair is thy love, my sister, my spouse! how much better is thy love than wine! and the smell of thine ointments than all spices!

4723.text: Thy lips, O my spouse, drop as the honeycomb: honey and milk are under thy tongue; and the smell of thy garments is like the smell of Lebanon.

4724.text: A garden inclosed is my sister, my spouse; a spring shut up, a fountain sealed.

4725.text: Thy plants are an orchard of pomegranates, with pleasant fruits; camphire, with spikenard,

4726.text: Spikenard and saffron; calamus and cinnamon, with all trees of frankincense; myrrh and aloes, with all the chief spices:

4727.text: A fountain of gardens, a well of living waters, and streams from Lebanon.

4728.text: Awake, O north wind; and come, thou south; blow upon my garden, that the spices thereof may flow out. Let my beloved come into his garden, and eat his pleasant fruits.

4729.text: I am come into my garden, my sister, my spouse: I have gathered my myrrh with my spice; I have eaten my honeycomb with my honey; I have drunk my wine with my milk: eat, O friends; drink, yea, drink abundantly, O beloved.

4730.text: I sleep, but my heart waketh: it is the voice of my beloved that knocketh, saying, Open to me, my sister, my love, my dove, my undefiled: for my head is filled with dew, and my locks with the drops of the night.

4731.text: I have put off my coat; how shall I put it on? I have washed my feet; how shall I defile them?

4732.text: My beloved put in his hand by the hole of the door, and my bowels were moved for him.

4733.text: I rose up to open to my beloved; and my hands dropped with myrrh, and my fingers with sweet smelling myrrh, upon the handles of the lock.

4734.text: I opened to my beloved; but my beloved had withdrawn himself, and was gone: my soul failed when he spake: I sought him, but I could not find him; I called him, but he gave me no answer.

4735.text: The watchmen that went about the city found me, they smote me, they wounded me; the keepers of the walls took away my veil from me.

4736.text: I charge you, O daughters of Jerusalem, if ye find my beloved, that ye tell him, that I am sick of love.

4737.text: What is thy beloved more than another beloved, O thou fairest among women? what is thy beloved more than another beloved, that thou dost so charge us?

4738.text: My beloved is white and ruddy, the chiefest among ten thousand.

4739.text: His head is as the most fine gold, his locks are bushy, and black as a raven.

4740.text: His eyes are as the eyes of doves by the rivers of waters, washed with milk, and fitly set.

4741.text: His cheeks are as a bed of spices, as sweet flowers: his lips like lilies, dropping sweet smelling myrrh.

4742.text: His hands are as gold rings set with the beryl: his belly is as bright ivory overlaid with sapphires.

4743.text: His legs are as pillars of marble, set upon sockets of fine gold: his countenance is as Lebanon, excellent as the cedars.

4744.text: His mouth is most sweet: yea, he is altogether lovely. This is my beloved, and this is my friend, O daughters of Jerusalem.

4745.text: Whither is thy beloved gone, O thou fairest among women? whither is thy beloved turned aside? that we may seek him with thee.

4746.text: My beloved is gone down into his garden, to the beds of spices, to feed in the gardens, and to gather lilies.

4747.text: I am my beloved’s, and my beloved is mine: he feedeth among the lilies.

4748.text: Thou art beautiful, O my love, as Tirzah, comely as Jerusalem, terrible as an army with banners.

4749.text: Turn away thine eyes from me, for they have overcome me: thy hair is as a flock of goats that appear from Gilead.

4750.text: Thy teeth are as a flock of sheep which go up from the washing, whereof every one beareth twins, and there is not one barren among them.

4751.text: As a piece of a pomegranate are thy temples within thy locks.

4752.text: There are threescore queens, and fourscore concubines, and virgins without number.

4753.text: My dove, my undefiled is but one; she is the only one of her mother, she is the choice one of her that bare her. The daughters saw her, and blessed her; yea, the queens and the concubines, and they praised her.

4754.text: Who is she that looketh forth as the morning, fair as the moon, clear as the sun, and terrible as an army with banners?

4755.text: I went down into the garden of nuts to see the fruits of the valley, and to see whether the vine flourished, and the pomegranates budded.

4756.text: Or ever I was aware, my soul made me like the chariots of Amminadib.

4757.text: Return, return, O Shulamite; return, return, that we may look upon thee. What will ye see in the Shulamite? As it were the company of two armies.

4758.text: How beautiful are thy feet with shoes, O prince’s daughter! the joints of thy thighs are like jewels, the work of the hands of a cunning workman.

4759.text: Thy navel is like a round goblet, which wanteth not liquor: thy belly is like an heap of wheat set about with lilies.

4760.text: Thy two breasts are like two young roes that are twins.

4761.text: Thy neck is as a tower of ivory; thine eyes like the fishpools in Heshbon, by the gate of Bath–rabbim: thy nose is as the tower of Lebanon which looketh toward Damascus.

4762.text: Thine head upon thee is like Carmel, and the hair of thine head like purple; the king is held in the galleries.

4763.text: How fair and how pleasant art thou, O love, for delights!

4764.text: This thy stature is like to a palm tree, and thy breasts to clusters of grapes.

4765.text: I said, I will go up to the palm tree, I will take hold of the boughs thereof: now also thy breasts shall be as clusters of the vine, and the smell of thy nose like apples;

4766.text: And the roof of thy mouth like the best wine for my beloved, that goeth down sweetly, causing the lips of those that are asleep to speak.

4767.text: I am my beloved’s, and his desire is toward me.

4768.text: Come, my beloved, let us go forth into the field; let us lodge in the villages.

4769.text: Let us get up early to the vineyards; let us see if the vine flourish, whether the tender grape appear, and the pomegranates bud forth: there will I give thee my loves.

4770.text: The mandrakes give a smell, and at our gates are all manner of pleasant fruits, new and old, which I have laid up for thee, O my beloved.

4771.text: O that thou wert as my brother, that sucked the breasts of my mother! when I should find thee without, I would kiss thee; yea, I should not be despised.

4772.text: I would lead thee, and bring thee into my mother’s house, who would instruct me: I would cause thee to drink of spiced wine of the juice of my pomegranate.

4773.text: His left hand should be under my head, and his right hand should embrace me.

4774.text: I charge you, O daughters of Jerusalem, that ye stir not up, nor awake my love, until he please.

4775.text: Who is this that cometh up from the wilderness, leaning upon her beloved? I raised thee up under the apple tree: there thy mother brought thee forth: there she brought thee forth that bare thee.

4776.text: Set me as a seal upon thine heart, as a seal upon thine arm: for love is strong as death; jealousy is cruel as the grave: the coals thereof are coals of fire, which hath a most vehement flame.

4777.text: Many waters cannot quench love, neither can the floods drown it: if a man would give all the substance of his house for love, it would utterly be contemned.

4778.text: We have a little sister, and she hath no breasts: what shall we do for our sister in the day when she shall be spoken for?

4779.text: If she be a wall, we will build upon her a palace of silver: and if she be a door, we will inclose her with boards of cedar.

4780.text: I am a wall, and my breasts like towers: then was I in his eyes as one that found favour.

4781.text: Solomon had a vineyard at Baal–hamon; he let out the vineyard unto keepers; every one for the fruit thereof was to bring a thousand pieces of silver.

4782.text: My vineyard, which is mine, is before me: thou, O Solomon, must have a thousand, and those that keep the fruit thereof two hundred.

4783.text: Thou that dwellest in the gardens, the companions hearken to thy voice: cause me to hear it.

4784.text: Make haste, my beloved, and be thou like to a roe or to a young hart upon the mountains of spices.

4785.text: There was a man in the land of Uz, whose name was Job. That man was blameless and upright, and one who feared God, and turned away from evil.

4786.text: There were born to him seven sons and three daughters.

4787.text: His possessions also were seven thousand sheep, three thousand camels, five hundred yoke of oxen, five hundred female donkeys, and a very great household; so that this man was the greatest of all the children of the east.

4788.text: His sons went and held a feast in the house of each one on his birthday; and they sent and called for their three sisters to eat and to drink with them.

4789.text: It was so, when the days of their feasting had run their course, that Job sent and sanctified them, and rose up early in the morning, and offered burnt offerings according to the number of them all. For Job said, "It may be that my sons have sinned, and renounced God in their hearts." Job did so continually.

4790.text: Now it happened on the day when the God's sons came to present themselves before the Lord, that Satan also came among them.

4791.text: The Lord said to Satan, "Where have you come from?" Then Satan answered the Lord, and said, "From going back and forth in the earth, and from walking up and down in it."

4792.text: The Lord said to Satan, "Have you considered my servant, Job? For there is none like him in the earth, a blameless and an upright man, one who fears God, and turns away from evil."

4793.text: Then Satan answered the Lord, and said, "Does Job fear God for nothing?

4794.text: Haven't you made a hedge around him, and around his house, and around all that he has, on every side? You have blessed the work of his hands, and his substance is increased in the land.

4795.text: But put forth your hand now, and touch all that he has, and he will renounce you to your face."

4796.text: The Lord said to Satan, "Behold, all that he has is in your power. Only on himself do not put forth your hand." So Satan went forth from the presence of the Lord.

4797.text: It fell on a day when his sons and his daughters were eating and drinking wine in their eldest brother's house,

4798.text: that there came a messenger to Job, and said, "The oxen were plowing, and the donkeys feeding beside them,

4799.text: and the Sabeans attacked, and took them away. Yes, they have killed the servants with the edge of the sword, and I alone have escaped to tell you."

4800.text: While he was still speaking, there also came another, and said, "The fire of God has fallen from the sky, and has burned up the sheep and the servants, and consumed them, and I alone have escaped to tell you."

4801.text: While he was still speaking, there came also another, and said, "The Chaldeans made three bands, and swept down on the camels, and have taken them away, yes, and killed the servants with the edge of the sword; and I alone have escaped to tell you."

4802.text: While he was still speaking, there came also another, and said, "Your sons and your daughters were eating and drinking wine in their eldest brother's house,

4803.text: and behold, there came a great wind from the wilderness, and struck the four corners of the house, and it fell on the young men, and they are dead. I alone have escaped to tell you."

4804.text: Then Job arose, and tore his robe, and shaved his head, and fell down on the ground, and worshiped.

4805.text: He said, "Naked I came out of my mother's womb, and naked shall I return there. The Lord gave, and the Lord has taken away. Blessed be the name of the Lord."

4806.text: In all this, Job did not sin, nor charge God with wrongdoing.

4807.text: Again it happened on the day when the God's sons came to present themselves before the Lord, that Satan came also among them to present himself before the Lord.

4808.text: The Lord said to Satan, "Where have you come from?" Satan answered the Lord, and said, "From going back and forth in the earth, and from walking up and down in it."

4809.text: The Lord said to Satan, "Have you considered my servant Job? For there is none like him in the earth, a blameless and an upright man, one who fears God, and turns away from evil. He still maintains his integrity, although you incited me against him, to ruin him without cause."

4810.text: Satan answered the Lord, and said, "Skin for skin. Yes, all that a man has he will give for his life.

4811.text: But put forth your hand now, and touch his bone and his flesh, and he will renounce you to your face."

4812.text: The Lord said to Satan, "Behold, he is in your hand. Only spare his life."

4813.text: So Satan went forth from the presence of the Lord, and struck Job with painful sores from the sole of his foot to his head.

4814.text: He took for himself a potsherd to scrape himself with, and he sat among the ashes.

4815.text: Then his wife said to him, "Do you still maintain your integrity? Renounce God, and die."

4816.text: But he said to her, "You speak as one of the foolish women would speak. What? Shall we receive good at the hand of God, and shall we not receive evil?" In all this Job did not sin with his lips.

4817.text: Now when Job's three friends heard of all this evil that had come on him, they each came from his own place: Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite, and they made an appointment together to come to sympathize with him and to comfort him.

4818.text: When they lifted up their eyes from a distance, and did not recognize him, they raised their voices, and wept; and they each tore his robe, and sprinkled dust on their heads toward the sky.

4819.text: So they sat down with him on the ground seven days and seven nights, and none spoke a word to him, for they saw that his grief was very great.

4820.text: After this Job opened his mouth, and cursed the day of his birth.

4822.text: "Let the day perish in which I was born, the night which said, 'There is a boy conceived.'

4823.text: Let that day be darkness. Do not let God from above seek for it, neither let the light shine on it.

4824.text: Let darkness and the shadow of death claim it for their own. Let a cloud dwell on it. Let all that makes black the day terrify it.

4825.text: As for that night, let thick darkness seize on it. Let it not rejoice among the days of the year. Let it not come into the number of the months.

4826.text: Behold, let that night be barren. Let no joyful voice come therein.

4827.text: Let them curse it who curse the day, who are ready to rouse up leviathan.

4828.text: Let the stars of its twilight be dark. Let it look for light, but have none, neither let it see the eyelids of the morning,

4829.text: because it did not shut up the doors of my mother's womb, nor did it hide trouble from my eyes.

4830.text: "Why did I not die from the womb? Why did I not give up the spirit when my mother bore me?

4831.text: Why did the knees receive me? Or why the breast, that I should suck?

4832.text: For now should I have lain down and been quiet. I should have slept, then I would have been at rest,

4833.text: with kings and counselors of the earth, who built up waste places for themselves;

4834.text: or with princes who had gold, who filled their houses with silver:

4835.text: or as a hidden untimely birth I had not been, as infants who never saw light.

4836.text: There the wicked cease from troubling. There the weary are at rest.

4837.text: There the prisoners are at ease together. They do not hear the voice of the taskmaster.

4838.text: The small and the great are there. The servant is free from his master.

4839.text: "Why is light given to him who is in misery, life to the bitter in soul,

4840.text: Who long for death, but it doesn't come; and dig for it more than for hidden treasures,

4841.text: who rejoice exceedingly, and are glad, when they can find the grave?

4842.text: Why is light given to a man whose way is hid, whom God has hedged in?

4843.text: For my sighing comes before I eat. My groanings are poured out like water.

4844.text: For the thing which I fear comes on me, That which I am afraid of comes to me.

4845.text: I am not at ease, neither am I quiet, neither have I rest; but trouble comes."

4847.text: "If someone ventures to talk with you, will you be grieved? But who can withhold himself from speaking?

4848.text: Behold, you have instructed many, you have strengthened the weak hands.

4849.text: Your words have supported him who was falling, You have made firm the feeble knees.

4850.text: But now it is come to you, and you faint. It touches you, and you are troubled.

4851.text: Isn't your piety your confidence? Isn't the integrity of your ways your hope?

4852.text: "Remember, now, whoever perished, being innocent? Or where were the upright cut off?

4853.text: According to what I have seen, those who plow iniquity, and sow trouble, reap the same.

4854.text: By the breath of God they perish. By the blast of his anger are they consumed.

4855.text: The roaring of the lion, and the voice of the fierce lion, the teeth of the young lions, are broken.

4856.text: The old lion perishes for lack of prey. The cubs of the lioness are scattered abroad.

4857.text: "Now a thing was secretly brought to me. My ear received a whisper of it.

4858.text: In thoughts from the visions of the night, when deep sleep falls on men,

4859.text: fear came on me, and trembling, which made all my bones shake.

4860.text: Then a spirit passed before my face. The hair of my flesh stood up.

4861.text: It stood still, but I couldn't discern its appearance. A form was before my eyes. Silence, then I heard a voice, saying,

4862.text: 'Shall mortal man be more just than God? Shall a man be more pure than his Maker?

4863.text: Behold, he puts no trust in his servants. He charges his angels with error.

4864.text: How much more, those who dwell in houses of clay, whose foundation is in the dust, who are crushed before the moth!

4865.text: Between morning and evening they are destroyed. They perish forever without any regarding it.

4866.text: Isn't their tent cord plucked up within them? They die, and that without wisdom.'

4867.text: "Call now; is there any who will answer you? To which of the holy ones will you turn?

4868.text: For resentment kills the foolish man, and jealousy kills the simple.

4869.text: I have seen the foolish taking root, but suddenly I cursed his habitation.

4870.text: His children are far from safety. They are crushed in the gate. Neither is there any to deliver them,

4871.text: whose harvest the hungry eats up, and take it even out of the thorns. The snare gapes for their substance.

4872.text: For affliction doesn't come forth from the dust, neither does trouble spring out of the ground;

4873.text: but man is born to trouble, as the sparks fly upward.

4874.text: "But as for me, I would seek God. I would commit my cause to God,

4875.text: who does great things that can't be fathomed, marvelous things without number;

4876.text: who gives rain on the earth, and sends waters on the fields;

4877.text: so that he sets up on high those who are low, those who mourn are exalted to safety.

4878.text: He frustrates the devices of the crafty, So that their hands can't perform their enterprise.

4879.text: He takes the wise in their own craftiness; the counsel of the cunning is carried headlong.

4880.text: They meet with darkness in the day time, and grope at noonday as in the night.

4881.text: But he saves from the sword of their mouth, even the needy from the hand of the mighty.

4882.text: So the poor has hope, and injustice shuts her mouth.

4883.text: "Behold, happy is the man whom God corrects. Therefore do not despise the chastening of the Almighty.

4884.text: For he wounds, and binds up. He injures, and his hands make whole.

4885.text: He will deliver you in six troubles; yes, in seven there shall no evil touch you.

4886.text: In famine he will redeem you from death; in war, from the power of the sword.

4887.text: You shall be hidden from the scourge of the tongue, neither shall you be afraid of destruction when it comes.

4888.text: At destruction and famine you shall laugh, neither shall you be afraid of the animals of the earth.

4889.text: For you shall be in league with the stones of the field. The animals of the field shall be at peace with you.

4890.text: You shall know that your tent is in peace. You shall visit your fold, and shall miss nothing.

4891.text: You shall know also that your seed shall be great, Your offspring as the grass of the earth.

4892.text: You shall come to your grave in a full age, like a shock of grain comes in its season.

4893.text: Look this, we have searched it, so it is. Hear it, and know it for your good."

4895.text: "Oh that my anguish were weighed, and all my calamity laid in the balances!

4896.text: For now it would be heavier than the sand of the seas, therefore have my words been rash.

4897.text: For the arrows of the Almighty are within me. My spirit drinks up their poison. The terrors of God set themselves in array against me.

4898.text: Does the wild donkey bray when he has grass? Or does the ox low over his fodder?

4899.text: Can that which has no flavor be eaten without salt? Or is there any taste in the white of an egg?

4900.text: My soul refuses to touch them. They are as loathsome food to me.

4901.text: "Oh that I might have my request, that God would grant the thing that I long for,

4902.text: even that it would please God to crush me; that he would let loose his hand, and cut me off!

4903.text: Be it still my consolation, yes, let me exult in pain that doesn't spare, that I have not denied the words of the Holy One.

4904.text: What is my strength, that I should wait? What is my end, that I should be patient?

4905.text: Is my strength the strength of stones? Or is my flesh of brass?

4906.text: Isn't it that I have no help in me, That wisdom is driven quite from me?

4907.text: "To him who is ready to faint, kindness should be shown from his friend; even to him who forsakes the fear of the Almighty.

4908.text: My brothers have dealt deceitfully as a brook, as the channel of brooks that pass away;

4909.text: Which are black by reason of the ice, in which the snow hides itself.

4910.text: In the dry season, they vanish. When it is hot, they are consumed out of their place.

4911.text: The caravans that travel beside them turn aside. They go up into the waste, and perish.

4912.text: The caravans of Tema looked. The companies of Sheba waited for them.

4913.text: They were distressed because they were confident. They came there, and were confounded.

4914.text: For now you are nothing. You see a terror, and are afraid.

4915.text: Did I say, 'Give to me?' or, 'Offer a present for me from your substance?'

4916.text: or, 'Deliver me from the adversary's hand?' or, 'Redeem me from the hand of the oppressors?'

4917.text: "Teach me, and I will hold my peace. Cause me to understand wherein I have erred.

4918.text: How forcible are words of uprightness! But your reproof, what does it reprove?

4919.text: Do you intend to reprove words, seeing that the speeches of one who is desperate are as wind?

4920.text: Yes, you would even cast lots for the fatherless, and make merchandise of your friend.

4921.text: Now therefore be pleased to look at me, for surely I shall not lie to your face.

4922.text: Please return. Let there be no injustice. Yes, return again. My cause is righteous.

4923.text: Is there injustice on my tongue? Can't my taste discern mischievous things?

4924.text: "Isn't a man forced to labor on earth? Aren't his days like the days of a hired hand?

4925.text: As a servant who earnestly desires the shadow, as a hireling who looks for his wages,

4926.text: so am I made to possess months of misery, wearisome nights are appointed to me.

4927.text: When I lie down, I say, 'When shall I arise, and the night be gone?' I toss and turn until the dawning of the day.

4928.text: My flesh is clothed with worms and clods of dust. My skin closes up, and breaks out afresh.

4929.text: My days are swifter than a weaver's shuttle, and are spent without hope.

4930.text: Oh remember that my life is a breath. My eye shall no more see good.

4931.text: The eye of him who sees me shall see me no more. Your eyes shall be on me, but I shall not be.

4932.text: As the cloud is consumed and vanishes away, so he who goes down to Sheol shall come up no more.

4933.text: He shall return no more to his house, neither shall his place know him any more.

4934.text: "Therefore I will not keep silent. I will speak in the anguish of my spirit. I will complain in the bitterness of my soul.

4935.text: Am I a sea, or a sea monster, that you put a guard over me?

4936.text: When I say, 'My bed shall comfort me. My couch shall ease my complaint;'

4937.text: then you scare me with dreams, and terrify me through visions:

4938.text: so that my soul chooses strangling, death rather than my bones.

4939.text: I loathe my life. I do not want to live forever. Leave me alone, for my days are but a breath.

4940.text: What is man, that you should magnify him, that you should set your mind on him,

4941.text: that you should visit him every morning, and test him every moment?

4942.text: How long will you not look away from me, nor leave me alone until I swallow down my spittle?

4943.text: If I have sinned, what do I do to you, you watcher of men? Why have you set me as a mark for you, so that I am a burden to myself?

4944.text: Why do you not pardon my disobedience, and take away my iniquity? For now shall I lie down in the dust. You will seek me diligently, but I shall not be."

4946.text: "How long will you speak these things? Shall the words of your mouth be a mighty wind?

4947.text: Does God pervert justice? Or does the Almighty pervert righteousness?

4948.text: If your children have sinned against him, He has delivered them into the hand of their disobedience.

4949.text: If you want to seek God diligently, make your supplication to the Almighty.

4950.text: If you were pure and upright, surely now he would awaken for you, and make the habitation of your righteousness prosperous.

4951.text: Though your beginning was small, yet your latter end would greatly increase.

4952.text: "Please inquire of past generations. Find out about the learning of their fathers.

4953.text: (For we are but of yesterday, and know nothing, because our days on earth are a shadow.)

4954.text: Shall they not teach you, tell you, and utter words out of their heart?

4955.text: "Can the papyrus grow up without mire? Can the rushes grow without water?

4956.text: While it is yet in its greenness, not cut down, it withers before any other reed.

4957.text: So are the paths of all who forget God. The hope of the godless man shall perish,

4958.text: Whose confidence shall break apart, Whose trust is a spider's web.

4959.text: He shall lean on his house, but it shall not stand. He shall cling to it, but it shall not endure.

4960.text: He is green before the sun. His shoots go forth over his garden.

4961.text: His roots are wrapped around the rock pile. He sees the place of stones.

4962.text: If he is destroyed from his place, then it shall deny him, saying, 'I have not seen you.'

4963.text: Behold, this is the joy of his way: out of the earth, others shall spring.

4964.text: "Behold, God will not cast away a blameless man, neither will he uphold the evildoers.

4965.text: He will still fill your mouth with laughter, your lips with shouting.

4966.text: Those who hate you shall be clothed with shame. The tent of the wicked shall be no more."

4968.text: "Truly I know that it is so, but how can man be just with God?

4969.text: If he is pleased to contend with him, he can't answer him one time in a thousand.

4970.text: God who is wise in heart, and mighty in strength: who has hardened himself against him, and prospered?

4971.text: He removes the mountains, and they do not know it, when he overturns them in his anger.

4972.text: He shakes the earth out of its place. Its pillars tremble.

4973.text: He commands the sun, and it doesn't rise, and seals up the stars.

4974.text: He alone stretches out the heavens, and treads on the waves of the sea.

4975.text: He makes the Bear, Orion, and the Pleiades, and the chambers of the south.

4976.text: He does great things past finding out; yes, marvelous things without number.

4977.text: Behold, he goes by me, and I do not see him. He passes on also, but I do not perceive him.

4978.text: Behold, he snatches away. Who can hinder him? Who will ask him, 'What are you doing?'

4979.text: "God will not withdraw his anger. The helpers of Rahab stoop under him.

4980.text: How much less shall I answer him, And choose my words to argue with him?

4981.text: Though I were righteous, yet I wouldn't answer him. I would make supplication to my judge.

4982.text: If I had called, and he had answered me, yet I wouldn't believe that he listened to my voice.

4983.text: For he breaks me with a storm, and multiplies my wounds without cause.

4984.text: He will not allow me to catch my breath, but fills me with bitterness.

4985.text: If it is a matter of strength, behold, he is mighty! If of justice, 'Who,' says he, 'will summon me?'

4986.text: Though I am righteous, my own mouth shall condemn me. Though I am blameless, it shall prove me perverse.

4987.text: I am blameless. I do not regard myself. I despise my life.

4988.text: "It is all the same. Therefore I say he destroys the blameless and the wicked.

4989.text: If the scourge kills suddenly, he will mock at the trial of the innocent.

4990.text: The earth is given into the hand of the wicked. He covers the faces of its judges. If not he, then who is it?

4991.text: "Now my days are swifter than a runner. They flee away, they see no good,

4992.text: They have passed away as the swift ships, as the eagle that swoops on the prey.

4993.text: If I say, 'I will forget my complaint, I will put off my sad face, and cheer up;'

4994.text: I am afraid of all my sorrows, I know that you will not hold me innocent.

4995.text: I shall be condemned. Why then do I labor in vain?

4996.text: If I wash myself with snow, and cleanse my hands with lye,

4997.text: yet you will plunge me in the ditch. My own clothes shall abhor me.

4998.text: For he is not a man, as I am, that I should answer him, that we should come together in judgment.

4999.text: There is no umpire between us, that might lay his hand on us both.

5000.text: Let him take his rod away from me. Let his terror not make me afraid;

5001.text: then I would speak, and not fear him, for I am not so in myself.

5002.text: "My soul is weary of my life. I will give free course to my complaint. I will speak in the bitterness of my soul.

5003.text: I will tell God, 'Do not condemn me. Show me why you contend with me.

5004.text: Is it good to you that you should oppress, that you should despise the work of your hands, and smile on the counsel of the wicked?

5005.text: Do you have eyes of flesh? Or do you see as man sees?

5006.text: Are your days as the days of mortals, or your years as man's years,

5007.text: that you inquire after my iniquity, and search after my sin?

5008.text: Although you know that I am not wicked, there is no one who can deliver out of your hand.

5009.text: "'Your hands have framed me and fashioned me altogether, yet you destroy me.

5010.text: Remember, I beg you, that you have fashioned me as clay. Will you bring me into dust again?

5011.text: Haven't you poured me out like milk, and curdled me like cheese?

5012.text: You have clothed me with skin and flesh, and knit me together with bones and sinews.

5013.text: You have granted me life and loving kindness. Your visitation has preserved my spirit.

5014.text: Yet you hid these things in your heart. I know that this is with you:

5015.text: if I sin, then you mark me. You will not acquit me from my iniquity.

5016.text: If I am wicked, woe to me. If I am righteous, I still shall not lift up my head, being filled with disgrace, and conscious of my affliction.

5017.text: If my head is held high, you hunt me like a lion. Again you show yourself powerful to me.

5018.text: You renew your witnesses against me, and increase your indignation on me. Changes and warfare are with me.

5019.text: "'Why, then, have you brought me forth out of the womb? I wish I had given up the spirit, and no eye had seen me.

5020.text: I should have been as though I had not been. I should have been carried from the womb to the grave.

5021.text: Aren't my days few? Cease then. Leave me alone, that I may find a little comfort,

5022.text: before I go where I shall not return from, to the land of darkness and of the shadow of death;

5023.text: the land dark as midnight, of the shadow of death, without any order, where the light is as midnight.'"

5025.text: "Shouldn't the multitude of words be answered? Should a man full of talk be justified?

5026.text: Should your boastings make men hold their peace? When you mock, shall no man make you ashamed?

5027.text: For you say, 'My doctrine is pure. I am clean in your eyes.'

5028.text: But oh that God would speak, and open his lips against you,

5029.text: that he would show you the secrets of wisdom! For true wisdom has two sides. Know therefore that God exacts of you less than your iniquity deserves.

5030.text: "Can you fathom the mystery of God? Or can you probe the limits of the Almighty?

5031.text: They are high as heaven. What can you do? They are deeper than Sheol. What can you know?

5032.text: Its measure is longer than the earth, and broader than the sea.

5033.text: If he passes by, or confines, or convenes a court, then who can oppose him?

5034.text: For he knows false men. He sees iniquity also, even though he doesn't consider it.

5035.text: An empty-headed man becomes wise when a man is born as a wild donkey's colt.

5036.text: "If you set your heart aright, stretch out your hands toward him.

5037.text: If iniquity is in your hand, put it far away. Do not let unrighteousness dwell in your tents.

5038.text: Surely then you shall lift up your face without spot; Yes, you shall be steadfast, and shall not fear:

5039.text: for you shall forget your misery. You shall remember it as waters that are passed away.

5040.text: Life shall be clearer than the noonday. Though there is darkness, it shall be as the morning.

5041.text: You shall be secure, because there is hope. Yes, you shall search, and shall take your rest in safety.

5042.text: Also you shall lie down, and none shall make you afraid. Yes, many shall court your favor.

5043.text: But the eyes of the wicked shall fail. They shall have no way to flee. Their hope shall be the giving up of the spirit."

5045.text: "No doubt, but you are the people, and wisdom shall die with you.

5046.text: But I have understanding as well as you; I am not inferior to you. Yes, who doesn't know such things as these?

5047.text: I am like one who is a joke to his neighbor, I, who called on God, and he answered. The just, the blameless man is a joke.

5048.text: In the thought of him who is at ease there is contempt for misfortune. It is ready for them whose foot slips.

5049.text: The tents of robbers prosper. Those who provoke God are secure, who carry their God in their hands.

5050.text: "But ask the animals, now, and they shall teach you; the birds of the sky, and they shall tell you.

5051.text: Or speak to the earth, and it shall teach you. The fish of the sea shall declare to you.

5052.text: Who doesn't know that in all these, the hand of the Lord has done this,

5053.text: in whose hand is the life of every living thing, and the breath of all mankind?

5054.text: Doesn't the ear try words, even as the palate tastes its food?

5055.text: With aged men is wisdom, in length of days understanding.

5056.text: "With God is wisdom and might. He has counsel and understanding.

5057.text: Behold, he breaks down, and it can't be built again. He imprisons a man, and there can be no release.

5058.text: Behold, he withholds the waters, and they dry up. Again, he sends them out, and they overturn the earth.

5059.text: With him is strength and wisdom. The deceived and the deceiver are his.

5060.text: He leads counselors away stripped. He makes judges fools.

5061.text: He loosens the bond of kings. He binds their waist with a belt.

5062.text: He leads priests away stripped, and overthrows the mighty.

5063.text: He removes the speech of those who are trusted, and takes away the understanding of the elders.

5064.text: He pours contempt on princes, and loosens the belt of the strong.

5065.text: He uncovers deep things out of darkness, and brings out to light the shadow of death.

5066.text: He increases the nations, and he destroys them. He enlarges the nations, and he leads them captive.

5067.text: He takes away understanding from the chiefs of the people of the earth, and causes them to wander in a wilderness where there is no way.

5068.text: They grope in the dark without light. He makes them stagger like a drunken man.

5069.text: "Behold, my eye has seen all this. My ear has heard and understood it.

5070.text: What you know, I know also. I am not inferior to you.

5071.text: "Surely I would speak to the Almighty. I desire to reason with God.

5072.text: But you are forgers of lies. You are all physicians of no value.

5073.text: Oh that you would be completely silent! Then you would be wise.

5074.text: Hear now my reasoning. Listen to the pleadings of my lips.

5075.text: Will you speak unrighteously for God, and talk deceitfully for him?

5076.text: Will you show partiality to him? Will you contend for God?

5077.text: Is it good that he should search you out? Or as one deceives a man, will you deceive him?

5078.text: He will surely reprove you if you secretly show partiality.

5079.text: Shall not his majesty make you afraid, And his dread fall on you?

5080.text: Your memorable sayings are proverbs of ashes, Your defenses are defenses of clay.

5081.text: "Be silent, leave me alone, that I may speak. Let come on me what will.

5082.text: Why should I take my flesh in my teeth, and put my life in my hand?

5083.text: Behold, he will kill me. I have no hope. Nevertheless, I will maintain my ways before him.

5084.text: This also shall be my salvation, that a godless man shall not come before him.

5085.text: Hear diligently my speech. Let my declaration be in your ears.

5086.text: See now, I have set my cause in order. I know that I am righteous.

5087.text: Who is he who will contend with me? For then would I hold my peace and give up the spirit.

5088.text: "Only do not do two things to me; then I will not hide myself from your face:

5089.text: withdraw your hand far from me; and do not let your terror make me afraid.

5090.text: Then call, and I will answer; or let me speak, and you answer me.

5091.text: How many are my iniquities and sins? Make me know my disobedience and my sin.

5092.text: Why hide you your face, and hold me for your enemy?

5093.text: Will you harass a driven leaf? Will you pursue the dry stubble?

5094.text: For you write bitter things against me, and make me inherit the iniquities of my youth:

5095.text: You also put my feet in the stocks, and mark all my paths. You set a bound to the soles of my feet,

5096.text: though I am decaying like a rotten thing, like a garment that is moth-eaten.

5097.text: "Man, who is born of a woman, is of few days, and full of trouble.

5098.text: He comes forth like a flower, and is cut down. He also flees like a shadow, and doesn't continue.

5099.text: Do you open your eyes on such a one, and bring me into judgment with you?

5100.text: Who can bring a clean thing out of an unclean? Not one.

5101.text: Seeing his days are determined, the number of his months is with you, and you have appointed his bounds that he can't pass;

5102.text: Look away from him, that he may rest, until he shall accomplish, as a hireling, his day.

5103.text: "For there is hope for a tree, If it is cut down, that it will sprout again, that the tender branch of it will not cease.

5104.text: Though its root grows old in the earth, and its stock dies in the ground,

5105.text: yet through the scent of water it will bud, and put forth boughs like a plant.

5106.text: But man dies, and is laid low. Yes, man gives up the spirit, and where is he?

5107.text: As the waters fail from the sea, and the river wastes and dries up,

5108.text: so man lies down and doesn't rise. Until the heavens are no more, they shall not awake, nor be roused out of their sleep.

5109.text: "Oh that you would hide me in Sheol, that you would keep me secret, until your wrath is past, that you would appoint me a set time, and remember me!

5110.text: If a man dies, shall he live again? All the days of my warfare would I wait, until my release should come.

5111.text: You would call, and I would answer you. You would have a desire to the work of your hands.

5112.text: But now you number my steps. Do you not watch over my sin?

5113.text: My disobedience is sealed up in a bag. You fasten up my iniquity.

5114.text: "But the mountain falling comes to nothing. The rock is removed out of its place;

5115.text: The waters wear the stones. The torrents of it wash away the dust of the earth. So you destroy the hope of man.

5116.text: You forever prevail against him, and he departs. You change his face, and send him away.

5117.text: His sons come to honor, and he doesn't know it. They are brought low, but he doesn't perceive it of them.

5118.text: But his flesh on him has pain, and his soul within him mourns."

5120.text: "Should a wise man answer with vain knowledge, and fill himself with the east wind?

5121.text: Should he reason with unprofitable talk, or with speeches with which he can do no good?

5122.text: Yes, you do away with fear, and hinder devotion before God.

5123.text: For your iniquity teaches your mouth, and you choose the language of the crafty.

5124.text: Your own mouth condemns you, and not I. Yes, your own lips testify against you.

5125.text: "Are you the first man who was born? Or were you brought forth before the hills?

5126.text: Have you heard the secret counsel of God? Do you limit wisdom to yourself?

5127.text: What do you know, that we do not know? What do you understand, which is not in us?

5128.text: With us are both the gray-headed and the very aged men, much elder than your father.

5129.text: Are the consolations of God too small for you, even the word that is gentle toward you?

5130.text: Why does your heart carry you away? Why do your eyes flash,

5131.text: That you turn your spirit against God, and let such words go out of your mouth?

5132.text: What is man, that he should be clean? What is he who is born of a woman, that he should be righteous?

5133.text: Behold, he puts no trust in his holy ones. Yes, the heavens are not clean in his sight;

5134.text: how much less one who is abominable and corrupt, a man who drinks iniquity like water!

5135.text: "I will show you, listen to me; that which I have seen I will declare:

5136.text: (Which wise men have told by their fathers, and have not hidden it;

5137.text: to whom alone the land was given, and no stranger passed among them):

5138.text: the wicked man writhes in pain all his days, even the number of years that are laid up for the oppressor.

5139.text: A sound of terrors is in his ears. In prosperity the destroyer shall come on him.

5140.text: He doesn't believe that he shall return out of darkness. He is waited for by the sword.

5141.text: He wanders abroad for bread, saying, 'Where is it?' He knows that the day of darkness is ready at his hand.

5142.text: Distress and anguish make him afraid. They prevail against him, as a king ready to the battle.

5143.text: Because he has stretched out his hand against God, and behaves himself proudly against the Almighty;

5144.text: he runs at him with a stiff neck, with the thick shields of his bucklers;

5145.text: because he has covered his face with his fatness, and gathered fat on his thighs.

5146.text: He has lived in desolate cities, in houses which no one inhabited, which were ready to become heaps.

5147.text: He shall not be rich, neither shall his substance continue, neither shall their possessions be extended on the earth.

5148.text: He shall not depart out of darkness. The flame shall dry up his branches. By the breath of God's mouth shall he go away.

5149.text: Let him not trust in emptiness, deceiving himself; for emptiness shall be his reward.

5150.text: It shall be accomplished before his time. His branch shall not be green.

5151.text: He shall shake off his unripe grape as the vine, and shall cast off his flower as the olive tree.

5152.text: For the company of the godless shall be barren, and fire shall consume the tents of bribery.

5153.text: They conceive mischief, and bring forth iniquity. Their heart prepares deceit."

5155.text: "I have heard many such things. You are all miserable comforters!

5156.text: Shall vain words have an end? Or what provokes you that you answer?

5157.text: I also could speak as you do. If your soul were in my soul's place, I could join words together against you, and shake my head at you,

5158.text: but I would strengthen you with my mouth. The solace of my lips would relieve you.

5159.text: "Though I speak, my grief is not subsided. Though I forbear, what am I eased?

5160.text: But now, God, you have surely worn me out. You have made desolate all my company.

5161.text: You have shriveled me up. This is a witness against me. My leanness rises up against me. It testifies to my face.

5162.text: He has torn me in his wrath, and persecuted me. He has gnashed on me with his teeth. My adversary sharpens his eyes on me.

5163.text: They have gaped on me with their mouth. They have struck me on the cheek reproachfully. They gather themselves together against me.

5164.text: God delivers me to the ungodly, and casts me into the hands of the wicked.

5165.text: I was at ease, and he broke me apart. Yes, he has taken me by the neck, and dashed me to pieces. He has also set me up for his target.

5166.text: His archers surround me. He splits my kidneys apart, and does not spare. He pours out my gall on the ground.

5167.text: He breaks me with breach on breach. He runs on me like a giant.

5168.text: I have sewed sackcloth on my skin, and have thrust my horn in the dust.

5169.text: My face is red with weeping. Deep darkness is on my eyelids.

5170.text: Although there is no violence in my hands, and my prayer is pure.

5171.text: "Earth, do not cover my blood. Let my cry have no place to rest.

5172.text: Even now, behold, my witness is in heaven. He who vouches for me is on high.

5173.text: My friends scoff at me. My eyes pour out tears to God,

5174.text: that he would maintain the right of a man with God, of a son of man with his neighbor!

5175.text: For when a few years are come, I shall go the way from whence I shall not return.

5176.text: "My spirit is consumed. My days are extinct, And the grave is ready for me.

5177.text: Surely there are mockers with me. My eye dwells on their provocation.

5178.text: "Now give a pledge, be collateral for me with yourself. Who is there who will strike hands with me?

5179.text: For you have hidden their heart from understanding, Therefore you shall not exalt them.

5180.text: He who denounces his friends for a prey, Even the eyes of his children shall fail.

5181.text: "But he has made me a byword of the people. They spit in my face.

5182.text: My eye also is dim by reason of sorrow. All my members are as a shadow.

5183.text: Upright men shall be astonished at this. The innocent shall stir up himself against the godless.

5184.text: Yet shall the righteous hold on his way. He who has clean hands shall grow stronger and stronger.

5185.text: But as for you all, come on now again; I shall not find a wise man among you.

5186.text: My days are past, my plans are broken off, as are the thoughts of my heart.

5187.text: They change the night into day, saying 'The light is near' in the presence of darkness.

5188.text: If I look for Sheol as my house, if I have spread my couch in the darkness,

5189.text: If I have said to corruption, 'You are my father;' to the worm, 'My mother,' and 'my sister;'

5190.text: where then is my hope? As for my hope, who shall see it?

5191.text: Shall it go down with me to the gates of Sheol, or descend together into the dust?"

5193.text: "How long will you hunt for words? Consider, and afterwards we will speak.

5194.text: Why are we counted as animals, which have become unclean in your sight?

5195.text: You who tear yourself in your anger, shall the earth be forsaken for you? Or shall the rock be removed out of its place?

5196.text: "Yes, the light of the wicked shall be put out, The spark of his fire shall not shine.

5197.text: The light shall be dark in his tent. His lamp above him shall be put out.

5198.text: The steps of his strength shall be shortened. His own counsel shall cast him down.

5199.text: For he is cast into a net by his own feet, and he wanders into its mesh.

5200.text: A snare will take him by the heel. A trap will catch him.

5201.text: A noose is hidden for him in the ground, a trap for him in the way.

5202.text: Terrors shall make him afraid on every side, and shall chase him at his heels.

5203.text: His strength shall be famished. Calamity shall be ready at his side.

5204.text: The members of his body shall be devoured. The firstborn of death shall devour his members.

5205.text: He shall be rooted out of his tent where he trusts. He shall be brought to the king of terrors.

5206.text: There shall dwell in his tent that which is none of his. Sulfur shall be scattered on his habitation.

5207.text: His roots shall be dried up beneath. Above shall his branch be cut off.

5208.text: His memory shall perish from the earth. He shall have no name in the street.

5209.text: He shall be driven from light into darkness, and chased out of the world.

5210.text: He shall have neither son nor grandson among his people, nor any remaining where he sojourned.

5211.text: Those who come after shall be astonished at his day, as those who went before were frightened.

5212.text: Surely such are the dwellings of the unrighteous. This is the place of him who doesn't know God."

5214.text: "How long will you torment me, and crush me with words?

5215.text: You have reproached me ten times. You aren't ashamed that you attack me.

5216.text: If it is true that I have erred, my error remains with myself.

5217.text: If indeed you will magnify yourselves against me, and plead against me my reproach;

5218.text: know now that God has subverted me, and has surrounded me with his net.

5219.text: "Behold, I cry out 'Injustice!' but there is no justice.

5220.text: He has walled up my way so that I can't pass, and has set darkness in my paths.

5221.text: He has stripped me of my glory, and taken the crown from my head.

5222.text: He has broken me down on every side, and I am gone. My hope he has plucked up like a tree.

5223.text: He has also kindled his wrath against me. He counts me among his adversaries.

5224.text: His troops come on together, build a siege ramp against me, and encamp around my tent.

5225.text: "He has put my brothers far from me. My acquaintances are wholly estranged from me.

5226.text: My relatives have gone away. My familiar friends have forgotten me.

5227.text: Those who dwell in my house, and my maids, count me for a stranger. I am a foreigner in their sight.

5228.text: I call to my servant, and he gives me no answer. I beg him with my mouth.

5229.text: My breath is offensive to my wife. I am loathsome to the children of my own mother.

5230.text: Even young children despise me. If I arise, they speak against me.

5231.text: All my familiar friends abhor me. They whom I loved have turned against me.

5232.text: My bones stick to my skin and to my flesh. I have escaped by the skin of my teeth.

5233.text: "Have pity on me, have pity on me, you my friends; for the hand of God has touched me.

5234.text: Why do you persecute me as God, and are not satisfied with my flesh?

5235.text: "Oh that my words were now written! Oh that they were inscribed in a book!

5236.text: That with an iron pen and lead they were engraved in the rock forever!

5237.text: But as for me, I know that my Redeemer lives. In the end, he will stand upon the earth.

5238.text: After my skin is destroyed, then in my flesh shall I see God,

5239.text: Whom I, even I, shall see on my side. My eyes shall see, and not as a stranger. "My heart is consumed within me.

5240.text: If you say, 'How we will persecute him!' because the root of the matter is found in me,

5241.text: be afraid of the sword, for wrath brings the punishments of the sword, that you may know there is a judgment."

5243.text: "Therefore do my thoughts give answer to me, even by reason of my haste that is in me.

5244.text: I have heard the reproof which puts me to shame. The spirit of my understanding answers me.

5245.text: Do you not know this from old time, since man was placed on earth,

5246.text: that the triumphing of the wicked is short, the joy of the godless but for a moment?

5247.text: Though his height mount up to the heavens, and his head reach to the clouds,

5248.text: yet he shall perish forever like his own dung. Those who have seen him shall say, 'Where is he?'

5249.text: He shall fly away as a dream, and shall not be found. Yes, he shall be chased away like a vision of the night.

5250.text: The eye which saw him shall see him no more, neither shall his place any more see him.

5251.text: His children shall seek the favor of the poor. His hands shall give back his wealth.

5252.text: His bones are full of his youth, but youth shall lie down with him in the dust.

5253.text: "Though wickedness is sweet in his mouth, though he hide it under his tongue,

5254.text: though he spare it, and will not let it go, but keep it still within his mouth;

5255.text: yet his food in his bowels is turned. It is cobra venom within him.

5256.text: He has swallowed down riches, and he shall vomit them up again. God will cast them out of his belly.

5257.text: He shall suck cobra venom. The viper's tongue shall kill him.

5258.text: He shall not look at the rivers, the flowing streams of honey and butter.

5259.text: That for which he labored he shall restore, and shall not swallow it down. According to the substance that he has gotten, he shall not rejoice.

5260.text: For he has oppressed and forsaken the poor. He has violently taken away a house, and he shall not build it up.

5261.text: "Because he knew no quietness within him, he shall not save anything of that in which he delights.

5262.text: There was nothing left that he did not devour, therefore his prosperity shall not endure.

5263.text: In the fullness of his sufficiency, distress shall overtake him. The hand of everyone who is in misery shall come on him.

5264.text: When he is about to fill his belly, God will cast the fierceness of his wrath on him. It will rain on him while he is eating.

5265.text: He shall flee from the iron weapon. The bronze arrow shall strike him through.

5266.text: He draws it forth, and it comes out of his body. Yes, the glittering point comes out of his liver. Terrors are on him.

5267.text: All darkness is laid up for his treasures. An unfanned fire shall devour him. It shall consume that which is left in his tent.

5268.text: The heavens shall reveal his iniquity. The earth shall rise up against him.

5269.text: The increase of his house shall depart. They shall rush away in the day of his wrath.

5270.text: This is the portion of a wicked man from God, the heritage appointed to him by God."

5272.text: "Listen diligently to my speech. Let this be your consolation.

5273.text: Allow me, and I also will speak; After I have spoken, mock on.

5274.text: As for me, is my complaint to man? Why shouldn't I be impatient?

5275.text: Look at me, and be astonished. Lay your hand on your mouth.

5276.text: When I remember, I am troubled. Horror takes hold of my flesh.

5277.text: "Why do the wicked live, become old, yes, and grow mighty in power?

5278.text: Their child is established with them in their sight, their offspring before their eyes.

5279.text: Their houses are safe from fear, neither is the rod of God upon them.

5280.text: Their bulls breed without fail. Their cows calve, and do not miscarry.

5281.text: They send forth their little ones like a flock. Their children dance.

5282.text: They sing to the tambourine and harp, and rejoice at the sound of the pipe.

5283.text: They spend their days in prosperity. In an instant they go down to Sheol.

5284.text: They tell God, 'Depart from us, for we do not want to know about your ways.

5285.text: What is the Almighty, that we should serve him? What profit should we have, if we pray to him?'

5286.text: Behold, their prosperity is not in their hand. The counsel of the wicked is far from me.

5287.text: "How often is it that the lamp of the wicked is put out, that their calamity comes on them, that God distributes sorrows in his anger?

5288.text: How often is it that they are as stubble before the wind, as chaff that the storm carries away?

5289.text: You say, 'God lays up his iniquity for his children.' Let him recompense it to himself, that he may know it.

5290.text: Let his own eyes see his destruction. Let him drink of the wrath of the Almighty.

5291.text: For what does he care for his house after him, when the number of his months is cut off?

5292.text: "Shall any teach God knowledge, seeing he judges those who are high?

5293.text: One dies in his full strength, being wholly at ease and quiet.

5294.text: His pails are full of milk. The marrow of his bones is moistened.

5295.text: Another dies in bitterness of soul, and never tastes of good.

5296.text: They lie down alike in the dust. The worm covers them.

5297.text: "Behold, I know your thoughts, the devices with which you would wrong me.

5298.text: For you say, 'Where is the house of the prince? Where is the tent in which the wicked lived?'

5299.text: Haven't you asked wayfaring men? Do you not know their evidences,

5300.text: that the evil man is reserved to the day of calamity, That they are led forth to the day of wrath?

5301.text: Who shall declare his way to his face? Who shall repay him what he has done?

5302.text: Yet he will be borne to the grave. Men shall keep watch over the tomb.

5303.text: The clods of the valley shall be sweet to him. All men shall draw after him, as there were innumerable before him.

5304.text: So how can you comfort me with nonsense, seeing that in your answers there remains only falsehood?"

5306.text: "Can a man be profitable to God? Surely he who is wise is profitable to himself.

5307.text: Is it any pleasure to the Almighty, that you are righteous? Or does it benefit him, that you make your ways perfect?

5308.text: Is it for your piety that he reproves you, that he enters with you into judgment?

5309.text: Isn't your wickedness great? Neither is there any end to your iniquities.

5310.text: For you have taken pledges from your brother for nothing, and stripped the naked of their clothing.

5311.text: You haven't given water to the weary to drink, and you have withheld bread from the hungry.

5312.text: But as for the mighty man, he had the earth. The honorable man, he lived in it.

5313.text: You have sent widows away empty, and the arms of the fatherless have been broken.

5314.text: Therefore snares are around you. Sudden fear troubles you,

5315.text: or darkness, so that you can not see, and floods of waters cover you.

5316.text: "Isn't God in the heights of heaven? See the height of the stars, how high they are!

5317.text: You say, 'What does God know? Can he judge through the thick darkness?

5318.text: Thick clouds are a covering to him, so that he doesn't see. He walks on the vault of the sky.'

5319.text: Will you keep the old way, which wicked men have trodden,

5320.text: who were snatched away before their time, whose foundation was poured out as a stream,

5321.text: who said to God, 'Depart from us;' and, 'What can the Almighty do for us?'

5322.text: Yet he filled their houses with good things, but the counsel of the wicked is far from me.

5323.text: The righteous see it, and are glad. The innocent ridicule them,

5324.text: saying, 'Surely those who rose up against us are cut off. The fire has consumed the remnant of them.'

5325.text: "Acquaint yourself with him, now, and be at peace. Thereby good shall come to you.

5326.text: Please receive instruction from his mouth, and lay up his words in your heart.

5327.text: If you return to the Almighty, you shall be built up, if you put away unrighteousness far from your tents.

5328.text: Lay your treasure in the dust, the gold of Ophir among the stones of the brooks.

5329.text: The Almighty will be your treasure, and precious silver to you.

5330.text: For then you will delight yourself in the Almighty, and shall lift up your face to God.

5331.text: You shall make your prayer to him, and he will hear you. You shall pay your vows.

5332.text: You shall also decree a thing, and it shall be established to you. Light shall shine on your ways.

5333.text: When they cast down, you shall say, 'be lifted up.' He will save the humble person.

5334.text: He will even deliver him who is not innocent. Yes, he shall be delivered through the cleanness of your hands."

5336.text: "Even today my complaint is rebellious. His hand is heavy in spite of my groaning.

5337.text: Oh that I knew where I might find him! That I might come even to his seat!

5338.text: I would set my cause in order before him, and fill my mouth with arguments.

5339.text: I would know the words which he would answer me, and understand what he would tell me.

5340.text: Would he contend with me in the greatness of his power? No, but he would listen to me.

5341.text: There the upright might reason with him, so I should be delivered forever from my judge.

5342.text: "If I go east, he is not there; if west, I can't find him;

5343.text: He works to the north, but I can't see him. He turns south, but I can't catch a glimpse of him.

5344.text: But he knows the way that I take. When he has tried me, I shall come forth like gold.

5345.text: My foot has held fast to his steps. I have kept his way, and not turned aside.

5346.text: I haven't gone back from the commandment of his lips. I have treasured up the words of his mouth more than my necessary food.

5347.text: But he stands alone, and who can oppose him? What his soul desires, even that he does.

5348.text: For he performs that which is appointed for me. Many such things are with him.

5349.text: Therefore I am terrified at his presence. When I consider, I am afraid of him.

5350.text: For God has made my heart faint. The Almighty has terrified me.

5351.text: Because I was not cut off before the darkness, neither did he cover the thick darkness from my face.

5352.text: "Why aren't times laid up by the Almighty? Why do not those who know him see his days?

5353.text: There are people who remove the landmarks. They violently take away flocks, and feed them.

5354.text: They drive away the donkey of the fatherless, and they take the widow's ox for a pledge.

5355.text: They turn the needy out of the way. The poor of the earth all hide themselves.

5356.text: Behold, as wild donkeys in the desert, they go forth to their work, seeking diligently for food. The wilderness yields them bread for their children.

5357.text: They cut their provender in the field. They glean the vineyard of the wicked.

5358.text: They lie all night naked without clothing, and have no covering in the cold.

5359.text: They are wet with the showers of the mountains, and embrace the rock for lack of a shelter.

5360.text: There are those who pluck the fatherless from the breast, and take a pledge of the poor,

5361.text: So that they go around naked without clothing. Being hungry, they carry the sheaves.

5362.text: They make oil within the walls of these men. They tread wine presses, and suffer thirst.

5363.text: From out of the populous city, men groan. The soul of the wounded cries out, yet God doesn't regard the folly.

5364.text: "These are of those who rebel against the light. They do not know its ways, nor abide in its paths.

5365.text: The murderer rises with the light. He kills the poor and needy. In the night he is like a thief.

5366.text: The eye also of the adulterer waits for the twilight, saying, 'No eye shall see me.' He disguises his face.

5367.text: In the dark they dig through houses. They shut themselves up in the daytime. They do not know the light.

5368.text: For the morning is to all of them like thick darkness, for they know the terrors of the thick darkness.

5369.text: "They are foam on the surface of the waters. Their portion is cursed in the earth. They do not turn into the way of the vineyards.

5370.text: Drought and heat consume the snow waters, so does Sheol those who have sinned.

5371.text: The womb shall forget him. The worm shall feed sweetly on him. He shall be no more remembered. Unrighteousness shall be broken as a tree.

5372.text: He devours the barren who do not bear. He shows no kindness to the widow.

5373.text: Yet God preserves the mighty by his power. He rises up who has no assurance of life.

5374.text: God gives them security, and they rest in it. His eyes are on their ways.

5375.text: They are exalted; yet a little while, and they are gone. Yes, they are brought low, they are taken out of the way as all others, and are cut off as the tops of the ears of grain.

5376.text: If it isn't so now, who will prove me a liar, and make my speech worth nothing?"

5378.text: "Dominion and fear are with him. He makes peace in his high places.

5379.text: Can his armies be counted? On whom does his light not arise?

5380.text: How then can man be just with God? Or how can he who is born of a woman be clean?

5381.text: Behold, even the moon has no brightness, and the stars are not pure in his sight;

5382.text: How much less man, who is a worm, the son of man, who is a worm!"

5384.text: "How have you helped him who is without power! How have you saved the arm that has no strength!

5385.text: How have you counseled him who has no wisdom, and plentifully declared sound knowledge!

5386.text: To whom have you uttered words? Whose spirit came forth from you?

5387.text: "Those who are deceased tremble, those beneath the waters and all that live in them.

5388.text: Sheol is naked before God, and Abaddon has no covering.

5389.text: He stretches out the north over empty space, and hangs the earth on nothing.

5390.text: He binds up the waters in his thick clouds, and the cloud is not burst under them.

5391.text: He encloses the face of his throne, and spreads his cloud on it.

5392.text: He has described a boundary on the surface of the waters, and to the confines of light and darkness.

5393.text: The pillars of heaven tremble and are astonished at his rebuke.

5394.text: He stirs up the sea with his power, and by his understanding he strikes through Rahab.

5395.text: By his Spirit the heavens are garnished. His hand has pierced the swift serpent.

5396.text: Behold, these are but the outskirts of his ways. How small a whisper do we hear of him! But the thunder of his power who can understand?"

5397.text: Job again took up his parable, and said,

5398.text: "As God lives, who has taken away my right, the Almighty, who has made my soul bitter.

5399.text: (For the length of my life is still in me, and the spirit of God is in my nostrils);

5400.text: surely my lips shall not speak unrighteousness, neither shall my tongue utter deceit.

5401.text: Far be it from me that I should justify you. Until I die I will not put away my integrity from me.

5402.text: I hold fast to my righteousness, and will not let it go. My heart shall not reproach me so long as I live.

5403.text: "Let my enemy be as the wicked. Let him who rises up against me be as the unrighteous.

5404.text: For what is the hope of the godless, when he is cut off, when God takes away his life?

5405.text: Will God hear his cry when trouble comes on him?

5406.text: Will he delight himself in the Almighty, and call on God at all times?

5407.text: I will teach you about the hand of God. That which is with the Almighty will I not conceal.

5408.text: Behold, all of you have seen it yourselves; why then have you become altogether vain?

5409.text: "This is the portion of a wicked man with God, the heritage of oppressors, which they receive from the Almighty.

5410.text: If his children are multiplied, it is for the sword. His offspring shall not be satisfied with bread.

5411.text: Those who remain of him shall be buried in death. His widows shall make no lamentation.

5412.text: Though he heap up silver as the dust, and prepare clothing as the clay;

5413.text: he may prepare it, but the just shall put it on, and the innocent shall divide the silver.

5414.text: He builds his house as the moth, as a booth which the watchman makes.

5415.text: He lies down rich, but he shall not do so again. He opens his eyes, and he is not.

5416.text: Terrors overtake him like waters. A storm steals him away in the night.

5417.text: The east wind carries him away, and he departs. It sweeps him out of his place.

5418.text: For it hurls at him, and does not spare, as he flees away from his hand.

5419.text: Men shall clap their hands at him, and shall hiss him out of his place.

5420.text: "Surely there is a mine for silver, and a place for gold which they refine.

5421.text: Iron is taken out of the earth, and copper is smelted out of the ore.

5422.text: Man sets an end to darkness, and searches out, to the furthest bound, the stones of obscurity and of thick darkness.

5423.text: He breaks open a shaft away from where people live. They are forgotten by the foot. They hang far from men, they swing back and forth.

5424.text: As for the earth, out of it comes bread; Underneath it is turned up as it were by fire.

5425.text: Sapphires come from its rocks. It has dust of gold.

5426.text: That path no bird of prey knows, neither has the falcon's eye seen it.

5427.text: The proud animals have not trodden it, nor has the fierce lion passed by there.

5428.text: He puts forth his hand on the flinty rock, and he overturns the mountains by the roots.

5429.text: He cuts out channels among the rocks. His eye sees every precious thing.

5430.text: He binds the streams that they do not trickle. The thing that is hidden he brings forth to light.

5431.text: "But where shall wisdom be found? Where is the place of understanding?

5432.text: Man doesn't know its price; Neither is it found in the land of the living.

5433.text: The deep says, 'It isn't in me.' The sea says, 'It isn't with me.'

5434.text: It can't be gotten for gold, neither shall silver be weighed for its price.

5435.text: It can't be valued with the gold of Ophir, with the precious onyx, or the sapphire.

5436.text: Gold and glass can't equal it, neither shall it be exchanged for jewels of fine gold.

5437.text: No mention shall be made of coral or of crystal. Yes, the price of wisdom is above rubies.

5438.text: The topaz of Ethiopia shall not equal it, Neither shall it be valued with pure gold.
