5439.text: Whence then comes wisdom? Where is the place of understanding?

5440.text: Seeing it is hidden from the eyes of all living, and kept close from the birds of the sky.

5441.text: Destruction and Death say, 'We have heard a rumor of it with our ears.'

5442.text: "God understands its way, and he knows its place.

5443.text: For he looks to the ends of the earth, and sees under the whole sky.

5444.text: He establishes the force of the wind. Yes, he measures out the waters by measure.

5445.text: When he made a decree for the rain, and a way for the lightning of the thunder;

5446.text: then he saw it, and declared it. He established it, yes, and searched it out.

5447.text: To man he said, 'Behold, the fear of the Lord, that is wisdom. To depart from evil is understanding.'"

5448.text: Job again took up his parable, and said,

5449.text: "Oh that I were as in the months of old, as in the days when God watched over me;

5450.text: when his lamp shone on my head, and by his light I walked through darkness,

5451.text: as I was in the ripeness of my days, when the friendship of God was in my tent,

5452.text: when the Almighty was yet with me, and my children were around me,

5453.text: when my steps were washed with butter, and the rock poured out streams of oil for me,

5454.text: when I went forth to the city gate, when I prepared my seat in the street.

5455.text: The young men saw me and hid themselves. The aged rose up and stood.

5456.text: The princes refrained from talking, and laid their hand on their mouth.

5457.text: The voice of the nobles was hushed, and their tongue stuck to the roof of their mouth.

5458.text: For when the ear heard me, then it blessed me; and when the eye saw me, it commended me:

5459.text: Because I delivered the poor who cried, and the fatherless also, who had none to help him,

5460.text: the blessing of him who was ready to perish came on me, and I caused the widow's heart to sing for joy.

5461.text: I put on righteousness, and it clothed me. My justice was as a robe and a diadem.

5462.text: I was eyes to the blind, and feet to the lame.

5463.text: I was a father to the needy. The cause of him who I did not know, I searched out.

5464.text: I broke the jaws of the unrighteous, and plucked the prey out of his teeth.

5465.text: Then I said, 'I shall die in my own house, I shall number my days as the sand.

5466.text: My root is spread out to the waters. The dew lies all night on my branch.

5467.text: My glory is fresh in me. My bow is renewed in my hand.'

5468.text: "Men listened to me, waited, and kept silence for my counsel.

5469.text: After my words they did not speak again. My speech fell on them.

5470.text: They waited for me as for the rain. Their mouths drank as with the spring rain.

5471.text: I smiled on them when they had no confidence. They did not reject the light of my face.

5472.text: I chose out their way, and sat as chief. I lived as a king in the army, as one who comforts the mourners.

5473.text: "But now those who are younger than I have me in derision, whose fathers I would have disdained to put with my sheep dogs.

5474.text: Of what use is the strength of their hands to me, men in whom ripe age has perished?

5475.text: They are gaunt from lack and famine. They gnaw the dry ground, in the gloom of waste and desolation.

5476.text: They pluck salt herbs by the bushes. The roots of the broom are their food.

5477.text: They are driven out from the midst of men. They cry after them as after a thief;

5478.text: So that they dwell in frightful valleys, and in holes of the earth and of the rocks.

5479.text: Among the bushes they bray; and under the nettles they are gathered together.

5480.text: They are children of fools, yes, children of base men. They were flogged out of the land.

5481.text: "Now I have become their song. Yes, I am a byword to them.

5482.text: They abhor me, they stand aloof from me, and do not hesitate to spit in my face.

5483.text: For he has untied his cord, and afflicted me; and they have thrown off restraint before me.

5484.text: On my right hand rise the rabble. They thrust aside my feet, They cast up against me their ways of destruction.

5485.text: They mar my path, They set forward my calamity, without anyone's help.

5486.text: As through a wide breach they come, in the midst of the ruin they roll themselves in.

5487.text: Terrors have turned on me. They chase my honor as the wind. My welfare has passed away as a cloud.

5488.text: "Now my soul is poured out within me. Days of affliction have taken hold on me.

5489.text: In the night season my bones are pierced in me, and the pains that gnaw me take no rest.

5490.text: By great force is my garment disfigured. It binds me about as the collar of my coat.

5491.text: He has cast me into the mire. I have become like dust and ashes.

5492.text: I cry to you, and you do not answer me. I stand up, and you gaze at me.

5493.text: You have turned to be cruel to me. With the might of your hand you persecute me.

5494.text: You lift me up to the wind, and drive me with it. You dissolve me in the storm.

5495.text: For I know that you will bring me to death, To the house appointed for all living.

5496.text: "However doesn't one stretch out a hand in his fall? Or in his calamity therefore cry for help?

5497.text: Did I not weep for him who was in trouble? Wasn't my soul grieved for the needy?

5498.text: When I looked for good, then evil came; When I waited for light, there came darkness.

5499.text: My heart is troubled, and doesn't rest. Days of affliction have come on me.

5500.text: I go mourning without the sun. I stand up in the assembly, and cry for help.

5501.text: I am a brother to jackals, and a companion to ostriches.

5502.text: My skin grows black and peels from me. My bones are burned with heat.

5503.text: Therefore my harp has turned to mourning, and my pipe into the voice of those who weep.

5504.text: "I made a covenant with my eyes, how then should I look lustfully at a young woman?

5505.text: For what is the portion from God above, and the heritage from the Almighty on high?

5506.text: Is it not calamity for the unrighteous, and disaster for the workers of iniquity?

5507.text: Doesn't he see my ways, and number all my steps?

5508.text: "If I have walked with falsehood, and my foot has hurried to deceit

5509.text: (let me be weighed in an even balance, that God may know my integrity);

5510.text: if my step has turned out of the way, if my heart walked after my eyes, if any defilement has stuck to my hands,

5511.text: then let me sow, and let another eat. Yes, let the produce of my field be rooted out.

5512.text: "If my heart has been enticed to a woman, and I have lain in wait at my neighbor's door,

5513.text: then let my wife grind for another, and let others sleep with her.

5514.text: For that would be a heinous crime. Yes, it would be an iniquity to be punished by the judges:

5515.text: For it is a fire that consumes to destruction, and would root out all my increase.

5516.text: "If I have despised the cause of my male servant or of my female servant, when they contended with me;

5517.text: What then shall I do when God rises up? When he visits, what shall I answer him?

5518.text: Did not he who made me in the womb make him? Did not the same one fashion us in the womb?

5519.text: "If I have withheld the poor from their desire, or have caused the eyes of the widow to fail,

5520.text: or have eaten my morsel alone, and the fatherless has not eaten of it

5521.text: (no, from my youth he grew up with me as with a father, her have I guided from my mother's womb);

5522.text: if I have seen any perish for want of clothing, or that the needy had no covering;

5523.text: if his heart hasn't blessed me, if he hasn't been warmed with my sheep's fleece;

5524.text: if I have lifted up my hand against the fatherless, because I saw my help in the gate,

5525.text: then let my shoulder fall from the shoulder blade, and my arm be broken from the bone.

5526.text: For calamity from God is a terror to me. Because his majesty, I can do nothing.

5527.text: "If I have made gold my hope, and have said to the fine gold, 'You are my confidence;'

5528.text: If I have rejoiced because my wealth was great, and because my hand had gotten much;

5529.text: if I have seen the sun when it shined, or the moon moving in splendor,

5530.text: and my heart has been secretly enticed, and my hand threw a kiss from my mouth,

5531.text: this also would be an iniquity to be punished by the judges; for I should have denied the God who is above.

5532.text: "If I have rejoiced at the destruction of him who hated me, or lifted up myself when evil found him;

5533.text: (yes, I have not allowed my mouth to sin by asking his life with a curse);

5534.text: if the men of my tent have not said, 'Who can find one who has not been filled with his meat?'

5535.text: (the foreigner has not lodged in the street, but I have opened my doors to the traveler);

5536.text: if like Adam I have covered my transgressions, by hiding my iniquity in my heart,

5537.text: because I feared the great multitude, and the contempt of families terrified me, so that I kept silence, and did not go out of the door-

5538.text: oh that I had one to hear me! (behold, here is my signature, let the Almighty answer me); let the accuser write my indictment!

5539.text: Surely I would carry it on my shoulder; and I would bind it to me as a crown.

5540.text: I would declare to him the number of my steps; as a prince would I go near to him.

5541.text: If my land cries out against me, and its furrows weep together;

5542.text: if I have eaten its fruits without money, or have caused its owners to lose their life,

5543.text: let briars grow instead of wheat, and stinkweed instead of barley." The words of Job are ended.

5544.text: So these three men ceased to answer Job, because he was righteous in his own eyes.

5545.text: Then the wrath of Elihu the son of Barachel, the Buzite, of the family of Ram, was kindled against Job. His wrath was kindled because he justified himself rather than God.

5546.text: Also his wrath was kindled against his three friends, because they had found no answer, and yet had condemned Job.

5547.text: Now Elihu had waited to speak to Job, because they were elder than he.

5548.text: When Elihu saw that there was no answer in the mouth of these three men, his wrath was kindled.

5549.text: Elihu the son of Barachel the Buzite answered, "I am young, and you are very old; Therefore I held back, and did not dare show you my opinion.

5550.text: I said, 'Days should speak, and multitude of years should teach wisdom.'

5551.text: But there is a spirit in man, and the breath of the Almighty gives them understanding.

5552.text: It is not the great who are wise, nor the aged who understand justice.

5553.text: Therefore I said, 'Listen to me; I also will show my opinion.'

5554.text: "Behold, I waited for your words, and I listened for your reasoning, while you searched out what to say.

5555.text: Yes, I gave you my full attention, but there was no one who convinced Job, or who answered his words, among you.

5556.text: Beware lest you say, 'We have found wisdom, God may refute him, not man;'

5557.text: for he has not directed his words against me; neither will I answer him with your speeches.

5558.text: "They are amazed. They answer no more. They do not have a word to say.

5559.text: Shall I wait, because they do not speak, because they stand still, and answer no more?

5560.text: I also will answer my part, and I also will show my opinion.

5561.text: For I am full of words. The spirit within me constrains me.

5562.text: Behold, my breast is as wine which has no vent; like new wineskins it is ready to burst.

5563.text: I will speak, that I may be refreshed. I will open my lips and answer.

5564.text: Please do not let me respect any man's person, neither will I give flattering titles to any man.

5565.text: For I do not know how to give flattering titles; or else my Maker would soon take me away.

5566.text: "However, Job, Please hear my speech, and listen to all my words.

5567.text: See now, I have opened my mouth. My tongue has spoken in my mouth.

5568.text: My words shall utter the uprightness of my heart. That which my lips know they shall speak sincerely.

5569.text: The Spirit of God has made me, and the breath of the Almighty gives me life.

5570.text: If you can, answer me. Set your words in order before me, and stand forth.

5571.text: Behold, I am toward God even as you are. I am also formed out of the clay.

5572.text: Behold, my terror shall not make you afraid, neither shall my pressure be heavy on you.

5573.text: "Surely you have spoken in my hearing, I have heard the voice of your words, saying,

5574.text: 'I am clean, without disobedience. I am innocent, neither is there iniquity in me.

5575.text: Behold, he finds occasions against me. He counts me for his enemy.

5576.text: He puts my feet in the stocks. He marks all my paths.'

5577.text: "Behold, I will answer you. In this you are not just, for God is greater than man.

5578.text: Why do you strive against him, because he doesn't give account of any of his matters?

5579.text: For God speaks once, yes twice, though man pays no attention.

5580.text: In a dream, in a vision of the night, when deep sleep falls on men, in slumbering on the bed;

5581.text: Then he opens the ears of men, and seals their instruction,

5582.text: That he may withdraw man from his purpose, and hide pride from man.

5583.text: He keeps back his soul from the pit, and his life from perishing by the sword.

5584.text: He is chastened also with pain on his bed, with continual strife in his bones;

5585.text: So that his life abhors bread, and his soul dainty food.

5586.text: His flesh is so consumed away, that it can't be seen. His bones that were not seen stick out.

5587.text: Yes, his soul draws near to the pit, and his life to the destroyers.

5588.text: "If there is beside him an angel, an interpreter, one among a thousand, to show to man what is right for him;

5589.text: then God is gracious to him, and says, 'Deliver him from going down to the pit, I have found a ransom.'

5590.text: His flesh shall be fresher than a child's. He returns to the days of his youth.

5591.text: He prays to God, and he is favorable to him, so that he sees his face with joy. He restores to man his righteousness.

5592.text: He sings before men, and says, 'I have sinned, and perverted that which was right, and it did not profit me.

5593.text: He has redeemed my soul from going into the pit. My life shall see the light.'

5594.text: "Behold, God works all these things, twice, yes three times, with a man,

5595.text: to bring back his soul from the pit, that he may be enlightened with the light of the living.

5596.text: Mark well, Job, and listen to me. Hold your peace, and I will speak.

5597.text: If you have anything to say, answer me. Speak, for I desire to justify you.

5598.text: If not, listen to me. Hold your peace, and I will teach you wisdom."

5600.text: "Hear my words, you wise men. Give ear to me, you who have knowledge.

5601.text: For the ear tries words, as the palate tastes food.

5602.text: Let us choose for us that which is right. Let us know among ourselves what is good.

5603.text: For Job has said, 'I am righteous, God has taken away my right:

5604.text: Notwithstanding my right I am considered a liar. My wound is incurable, though I am without disobedience.'

5605.text: What man is like Job, who drinks scorn like water,

5606.text: Who goes in company with the workers of iniquity, and walks with wicked men?

5607.text: For he has said, 'It profits a man nothing that he should delight himself with God.'

5608.text: "Therefore listen to me, you men of understanding: far be it from God, that he should do wickedness, from the Almighty, that he should commit iniquity.

5609.text: For the work of a man he will render to him, and cause every man to find according to his ways.

5610.text: Yes surely, God will not do wickedly, neither will the Almighty pervert justice.

5611.text: Who put him in charge of the earth? or who has appointed him over the whole world?

5612.text: If he set his heart on himself, If he gathered to himself his spirit and his breath,

5613.text: all flesh would perish together, and man would turn again to dust.

5614.text: "If now you have understanding, hear this. Listen to the voice of my words.

5615.text: Shall even one who hates justice govern? Will you condemn him who is righteous and mighty?-

5616.text: Who says to a king, 'Vile!' or to nobles, 'Wicked!'?

5617.text: Who doesn't respect the persons of princes, nor regards the rich more than the poor; for they all are the work of his hands.

5618.text: In a moment they die, even at midnight. The people are shaken and pass away. The mighty are taken away without a hand.

5619.text: "For his eyes are on the ways of a man. He sees all his goings.

5620.text: There is no darkness, nor thick gloom, where the workers of iniquity may hide themselves.

5621.text: For he doesn't need to consider a man further, that he should go before God in judgment.

5622.text: He breaks in pieces mighty men in ways past finding out, and sets others in their place.

5623.text: Therefore he takes knowledge of their works. He overturns them in the night, so that they are destroyed.

5624.text: He strikes them as wicked men in the open sight of others;

5625.text: because they turned aside from following him, and wouldn't pay attention to any of his ways,

5626.text: so that they caused the cry of the poor to come to him. He heard the cry of the afflicted.

5627.text: When he gives quietness, who then can condemn? When he hides his face, who then can see him? Alike whether to a nation, or to a man,

5628.text: that the godless man may not reign, that there be no one to ensnare the people.

5629.text: "For has any said to God, 'I am guilty, but I will not offend any more.

5630.text: Teach me that which I do not see. If I have done iniquity, I will do it no more'?

5631.text: Shall his recompense be as you desire, that you refuse it? For you must choose, and not I. Therefore speak what you know.

5632.text: Men of understanding will tell me, yes, every wise man who hears me:

5633.text: 'Job speaks without knowledge. His words are without wisdom.'

5634.text: I wish that Job were tried to the end, because of his answering like wicked men.

5635.text: For he adds rebellion to his sin. He claps his hands among us, and multiplies his words against God."

5637.text: "Do you think this to be your right, or do you say, 'My righteousness is more than God's,'

5638.text: That you ask, 'What advantage will it be to you? What profit shall I have, more than if I had sinned?'

5639.text: I will answer you, and your companions with you.

5640.text: Look to the heavens, and see. See the skies, which are higher than you.

5641.text: If you have sinned, what effect do you have against him? If your transgressions are multiplied, what do you do to him?

5642.text: If you are righteous, what do you give him? Or what does he receive from your hand?

5643.text: Your wickedness may hurt a man as you are, and your righteousness may profit a son of man.

5644.text: "By reason of the multitude of oppressions they cry out. They cry for help by reason of the arm of the mighty.

5645.text: But none says, 'Where is God my Maker, who gives songs in the night,

5646.text: who teaches us more than the animals of the earth, and makes us wiser than the birds of the sky?'

5647.text: There they cry, but none gives answer, because of the pride of evil men.

5648.text: Surely God will not hear an empty cry, neither will the Almighty regard it.

5649.text: How much less when you say you do not see him. The cause is before him, and you wait for him!

5650.text: But now, because he has not visited in his anger, neither does he greatly regard arrogance.

5651.text: Therefore Job opens his mouth with empty talk, and he multiplies words without knowledge."

5653.text: "Bear with me a little, and I will show you; for I still have something to say on God's behalf.

5654.text: I will get my knowledge from afar, and will ascribe righteousness to my Maker.

5655.text: For truly my words are not false. One who is perfect in knowledge is with you.

5656.text: "Behold, God is mighty, and doesn't despise anyone. He is mighty in strength of understanding.

5657.text: He doesn't preserve the life of the wicked, but gives to the afflicted their right.

5658.text: He doesn't withdraw his eyes from the righteous, but with kings on the throne, he sets them forever, and they are exalted.

5659.text: If they are bound in fetters, and are taken in the cords of afflictions,

5660.text: then he shows them their work, and their transgressions, that they have behaved themselves proudly.

5661.text: He also opens their ears to instruction, and commands that they return from iniquity.

5662.text: If they listen and serve him, they shall spend their days in prosperity, and their years in pleasures.

5663.text: But if they do not listen, they shall perish by the sword; they shall die without knowledge.

5664.text: "But those who are godless in heart lay up anger. They do not cry for help when he binds them.

5665.text: They die in youth. Their life perishes among the unclean.

5666.text: He delivers the afflicted by their affliction, and opens their ear in oppression.

5667.text: Yes, he would have allured you out of distress, into a broad place, where there is no restriction. That which is set on your table would be full of fatness.

5668.text: "But you are full of the judgment of the wicked. Judgment and justice take hold of you.

5669.text: Do not let riches entice you to wrath, neither let the great size of a bribe turn you aside.

5670.text: Would your wealth sustain you in distress, or all the might of your strength?

5671.text: Do not desire the night, when people are cut off in their place.

5672.text: Take heed, do not regard iniquity; for you have chosen this rather than affliction.

5673.text: Behold, God is exalted in his power. Who is a teacher like him?

5674.text: Who has prescribed his way for him? Or who can say, 'You have committed unrighteousness?'

5675.text: "Remember that you magnify his work, whereof men have sung.

5676.text: All men have looked thereon. Man sees it afar off.

5677.text: Behold, God is great, and we do not know him. The number of his years is unsearchable.

5678.text: For he draws up the drops of water, which distill in rain from his vapor,

5679.text: Which the skies pour down and which drop on man abundantly.

5680.text: Yes, can any understand the spreading of the clouds, and the thunderings of his pavilion?

5681.text: Behold, he spreads his light around him. He covers the bottom of the sea.

5682.text: For by these he judges the people. He gives food in abundance.

5683.text: He covers his hands with the lightning, and commands it to strike the mark.

5684.text: Its noise tells about him, and the livestock also concerning the storm that comes up.

5685.text: "Yes, at this my heart trembles, and is moved out of its place.

5686.text: Hear, oh, hear the noise of his voice, the sound that goes out of his mouth.

5687.text: He sends it forth under the whole sky, and his lightning to the ends of the earth.

5688.text: After it a voice roars. He thunders with the voice of his majesty. He doesn't hold back anything when his voice is heard.

5689.text: God thunders marvelously with his voice. He does great things, which we can't comprehend.

5690.text: For he says to the snow, 'Fall on the earth;' likewise to the shower of rain, and to the showers of his mighty rain.

5691.text: He seals up the hand of every man, that all men whom he has made may know it.

5692.text: Then the animals take cover, and remain in their dens.

5693.text: Out of its chamber comes the storm, and cold out of the north.

5694.text: By the breath of God, ice is given, and the breadth of the waters is frozen.

5695.text: Yes, he loads the thick cloud with moisture. He spreads abroad the cloud of his lightning.

5696.text: It is turned around by his guidance, that they may do whatever he commands them on the surface of the habitable world,

5697.text: Whether it is for correction, or for his land, or for loving kindness, that he causes it to come.

5698.text: "Listen to this, Job. Stand still, and consider the wondrous works of God.

5699.text: Do you know how God controls them, and causes the lightning of his cloud to shine?

5700.text: Do you know the workings of the clouds, the wondrous works of him who is perfect in knowledge?

5701.text: You whose clothing is warm, when the earth is still by reason of the south wind?

5702.text: Can you, with him, spread out the sky, which is strong as a cast metal mirror?

5703.text: Teach us what we shall tell him, for we can't make our case by reason of darkness.

5704.text: Shall it be told him that I would speak? Or should a man wish that he were swallowed up?

5705.text: Now men do not see the light which is bright in the skies, but the wind passes, and clears them.

5706.text: Out of the north comes golden splendor. With God is awesome majesty.

5707.text: We can't reach the Almighty. He is exalted in power. In justice and great righteousness, he will not oppress.

5708.text: Therefore men revere him. He doesn't regard any who are wise of heart."

5709.text: Then the Lord answered Job out of the whirlwind,

5710.text: "Who is this who darkens counsel by words without knowledge?

5711.text: Brace yourself like a man, for I will question you, then you answer me!

5712.text: "Where were you when I laid the foundations of the earth? Declare, if you have understanding.

5713.text: Who determined its measures, if you know? Or who stretched the line on it?

5714.text: Whereupon were its foundations fastened? Or who laid its cornerstone,

5715.text: when the morning stars sang together, and all the sons of God shouted for joy?

5716.text: "Or who shut up the sea with doors, when it broke forth from the womb,

5717.text: when I made clouds its garment, and wrapped it in thick darkness,

5718.text: marked out for it my bound, set bars and doors,

5719.text: and said, 'Here you may come, but no further. Here your proud waves shall be stayed?'

5720.text: "Have you commanded the morning in your days, and caused the dawn to know its place;

5721.text: that it might take hold of the ends of the earth, and shake the wicked out of it?

5722.text: It is changed as clay under the seal, and stands forth as a garment.

5723.text: From the wicked, their light is withheld. The high arm is broken.

5724.text: "Have you entered into the springs of the sea? Or have you walked in the recesses of the deep?

5725.text: Have the gates of death been revealed to you? Or have you seen the gates of the shadow of death?

5726.text: Have you comprehended the earth in its breadth? Declare, if you know it all.

5727.text: "What is the way to the dwelling of light? As for darkness, where is its place,

5728.text: that you should take it to its bound, that you should discern the paths to its house?

5729.text: Surely you know, for you were born then, and the number of your days is great!

5730.text: Have you entered the treasuries of the snow, or have you seen the treasures of the hail,

5731.text: which I have reserved against the time of trouble, against the day of battle and war?

5732.text: By what way is the lightning distributed, or the east wind scattered on the earth?

5733.text: Who has cut a channel for the flood water, or the path for the thunderstorm;

5734.text: To cause it to rain on a land where no man is; on the wilderness, in which there is no man;

5735.text: to satisfy the waste and desolate ground, to cause the tender grass to spring forth?

5736.text: Does the rain have a father? Or who fathers the drops of dew?

5737.text: Out of whose womb came the ice? The gray frost of the sky, who has given birth to it?

5738.text: The waters become hard like stone, when the surface of the deep is frozen.

5739.text: "Can you bind the cluster of the Pleiades, or loosen the cords of Orion?

5740.text: Can you lead forth the constellations in their season? Or can you guide the Bear with her cubs?

5741.text: Do you know the laws of the heavens? Can you establish its dominion over the earth?

5742.text: "Can you lift up your voice to the clouds, That abundance of waters may cover you?

5743.text: Can you send forth lightnings, that they may go? Do they report to you, 'Here we are?'

5744.text: Who has put wisdom in the inward parts? Or who has given understanding to the mind?

5745.text: Who can number the clouds by wisdom? Or who can pour out the bottles of the sky,

5746.text: when the dust runs into a mass, and the clods of earth stick together?

5747.text: "Can you hunt the prey for the lioness, or satisfy the appetite of the young lions,

5748.text: when they crouch in their dens, and lie in wait in the thicket?

5749.text: Who provides for the raven his prey, when his young ones cry to God, and wander for lack of food?

5750.text: "Do you know the time when the mountain goats give birth? Do you watch when the doe bears fawns?

5751.text: Can you number the months that they fulfill? Or do you know the time when they give birth?

5752.text: They bow themselves, they bring forth their young, they end their labor pains.

5753.text: Their young ones become strong. They grow up in the open field. They go forth, and do not return again.

5754.text: "Who has set the wild donkey free? Or who has loosened the bonds of the swift donkey,

5755.text: Whose home I have made the wilderness, and the salt land his dwelling place?

5756.text: He scorns the tumult of the city, neither does he hear the shouting of the driver.

5757.text: The range of the mountains is his pasture, He searches after every green thing.

5758.text: "Will the wild ox be content to serve you? Or will he stay by your feeding trough?

5759.text: Can you hold the wild ox in the furrow with his harness? Or will he till the valleys after you?

5760.text: Will you trust him, because his strength is great? Or will you leave to him your labor?

5761.text: Will you confide in him, that he will bring home your seed, and gather the grain of your threshing floor?

5762.text: "The wings of the ostrich wave proudly; but are they the feathers and plumage of love?

5763.text: For she leaves her eggs on the earth, warms them in the dust,

5764.text: and forgets that the foot may crush them, or that the wild animal may trample them.

5765.text: She deals harshly with her young ones, as if they were not hers. Though her labor is in vain, she is without fear,

5766.text: because God has deprived her of wisdom, neither has he imparted to her understanding.

5767.text: When she lifts up herself on high, she scorns the horse and his rider.

5768.text: "Have you given the horse might? Have you clothed his neck with a quivering mane?

5769.text: Have you made him to leap as a locust? The glory of his snorting is awesome.

5770.text: He paws in the valley, and rejoices in his strength. He goes out to meet the armed men.

5771.text: He mocks at fear, and is not dismayed, neither does he turn back from the sword.

5772.text: The quiver rattles against him, the flashing spear and the javelin.

5773.text: He eats up the ground with fierceness and rage, neither does he stand still at the sound of the trumpet.

5774.text: As often as the trumpet sounds he snorts, 'Aha!' He smells the battle afar off, the thunder of the captains, and the shouting.

5775.text: "Is it by your wisdom that the hawk soars, and stretches her wings toward the south?

5776.text: Is it at your command that the eagle mounts up, and makes his nest on high?

5777.text: On the cliff he dwells, and makes his home, on the point of the cliff, and the stronghold.

5778.text: From there he spies out the prey. His eyes see it afar off.

5779.text: His young ones also suck up blood. Where the slain are, there he is."

5781.text: "Shall he who argues contend with the Almighty? He who argues with God, let him answer it."

5783.text: "Behold, I am of small account. What shall I answer you? I lay my hand on my mouth.

5784.text: I have spoken once, and I will not answer; Yes, twice, but I will proceed no further."

5785.text: Then the Lord answered Job out of the whirlwind,

5786.text: "Now brace yourself like a man. I will question you, and you will answer me.

5787.text: Will you even annul my judgment? Will you condemn me, that you may be justified?

5788.text: Or do you have an arm like God? Can you thunder with a voice like him?

5789.text: "Now deck yourself with excellency and dignity. Array yourself with honor and majesty.

5790.text: Pour out the fury of your anger. Look at everyone who is proud, and bring him low.

5791.text: Look at everyone who is proud, and humble him. Crush the wicked in their place.

5792.text: Hide them in the dust together. Bind their faces in the hidden place.

5793.text: Then I will also admit to you that your own right hand can save you.

5794.text: "See now, behemoth, which I made as well as you. He eats grass as an ox.

5795.text: Look now, his strength is in his thighs. His force is in the muscles of his belly.

5796.text: He moves his tail like a cedar. The sinews of his thighs are knit together.

5797.text: His bones are like tubes of brass. His limbs are like bars of iron.

5798.text: He is the chief of the ways of God. He who made him gives him his sword.

5799.text: Surely the mountains produce food for him, where all the animals of the field play.

5800.text: He lies under the lotus trees, in the covert of the reed, and the marsh.

5801.text: The lotuses cover him with their shade. The willows of the brook surround him.

5802.text: Behold, if a river overflows, he doesn't tremble. He is confident, though the Jordan swells even to his mouth.

5803.text: Shall any take him when he is on the watch, or pierce through his nose with a snare?

5804.text: "Can you draw out Leviathan with a fishhook, or press down his tongue with a cord?

5805.text: Can you put a rope into his nose, or pierce his jaw through with a hook?

5806.text: Will he make many petitions to you, or will he speak soft words to you?

5807.text: Will he make a covenant with you, that you should take him for a servant forever?

5808.text: Will you play with him as with a bird? Or will you bind him for your girls?

5809.text: Will traders barter for him? Will they part him among the merchants?

5810.text: Can you fill his skin with barbed irons, or his head with fish spears?

5811.text: Lay your hand on him. Remember the battle, and do so no more.

5812.text: Behold, the hope of him is in vain. Won't one be cast down even at the sight of him?

5813.text: None is so fierce that he dare stir him up. Who then is he who can stand before me?

5814.text: Who has first given to me, that I should repay him? Everything under the heavens is mine.

5815.text: "I will not keep silence concerning his limbs, nor his mighty strength, nor his goodly frame.

5816.text: Who can strip off his outer garment? Who shall come within his jaws?

5817.text: Who can open the doors of his face? Around his teeth is terror.

5818.text: Strong scales are his pride, shut up together with a close seal.

5819.text: One is so near to another, that no air can come between them.

5820.text: They are joined one to another. They stick together, so that they can't be pulled apart.

5821.text: His sneezing flashes out light. His eyes are like the eyelids of the morning.

5822.text: Out of his mouth go burning torches. Sparks of fire leap forth.

5823.text: Out of his nostrils a smoke goes, as of a boiling pot over a fire of reeds.

5824.text: His breath kindles coals. A flame goes forth from his mouth.

5825.text: There is strength in his neck. Terror dances before him.

5826.text: The flakes of his flesh are joined together. They are firm on him. They can't be moved.

5827.text: His heart is as firm as a stone, yes, firm as the lower millstone.

5828.text: When he raises himself up, the mighty are afraid. They retreat before his thrashing.

5829.text: If one attacks him with the sword, it can't prevail; nor the spear, the dart, nor the pointed shaft.

5830.text: He counts iron as straw; and brass as rotten wood.

5831.text: The arrow can't make him flee. Sling stones are like chaff to him.

5832.text: Clubs are counted as stubble. He laughs at the rushing of the javelin.

5833.text: His undersides are like sharp potsherds, leaving a trail in the mud like a threshing sledge.

5834.text: He makes the deep to boil like a pot. He makes the sea like a pot of ointment.

5835.text: He makes a path shine after him. One would think the deep had white hair.

5836.text: On earth there is not his equal, that is made without fear.

5837.text: He sees everything that is high. He is king over all the sons of pride."

5839.text: "I know that you can do all things, and that no purpose of yours can be restrained.

5840.text: You asked, 'Who is this who hides counsel without knowledge?' therefore I have uttered that which I did not understand, things too wonderful for me, which I did not know.

5841.text: You said, 'Listen, now, and I will speak; I will question you, and you will answer me.'

5842.text: I had heard of you by the hearing of the ear, but now my eye sees you.

5843.text: Therefore I abhor myself, and repent in dust and ashes."

5844.text: It was so, that after the Lord had spoken these words to Job, the Lord said to Eliphaz the Temanite, "My wrath is kindled against you, and against your two friends; for you have not spoken of me the thing that is right, as my servant Job has.

5845.text: Now therefore, take to yourselves seven bulls and seven rams, and go to my servant Job, and offer up for yourselves a burnt offering; and my servant Job shall pray for you, for I will accept him, that I not deal with you according to your folly. For you have not spoken of me the thing that is right, as my servant Job has."

5846.text: So Eliphaz the Temanite and Bildad the Shuhite and Zophar the Naamathite went, and did what the Lord commanded them, and the Lord accepted Job.

5847.text: The Lord turned the captivity of Job, when he prayed for his friends. The Lord gave Job twice as much as he had before.

5848.text: Then came there to him all his brothers, and all his sisters, and all those who had been of his acquaintance before, and ate bread with him in his house. They comforted him, and consoled him concerning all the evil that the Lord had brought on him. Everyone also gave him a piece of money, and everyone a ring of gold.

5849.text: So the Lord blessed the latter end of Job more than his beginning. He had fourteen thousand sheep, six thousand camels, one thousand yoke of oxen, and a thousand female donkeys.

5850.text: He had also seven sons and three daughters.

5851.text: He called the name of the first, Jemimah; and the name of the second, Keziah; and the name of the third, Keren Happuch.

5852.text: In all the land were no women found so beautiful as the daughters of Job. Their father gave them an inheritance among their brothers.

5853.text: After this Job lived one hundred forty years, and saw his sons, and his sons' sons, to four generations.

5854.text: So Job died, being old and full of days.

5855.text: Blessed is the man who doesn't walk in the counsel of the wicked, nor stand in the way of sinners, nor sit in the seat of scoffers;

5856.text: but his delight is in the Lord's Law. On his Law he meditates day and night.

5857.text: He will be like a tree planted by the streams of water, that brings forth its fruit in its season, whose leaf also does not wither. Whatever he does shall prosper.

5858.text: The wicked are not so, but are like the chaff which the wind drives away.

5859.text: Therefore the wicked shall not stand in the judgment, nor sinners in the congregation of the righteous.

5860.text: For the Lord knows the way of the righteous, but the way of the wicked shall perish.

5861.text: Why do the nations rage, and the peoples plot a vain thing?

5862.text: The kings of the earth take a stand, and the rulers take counsel together, against the Lord, and against his Anointed, saying,

5863.text: "Let's break their bonds apart, and cast their cords from us."

5864.text: He who sits in the heavens will laugh. The Lord will have them in derision.

5865.text: Then he will speak to them in his anger, and terrify them in his wrath:

5866.text: "Yet I have set my king on my holy hill of Zion."

5867.text: I will tell of the decree. The Lord said to me, "You are my son. Today I have become your father.

5868.text: Ask of me, and I will give the nations for your inheritance, the uttermost parts of the earth for your possession.

5869.text: You shall rule them with a rod of iron. You shall dash them in pieces like a potter's vessel."

5870.text: Now therefore be wise, you kings. Be instructed, you judges of the earth.

5871.text: Serve the Lord with fear, and rejoice with trembling.

5872.text: Kiss the son, lest he be angry, and you perish in the way, for his wrath will soon be kindled. Blessed are all those who take refuge in him.

5873.text: Lord, how my adversaries have increased! Many are those who rise up against me.

5874.text: Many there are who say of my soul, "There is no help for him in God." Selah.

5875.text: But you, Lord, are a shield around me, my glory, and the one who lifts up my head.

5876.text: I cry to the Lord with my voice, and he answers me out of his holy hill. Selah.

5877.text: I laid myself down and slept. I awakened; for the Lord sustains me.

5878.text: I will not be afraid of tens of thousands of people who have set themselves against me on every side.

5879.text: Arise, Lord! Save me, my God! For you have struck all of my enemies on the cheek bone. You have broken the teeth of the wicked.

5880.text: Salvation belongs to the Lord. Your blessing be on your people. Selah.

5881.text: Answer me when I call, God of my righteousness. Give me relief from my distress. Have mercy on me, and hear my prayer.

5882.text: You sons of men, how long shall my glory be turned into dishonor? Will you love vanity, and seek after falsehood? Selah.

5883.text: But know that the Lord has set apart for himself him who is godly: The Lord will hear when I call to him.

5884.text: When agitated, do not sin. Search your own heart on your bed, and be still. Selah.

5885.text: Offer the sacrifices of righteousness. Put your trust in the Lord.

5886.text: Many say, "Who will show us any good?" Lord, let the light of your face shine on us.

5887.text: You have put gladness in my heart, more than when their grain and their new wine are increased.

5888.text: In peace I will both lay myself down and sleep, for you, the Lord alone, make me live in safety.

5889.text: Give ear to my words, Lord. Consider my meditation.

5890.text: Listen to the voice of my cry, my King and my God; for to you do I pray.

5891.text: Lord, in the morning you shall hear my voice. In the morning I will lay my requests before you, and will watch expectantly.

5892.text: For you are not a God who has pleasure in wickedness. Evil can't live with you.

5893.text: The arrogant shall not stand in your sight. You hate all workers of iniquity.

5894.text: You will destroy those who speak lies. The Lord abhors the bloodthirsty and deceitful man.

5895.text: But as for me, in the abundance of your loving kindness I will come into your house. I will bow toward your holy temple in reverence of you.

5896.text: Lead me, Lord, in your righteousness because of my enemies. Make your way straight before my face.

5897.text: For there is no faithfulness in their mouth. Their heart is destruction. Their throat is an open tomb; with their tongue they are deceitful.

5898.text: Hold them guilty, God. Let them fall by their own counsels; Thrust them out in the multitude of their transgressions, for they have rebelled against you.

5899.text: But let all those who take refuge in you rejoice, Let them always shout for joy, because you defend them. Let them also who love your name be joyful in you.

5900.text: For you will bless the righteous. Lord, you will surround him with favor as with a shield.

5901.text: Lord, do not rebuke me in your anger, neither discipline me in your wrath.

5902.text: Have mercy on me, Lord, for I am faint. Lord, heal me, for my bones are troubled.

5903.text: My soul is also in great anguish. But you, Lord-how long?

5904.text: Return, Lord. Deliver my soul, and save me for your loving kindness' sake.

5905.text: For in death there is no memory of you. In Sheol, who shall give you thanks?

5906.text: I am weary with my groaning. Every night I flood my bed. I drench my couch with my tears.

5907.text: My eye wastes away because of grief. It grows old because of all my adversaries.

5908.text: Depart from me, all you workers of iniquity, for the Lord has heard the voice of my weeping.

5909.text: The Lord has heard my supplication. The Lord accepts my prayer.

5910.text: May all my enemies be ashamed and dismayed. They shall turn back, they shall be disgraced suddenly.

5911.text: Lord, my God, I take refuge in you. Save me from all those who pursue me, and deliver me,

5912.text: lest they tear apart my soul like a lion, ripping it in pieces, while there is none to deliver.

5913.text: Lord, my God, if I have done this, if there is iniquity in my hands,

5914.text: if I have rewarded evil to him who was at peace with me (yes, if I have delivered him who without cause was my adversary),

5915.text: let the enemy pursue my soul, and overtake it; yes, let him tread my life down to the earth, and lay my glory in the dust. Selah.

5916.text: Arise, Lord, in your anger. Lift up yourself against the rage of my adversaries. Awake for me. You have commanded judgment.

5917.text: Let the congregation of the peoples surround you. Rule over them on high.

5918.text: The Lord administers judgment to the peoples. Judge me, Lord, according to my righteousness, and to my integrity that is in me.

5919.text: Oh let the wickedness of the wicked come to an end, but establish the righteous; their minds and hearts are searched by the righteous God.

5920.text: My shield is with God, who saves the upright in heart.

5921.text: God is a righteous judge, yes, a God who has indignation every day.

5922.text: If a man doesn't relent, he will sharpen his sword; he has bent and strung his bow.

5923.text: He has also prepared for himself the instruments of death. He makes ready his flaming arrows.

5924.text: Behold, he travails with iniquity. Yes, he has conceived mischief, and brought forth falsehood.

5925.text: He has dug a hole, and has fallen into the pit which he made.

5926.text: The trouble he causes shall return to his own head. His violence shall come down on the crown of his own head.

5927.text: I will give thanks to the Lord according to his righteousness, and will sing praise to the name of the Lord Most High.

5928.text: Lord, our Lord, how majestic is your name in all the earth, who has set your glory above the heavens!

5929.text: From the lips of babes and infants you have ordained praise, because of your adversaries, that you might silence the enemy and the avenger.

5930.text: When I consider your heavens, the work of your fingers, the moon and the stars, which you have ordained;

5931.text: what is man, that you think of him? What is the son of man, that you care for him?

5932.text: For you have made him a little lower than the angels, and crowned him with glory and honor.

5933.text: You make him ruler over the works of your hands. You have put all things under his feet:

5934.text: All sheep and cattle, yes, and the animals of the field,

5935.text: The birds of the sky, the fish of the sea, and whatever passes through the paths of the seas.

5936.text: Lord, our Lord, how majestic is your name in all the earth!

5937.text: ALEPH I will give thanks to the Lord with my whole heart. I will tell of all your marvelous works.

5938.text: I will be glad and rejoice in you. I will sing praise to your name, O Most High.

5939.text: When my enemies turn back, they stumble and perish in your presence.

5940.text: For you have maintained my just cause. You sit on the throne judging righteously.

5941.text: You have rebuked the nations. You have destroyed the wicked. You have blotted out their name forever and ever.

5942.text: The enemy is overtaken by endless ruin. The very memory of the cities which you have overthrown has perished.

5943.text: But the Lord reigns forever. He has prepared his throne for judgment.

5944.text: He will judge the world in righteousness. He will administer judgment to the peoples in uprightness.

5945.text: The Lord will also be a high tower for the oppressed; a high tower in times of trouble.

5946.text: Those who know your name will put their trust in you, for you, Lord, have not forsaken those who seek you.

5947.text: Sing praises to the Lord, who dwells in Zion, and declare among the people what he has done.

5948.text: For he who avenges blood remembers them. He doesn't forget the cry of the afflicted.

5949.text: Have mercy on me, Lord. See my affliction by those who hate me, and lift me up from the gates of death;

5950.text: that I may show forth all your praise. In the gates of the daughter of Zion, I will rejoice in your salvation.

5951.text: The nations have sunk down in the pit that they made. In the net which they hid, their own foot is taken.

5952.text: The Lord has made himself known. He has executed judgment. The wicked is snared by the work of his own hands. Meditation. Selah.

5953.text: The wicked shall be turned back to Sheol, even all the nations that forget God.

5954.text: For the needy shall not always be forgotten, nor the hope of the poor perish forever.

5955.text: Arise, Lord! Do not let man prevail. Let the nations be judged in your sight.

5956.text: Put them in fear, Lord. Let the nations know that they are only men. Selah.

5957.text: Why do you stand far off, Lord? Why do you hide yourself in times of trouble?

5958.text: In arrogance, the wicked hunt down the weak. They are caught in the schemes that they devise.

5959.text: For the wicked boasts of his heart's cravings. He blesses the greedy, and condemns the Lord.

5960.text: The wicked, in the pride of his face, has no room in his thoughts for God.

5961.text: His ways are prosperous at all times. Your judgments are far from his sight. As for all his adversaries, he sneers at them.

5962.text: He says in his heart, "I shall not be shaken. For generations I shall have no trouble."

5963.text: His mouth is full of cursing, deceit, and oppression. Under his tongue is mischief and iniquity.

5964.text: He lies in wait near the villages. From ambushes, he murders the innocent. His eyes are secretly set against the helpless.

5965.text: He lurks in secret as a lion in his ambush. He lies in wait to catch the helpless. He catches the helpless, when he draws him in his net.

5966.text: The helpless are crushed. They collapse. They fall under his strength.

5967.text: He says in his heart, "God has forgotten. He hides his face. He will never see it."

5968.text: Arise, Lord! God, lift up your hand! Do not forget the helpless.

5969.text: Why does the wicked person condemn God, and say in his heart, "God won't call me into account?"

5970.text: But you do see trouble and grief. You consider it to take it into your hand. You help the victim and the fatherless.

5971.text: Break the arm of the wicked. As for the evil man, seek out his wickedness until you find none.

5972.text: The Lord is King forever and ever! The nations will perish out of his land.

5973.text: Lord, you have heard the desire of the humble. You will prepare their heart. You will cause your ear to hear,

5974.text: to judge the fatherless and the oppressed, that man who is of the earth may terrify no more.

5975.text: In the Lord, I take refuge. How can you say to my soul, "Flee as a bird to your mountain!"

5976.text: For, behold, the wicked bend their bows. They set their arrows on the strings, that they may shoot in darkness at the upright in heart.

5977.text: If the foundations are destroyed, what can the righteous do?

5978.text: The Lord is in his holy temple. The Lord is on his throne in heaven. His eyes observe. His eyes examine the children of men.

5979.text: The Lord examines the righteous, but the wicked and him who loves violence his soul hates.

5980.text: On the wicked he will rain blazing coals; fire, sulfur, and scorching wind shall be the portion of their cup.

5981.text: For the Lord is righteous. He loves righteousness. The upright shall see his face.

5982.text: Help, Lord; for the godly man ceases. For the faithful fail from among the children of men.

5983.text: Everyone lies to his neighbor. They speak with flattering lips, and with a double heart.

5984.text: May the Lord cut off all flattering lips, and the tongue that boasts,

5985.text: who have said, "With our tongue we will prevail. Our lips are our own. Who is lord over us?"

5986.text: "Because of the oppression of the weak and because of the groaning of the needy, I will now arise," says the Lord; "I will set him in safety from those who malign him."

5987.text: The words of the Lord are flawless words, as silver refined in a clay furnace, purified seven times.

5988.text: You will keep them, Lord. You will preserve them from this generation forever.

5989.text: The wicked walk on every side, when what is vile is exalted among the sons of men.

5990.text: How long, Lord? Will you forget me forever? How long will you hide your face from me?

5991.text: How long shall I take counsel in my soul, having sorrow in my heart every day? How long shall my enemy triumph over me?

5992.text: Behold, and answer me, Lord, my God. Give light to my eyes, lest I sleep in death;

5993.text: Lest my enemy say, "I have prevailed against him;" Lest my adversaries rejoice when I fall.

5994.text: But I trust in your loving kindness. My heart rejoices in your salvation.

5995.text: I will sing to the Lord, because he has been good to me.

5996.text: The fool has said in his heart, "There is no God." They are corrupt. They have done abominable works. There is none who does good.

5997.text: The Lord looked down from heaven on the children of men, to see if there were any who did understand, who did seek after God.

5998.text: They have all gone aside. They have together become corrupt. There is none who does good, no, not one.

5999.text: Have all the workers of iniquity no knowledge, who eat up my people as they eat bread, and do not call on the Lord?

6000.text: There they were in great fear, for God is in the generation of the righteous.

6001.text: You would frustrate the plans of the lowly, but the Lord is his refuge.

6002.text: Oh that the salvation of Israel would come out of Zion! When the Lord restores the fortunes of his people, then Jacob shall rejoice, and Israel shall be glad.

6003.text: Lord, who shall dwell in your sanctuary? Who shall live on your holy hill?

6004.text: He who walks blamelessly does what is right, and speaks truth in his heart;

6005.text: He who doesn't slander with his tongue, nor does evil to his friend, nor casts slurs against his fellow man;

6006.text: In whose eyes a vile man is despised, but who honors those who fear the Lord; he who keeps an oath even when it hurts, and doesn't change;

6007.text: he who doesn't lend out his money for usury, nor take a bribe against the innocent. He who does these things shall never be shaken.

6008.text: Preserve me, God, for in you do I take refuge.

6009.text: My soul, you have said to the Lord, "You are my Lord. Apart from you I have no good thing."

6010.text: As for the holy ones who are in the land, they are the excellent ones in whom is all my delight.

6011.text: Their sorrows shall be multiplied who give gifts to another god. Their drink offerings of blood I will not offer, nor take their names on my lips.

6012.text: The Lord assigned my portion and my cup. You made my lot secure.

6013.text: The lines have fallen to me in pleasant places. Yes, I have a good inheritance.

6014.text: I will bless the Lord, who has given me counsel. Yes, my heart instructs me in the night seasons.

6015.text: I have set the Lord always before me. Because he is at my right hand, I shall not be moved.

6016.text: Therefore my heart is glad, and my glory rejoices. My body shall also dwell in safety.

6017.text: For you will not leave my soul in Sheol, neither will you allow your holy one to see corruption.

6018.text: You will show me the path of life. In your presence is fullness of joy. In your right hand there are pleasures forevermore.

6019.text: Hear, Lord, my righteous plea; Give ear to my prayer, that doesn't go out of deceitful lips.

6020.text: Let my sentence come forth from your presence. Let your eyes look on equity.

6021.text: You have proved my heart. You have visited me in the night. You have tried me, and found nothing. I have resolved that my mouth shall not disobey.

6022.text: As for the works of men, by the word of your lips, I have kept myself from the ways of the violent.

6023.text: My steps have held fast to your paths. My feet have not slipped.

6024.text: I have called on you, for you will answer me, God. Turn your ear to me. Hear my speech.

6025.text: Show your marvelous loving kindness, you who save those who take refuge by your right hand from their enemies.

6026.text: Keep me as the apple of your eye. Hide me under the shadow of your wings,

6027.text: from the wicked who oppress me, my deadly enemies, who surround me.

6028.text: They close up their callous hearts. With their mouth they speak proudly.

6029.text: They have now surrounded us in our steps. They set their eyes to cast us down to the earth.

6030.text: He is like a lion that is greedy of his prey, as it were a young lion lurking in secret places.

6031.text: Arise, Lord, confront him. Cast him down. Deliver my soul from the wicked by your sword;

6032.text: from men by your hand, Lord, from men of the world, whose portion is in this life. You fill the belly of your cherished ones. Your sons have plenty, and they store up wealth for their children.

6033.text: As for me, I shall see your face in righteousness. I shall be satisfied, when I awake, with seeing your form.

6034.text: I love you, Lord, my strength.

6035.text: The Lord is my rock, my fortress, and my deliverer; my God, my rock, in whom I take refuge; my shield, and the horn of my salvation, my high tower.

6036.text: I call on the Lord, who is worthy to be praised; and I am saved from my enemies.

6037.text: The cords of death surrounded me. The floods of ungodliness made me afraid.

6038.text: The cords of Sheol were around me. The snares of death came on me.

6039.text: In my distress I called on the Lord, and cried to my God. He heard my voice out of his temple. My cry before him came into his ears.

6040.text: Then the earth shook and trembled. The foundations also of the mountains quaked and were shaken, because he was angry.

6041.text: Smoke went out of his nostrils. Consuming fire came out of his mouth. Coals were kindled by it.

6042.text: He bowed the heavens also, and came down. Thick darkness was under his feet.

6043.text: He rode on a cherub, and flew. Yes, he soared on the wings of the wind.

6044.text: He made darkness his hiding place, his pavilion around him, darkness of waters, thick clouds of the skies.

6045.text: At the brightness before him his thick clouds passed, hailstones and coals of fire.

6046.text: The Lord also thundered in the sky. The Most High uttered his voice: hailstones and coals of fire.

6047.text: He sent out his arrows, and scattered them; Yes, great lightning bolts, and routed them.

6048.text: Then the channels of waters appeared. The foundations of the world were laid bare at your rebuke, Lord, at the blast of the breath of your nostrils.

6049.text: He sent from on high. He took me. He drew me out of many waters.

6050.text: He delivered me from my strong enemy, from those who hated me; for they were too mighty for me.

6051.text: They came on me in the day of my calamity, but the Lord was my support.

6052.text: He brought me forth also into a large place. He delivered me, because he delighted in me.

6053.text: The Lord has rewarded me according to my righteousness. According to the cleanness of my hands has he recompensed me.

6054.text: For I have kept the ways of the Lord, and have not wickedly departed from my God.

6055.text: For all his ordinances were before me. I did not put away his statutes from me.

6056.text: I was also blameless with him. I kept myself from my iniquity.

6057.text: Therefore the Lord has rewarded me according to my righteousness, according to the cleanness of my hands in his eyesight.

6058.text: With the merciful you will show yourself merciful. With the perfect man, you will show yourself perfect.

6059.text: With the pure, you will show yourself pure. With the crooked you will show yourself shrewd.

6060.text: For you will save the afflicted people, but the haughty eyes you will bring down.

6061.text: For you will light my lamp, Lord. My God will light up my darkness.

6062.text: For by you, I advance through a troop. By my God, I leap over a wall.

6063.text: As for God, his way is perfect. The word of the Lord is tried. He is a shield to all those who take refuge in him.

6064.text: For who is God, except the Lord? Who is a rock, besides our God,

6065.text: the God who arms me with strength, and makes my way perfect?

6066.text: He makes my feet like deer's feet, and sets me on my high places.

6067.text: He teaches my hands to war, so that my arms bend a bow of bronze.

6068.text: You have also given me the shield of your salvation. Your right hand sustains me. Your gentleness has made me great.

6069.text: You have enlarged my steps under me, My feet have not slipped.

6070.text: I will pursue my enemies, and overtake them. Neither will I turn again until they are consumed.

6071.text: I will strike them through, so that they will not be able to rise. They shall fall under my feet.

6072.text: For you have girded me with strength to the battle. You have subdued under me those who rose up against me.

6073.text: You have also made my enemies turn their backs to me, that I might cut off those who hate me.

6074.text: They cried, but there was none to save; even to the Lord, but he did not answer them.

6075.text: Then I beat them small as the dust before the wind. I cast them out as the mire of the streets.

6076.text: You have delivered me from the strivings of the people. You have made me the head of the nations. A people whom I have not known shall serve me.

6077.text: As soon as they hear of me they shall obey me. The foreigners shall submit themselves to me.

6078.text: The foreigners shall fade away, and shall come trembling out of their close places.

6079.text: The Lord lives; and blessed be my rock. Exalted be the God of my salvation,

6080.text: even the God who executes vengeance for me, and subdues peoples under me.

6081.text: He rescues me from my enemies. Yes, you lift me up above those who rise up against me. You deliver me from the violent man.

6082.text: Therefore I will give thanks to you, Lord, among the nations, and will sing praises to your name.

6083.text: He gives great deliverance to his king, and shows loving kindness to his anointed, to David and to his seed, forevermore.

6084.text: The heavens declare the glory of God. The expanse shows his handiwork.

6085.text: Day after day they pour forth speech, and night after night they display knowledge.

6086.text: There is no speech nor language, where their voice is not heard.

6087.text: Their voice has gone out through all the earth, their words to the end of the world. In them he has set a tent for the sun,

6088.text: which is as a bridegroom coming out of his chamber, like a strong man rejoicing to run his course.

6089.text: His going forth is from the end of the heavens, his circuit to its ends; There is nothing hidden from its heat.

6090.text: The Lord's Law is perfect, restoring the soul. The Lord's testimony is sure, making wise the simple.

6091.text: The Lord's precepts are right, rejoicing the heart. The Lord's commandment is pure, enlightening the eyes.

6092.text: The fear of the Lord is clean, enduring forever. The Lord's ordinances are true, and righteous altogether.

6093.text: More to be desired are they than gold, yes, than much fine gold; sweeter also than honey and the extract of the honeycomb.

6094.text: Moreover by them is your servant warned. In keeping them there is great reward.

6095.text: Who can discern his errors? Forgive me from hidden errors.

6096.text: Keep back your servant also from presumptuous sins. Let them not have dominion over me. Then I will be upright. I will be blameless and innocent of great transgression.

6097.text: Let the words of my mouth and the meditation of my heart be acceptable in your sight, Lord, my rock, and my redeemer.

6098.text: May the Lord answer you in the day of trouble. May the name of the God of Jacob set you up on high,

6099.text: send you help from the sanctuary, grant you support from Zion,

6100.text: remember all your offerings, and accept your burnt sacrifice. Selah.

6101.text: May He grant you your heart's desire, and fulfill all your counsel.

6102.text: We will triumph in your salvation. In the name of our God, we will set up our banners. May the Lord grant all your requests.

6103.text: Now I know that the Lord saves his anointed. He will answer him from his holy heaven, with the saving strength of his right hand.

6104.text: Some trust in chariots, and some in horses, but we trust the name of the Lord our God.

6105.text: They are bowed down and fallen, but we rise up, and stand upright.

6106.text: Save, Lord! Let the King answer us when we call!

6107.text: The king rejoices in your strength, Lord! How greatly he rejoices in your salvation!

6108.text: You have given him his heart's desire, and have not withheld the request of his lips. Selah.

6109.text: For you meet him with the blessings of goodness. You set a crown of fine gold on his head.

6110.text: He asked life of you, you gave it to him, even length of days forever and ever.

6111.text: His glory is great in your salvation. You lay honor and majesty on him.

6112.text: For you make him most blessed forever. You make him glad with joy in your presence.

6113.text: For the king trusts in the Lord. Through the loving kindness of the Most High, he shall not be moved.

6114.text: Your hand will find out all of your enemies. Your right hand will find out those who hate you.

6115.text: You will make them as a fiery furnace in the time of your anger. The Lord will swallow them up in his wrath. The fire shall devour them.

6116.text: You will destroy their descendants from the earth, their posterity from among the children of men.

6117.text: For they intended evil against you. They plotted evil against you which cannot succeed.

6118.text: For you will make them turn their back, when you aim drawn bows at their face.

6119.text: Be exalted, Lord, in your strength, so we will sing and praise your power.

6120.text: My God, my God, why have you forsaken me? Why are you so far from helping me, and from the words of my groaning?

6121.text: My God, I cry in the daytime, but you do not answer; in the night season, and am not silent.

6122.text: But you are holy, you who inhabit the praises of Israel.

6123.text: Our fathers trusted in you. They trusted, and you delivered them.

6124.text: They cried to you, and were delivered. They trusted in you, and were not disappointed.

6125.text: But I am a worm, and no man; a reproach of men, and despised by the people.

6126.text: All those who see me mock me. They insult me with their lips. They shake their heads, saying,

6127.text: "He trusts in the Lord; let him deliver him. Let him rescue him, since he delights in him."

6128.text: But you brought me out of the womb. You made me trust at my mother's breasts.

6129.text: I was thrown on you from my mother's womb. You are my God since my mother bore me.

6130.text: Do not be far from me, for trouble is near. For there is none to help.

6131.text: Many bulls have surrounded me. Strong bulls of Bashan have encircled me.

6132.text: They open their mouths wide against me, lions tearing prey and roaring.

6133.text: I am poured out like water. All my bones are out of joint. My heart is like wax; it is melted within me.

6134.text: My strength is dried up like a potsherd. My tongue sticks to the roof of my mouth. You have brought me into the dust of death.

6135.text: For dogs have surrounded me. A company of evildoers have enclosed me. They have pierced my hands and feet.

6136.text: I can count all of my bones. They look and stare at me.

6137.text: They divide my garments among them. They cast lots for my clothing.

6138.text: But do not be far off, Lord. You are my help: hurry to help me.

6139.text: Deliver my soul from the sword, my precious life from the power of the dog.

6140.text: Save me from the lion's mouth! Yes, from the horns of the wild oxen, you have answered me.

6141.text: I will declare your name to my brothers. In the midst of the assembly, I will praise you.

6142.text: You who fear the Lord, praise him! All you descendants of Jacob, glorify him! Stand in awe of him, all you descendants of Israel!

6143.text: For he has not despised nor abhorred the affliction of the afflicted, Neither has he hidden his face from him; but when he cried to him, he heard.

6144.text: Of you comes my praise in the great assembly. I will pay my vows before those who fear him.

6145.text: The humble shall eat and be satisfied. They shall praise the Lord who seek after him. Let your hearts live forever.

6146.text: All the ends of the earth shall remember and turn to the Lord. All the relatives of the nations shall worship before you.

6147.text: For the kingdom is the Lord's. He is the ruler over the nations.

6148.text: All the rich ones of the earth shall eat and worship. All those who go down to the dust shall bow before him, even he who can't keep his soul alive.

6149.text: Posterity shall serve him. Future generations shall be told about the Lord.

6150.text: They shall come and shall declare his righteousness to a people that shall be born, for he has done it.

6151.text: The Lord is my shepherd: I shall lack nothing.

6152.text: He makes me lie down in green pastures. He leads me beside still waters.

6153.text: He restores my soul. He guides me in the paths of righteousness for his name's sake.

6154.text: Even though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil, for you are with me. Your rod and your staff, they comfort me.

6155.text: You prepare a table before me in the presence of my enemies. You anoint my head with oil. My cup runs over.

6156.text: Surely goodness and loving kindness shall follow me all the days of my life, and I will dwell in the Lord's house forever.

6157.text: The earth is the Lord's, with its fullness; the world, and those who dwell therein.

6158.text: For he has founded it on the seas, and established it on the floods.

6159.text: Who may ascend to the Lord's hill? Who may stand in his holy place?

6160.text: He who has clean hands and a pure heart; who has not lifted up his soul to falsehood, and has not sworn deceitfully.

6161.text: He shall receive a blessing from the Lord, righteousness from the God of his salvation.

6162.text: This is the generation of those who seek Him, who seek your face-even Jacob. Selah.

6163.text: Lift up your heads, you gates! Be lifted up, you everlasting doors, and the King of glory will come in.

6164.text: Who is the King of glory? The Lord strong and mighty, The Lord mighty in battle.

6165.text: Lift up your heads, you gates; lift them up, you everlasting doors, and the King of glory will come in.

6166.text: Who is this King of glory? The Lord of hosts is the King of glory! Selah.

6167.text: ALEPH To you, Lord, do I lift up my soul.

6168.text: My God, I have trusted in you. Do not let me be shamed. Do not let my enemies triumph over me.

6169.text: Yes, no one who waits for you shall be shamed. They shall be shamed who deal treacherously without cause.

6170.text: Show me your ways, Lord. Teach me your paths.

6171.text: Guide me in your truth, and teach me, For you are the God of my salvation, I wait for you all day long.

6172.text: Lord, remember your tender mercies and your loving kindness, for they are from old times.

6173.text: Do not remember the sins of my youth, nor my transgressions. Remember me according to your loving kindness, for your goodness' sake, Lord.

6174.text: Good and upright is the Lord, therefore he will instruct sinners in the way.

6175.text: He will guide the humble in justice. He will teach the humble his way.

6176.text: All the paths of the Lord are loving kindness and truth to such as keep his covenant and his testimonies.

6177.text: For your name's sake, Lord, pardon my iniquity, for it is great.

6178.text: What man is he who fears the Lord? He shall instruct him in the way that he shall choose.

6179.text: His soul shall dwell at ease. His seed shall inherit the land.

6180.text: The friendship of the Lord is with those who fear him. He will show them his covenant.

6181.text: My eyes are ever on the Lord, for he will pluck my feet out of the net.

6182.text: Turn to me, and have mercy on me, for I am desolate and afflicted.

6183.text: The troubles of my heart are enlarged. Oh bring me out of my distresses.

6184.text: Consider my affliction and my travail. Forgive all my sins.

6185.text: Consider my enemies, for they are many. They hate me with cruel hatred.

6186.text: Oh keep my soul, and deliver me. Let me not be disappointed, for I take refuge in you.

6187.text: Let integrity and uprightness preserve me, for I wait for you.

6188.text: Redeem Israel, God, from all of his troubles.

6189.text: Judge me, Lord, for I have walked in my integrity. I have trusted also in Lord without wavering.

6190.text: Examine me, Lord, and prove me. Try my heart and my mind.

6191.text: For your loving kindness is before my eyes. I have walked in your truth.

6192.text: I have not sat with deceitful men, neither will I go in with hypocrites.

6193.text: I hate the assembly of evildoers, and will not sit with the wicked.

6194.text: I will wash my hands in innocence, so I will go about your altar, Lord;

6195.text: that I may make the voice of thanksgiving to be heard, and tell of all your wondrous works.

6196.text: Lord, I love the habitation of your house, the place where your glory dwells.

6197.text: Do not gather my soul with sinners, nor my life with bloodthirsty men;

6198.text: in whose hands is wickedness, their right hand is full of bribes.

6199.text: But as for me, I will walk in my integrity. Redeem me, and be merciful to me.

6200.text: My foot stands in an even place. In the congregations I will bless the Lord.

6201.text: The Lord is my light and my salvation. Whom shall I fear? The Lord is the strength of my life. Of whom shall I be afraid?

6202.text: When evildoers came at me to eat up my flesh, even my adversaries and my foes, they stumbled and fell.

6203.text: Though an army should encamp against me, my heart shall not fear. Though war should rise against me, even then I will be confident.

6204.text: One thing I have asked of the Lord, that I will seek after, that I may dwell in the house of the Lord all the days of my life, to see the Lord's beauty, and to inquire in his temple.

6205.text: For in the day of trouble he will keep me secretly in his pavilion. In the covert of his tabernacle he will hide me. He will lift me up on a rock.

6206.text: Now my head will be lifted up above my enemies around me. I will offer sacrifices of joy in his tent. I will sing, yes, I will sing praises to the Lord.

6207.text: Hear, Lord, when I cry with my voice. Have mercy also on me, and answer me.

6208.text: When you said, "Seek my face," my heart said to you, "I will seek your face, Lord."

6209.text: Do not hide your face from me. Do not put your servant away in anger. You have been my help. Do not abandon me, neither forsake me, God of my salvation.

6210.text: When my father and my mother forsake me, then the Lord will take me up.

6211.text: Teach me your way, Lord. Lead me in a straight path, because of my enemies.

6212.text: Do not deliver me over to the desire of my adversaries, for false witnesses have risen up against me, such as breathe out cruelty.

6213.text: I am still confident of this: I will see the goodness of the Lord in the land of the living.

6214.text: Wait for the Lord. Be strong, and let your heart take courage. Yes, wait for the Lord.

6215.text: To you, Lord, I call. My rock, do not be deaf to me; lest, if you are silent to me, I would become like those who go down into the pit.

6216.text: Hear the voice of my petitions, when I cry to you, when I lift up my hands toward your Most Holy Place.

6217.text: Do not draw me away with the wicked, with the workers of iniquity who speak peace with their neighbors, but mischief is in their hearts.

6218.text: Give them according to their work, and according to the wickedness of their doings. Give them according to the operation of their hands. Bring back on them what they deserve.

6219.text: Because they do not regard the works of the Lord, nor the operation of his hands, he will break them down and not build them up.

6220.text: Blessed be the Lord, because he has heard the voice of my petitions.

6221.text: The Lord is my strength and my shield. My heart has trusted in him, and I am helped. Therefore my heart greatly rejoices. With my song I will thank him.

6222.text: The Lord is their strength. He is a stronghold of salvation to his anointed.

6223.text: Save your people, and bless your inheritance. Be their shepherd also, and bear them up forever.

6224.text: Ascribe to the Lord, you sons of the mighty, ascribe to the Lord glory and strength.

6225.text: Ascribe to the Lord the glory due to his name. Worship the Lord in holy array.

6226.text: The Lord's voice is on the waters. The God of glory thunders, even the Lord on many waters.

6227.text: The Lord's voice is powerful. The Lord's voice is full of majesty.

6228.text: The voice of the Lord breaks the cedars. Yes, the Lord breaks in pieces the cedars of Lebanon.

6229.text: He makes them also to skip like a calf; Lebanon and Sirion like a young, wild ox.

6230.text: The Lord's voice strikes with flashes of lightning.

6231.text: The Lord's voice shakes the wilderness. The Lord shakes the wilderness of Kadesh.

6232.text: The Lord's voice makes the deer calve, and strips the forests bare. In his temple everything says, "Glory!"

6233.text: The Lord sat enthroned at the Flood. Yes, the Lord sits as King forever.

6234.text: The Lord will give strength to his people. The Lord will bless his people with peace.

6235.text: I will extol you, Lord, for you have raised me up, and have not made my foes to rejoice over me.

6236.text: Lord my God, I cried to you, and you have healed me.
