7834.text: You have rebuked the proud who are cursed, who wander from your commandments.

7835.text: Take reproach and contempt away from me, for I have kept your statutes.

7836.text: Though princes sit and slander me, your servant will meditate on your statutes.

7837.text: Indeed your statutes are my delight, and my counselors.

7838.text: My soul is laid low in the dust. Revive me according to your word!

7839.text: I declared my ways, and you answered me. Teach me your statutes.

7840.text: Let me understand the teaching of your precepts! Then I will meditate on your wondrous works.

7841.text: My soul is weary with sorrow: strengthen me according to your word.

7842.text: Keep me from the way of deceit. Grant me your Law graciously!

7843.text: I have chosen the way of truth. I have set your ordinances before me.

7844.text: I cling to your statutes, Lord. Do not let me be disappointed.

7845.text: I run in the path of your commandments, for you have set my heart free.

7846.text: Teach me, Lord, the way of your statutes. I will keep them to the end.

7847.text: Give me understanding, and I will keep your Law. Yes, I will obey it with my whole heart.

7848.text: Direct me in the path of your commandments, for I delight in them.

7849.text: Turn my heart toward your statutes, not toward selfish gain.

7850.text: Turn my eyes away from looking at worthless things. Revive me in your ways.

7851.text: Fulfill your promise to your servant, that you may be feared.

7852.text: Take away my disgrace that I dread, for your ordinances are good.

7853.text: Behold, I long for your precepts! Revive me in your righteousness.

7854.text: Let your loving kindness also come to me, Lord, your salvation, according to your word.

7855.text: So I will have an answer for him who reproaches me, for I trust in your word.

7856.text: Do not snatch the word of truth out of my mouth, for I put my hope in your ordinances.

7857.text: So I will obey your Law continually, forever and ever.

7858.text: I will walk in liberty, for I have sought your precepts.

7859.text: I will also speak of your statutes before kings, and will not be disappointed.

7860.text: I will delight myself in your commandments, because I love them.

7861.text: I reach out my hands for your commandments, which I love. I will meditate on your statutes.

7862.text: Remember your word to your servant, because you gave me hope.

7863.text: This is my comfort in my affliction, for your word has revived me.

7864.text: The arrogant mock me excessively, but I do not swerve from your Law.

7865.text: I remember your ordinances of old, Lord, and have comforted myself.

7866.text: Indignation has taken hold on me, because of the wicked who forsake your Law.

7867.text: Your statutes have been my songs, in the house where I live.

7868.text: I have remembered your name, Lord, in the night, and I obey your Law.

7869.text: This is my way, that I keep your precepts.

7870.text: The Lord is my portion. I promised to obey your words.

7871.text: I sought your favor with my whole heart. Be merciful to me according to your word.

7872.text: I considered my ways, and turned my steps to your statutes.

7873.text: I will hurry, and not delay, to obey your commandments.

7874.text: The ropes of the wicked bind me, but I won't forget your Law.

7875.text: At midnight I will rise to give thanks to you, because of your righteous ordinances.

7876.text: I am a friend of all those who fear you, of those who observe your precepts.

7877.text: The earth is full of your loving kindness, Lord. Teach me your statutes.

7878.text: Do good to your servant, according to your word, Lord.

7879.text: Teach me good judgment and knowledge, for I believe in your commandments.

7880.text: Before I was afflicted, I went astray; but now I observe your word.

7881.text: You are good, and do good. Teach me your statutes.

7882.text: The proud have smeared a lie upon me. With my whole heart, I will keep your precepts.

7883.text: Their heart is as callous as the fat, but I delight in your Law.

7884.text: It is good for me that I have been afflicted, that I may learn your statutes.

7885.text: The Law you have spoken is better to me than thousands of pieces of gold and silver.

7886.text: Your hands have made me and formed me. Give me understanding, that I may learn your commandments.

7887.text: Those who fear you will see me and be glad, because I have put my hope in your word.

7888.text: Lord, I know that your judgments are righteous, that in faithfulness you have humbled me.

7889.text: Please let your loving kindness be for my comfort, according to your word to your servant.

7890.text: Let your tender mercies come to me, that I may live; for your Law is my delight.

7891.text: Let the proud be disappointed, for they have overthrown me wrongfully. I will meditate on your precepts.

7892.text: Let those who fear you turn to me. They will know your statutes.

7893.text: Let my heart be blameless toward your decrees, that I may not be disappointed.

7894.text: My soul faints for your salvation. I hope in your word.

7895.text: My eyes fail for your word. I say, "When will you comfort me?"

7896.text: For I have become like a wineskin in the smoke. I do not forget your statutes.

7897.text: How many are the days of your servant? When will you execute judgment on those who persecute me?

7898.text: The proud have dug pits for me, contrary to your Law.

7899.text: All of your commandments are faithful. They persecute me wrongfully. Help me!

7900.text: They had almost wiped me from the earth, but I did not forsake your precepts.

7901.text: Preserve my life according to your loving kindness, so I will obey the statutes of your mouth.

7902.text: Lord, your word is settled in heaven forever.

7903.text: Your faithfulness is to all generations. You have established the earth, and it remains.

7904.text: Your laws remain to this day, for all things serve you.

7905.text: Unless your Law had been my delight, I would have perished in my affliction.

7906.text: I will never forget your precepts, for with them, you have revived me.

7907.text: I am yours. Save me, for I have sought your precepts.

7908.text: The wicked have waited for me, to destroy me. I will consider your statutes.

7909.text: I have seen a limit to all perfection, but your commands are boundless.

7910.text: How I love your Law! It is my meditation all day.

7911.text: Your commandments make me wiser than my enemies, for your commandments are always with me.

7912.text: I have more understanding than all my teachers, for your testimonies are my meditation.

7913.text: I understand more than the aged, because I have kept your precepts.

7914.text: I have kept my feet from every evil way, that I might observe your word.

7915.text: I have not turned aside from your ordinances, for you have taught me.

7916.text: How sweet are your promises to my taste, more than honey to my mouth!

7917.text: Through your precepts, I get understanding; therefore I hate every false way.

7918.text: Your word is a lamp to my feet, and a light for my path.

7919.text: I have sworn, and have confirmed it, that I will obey your righteous ordinances.

7920.text: I am afflicted very much. Revive me, Lord, according to your word.

7921.text: Accept, I beg you, the willing offerings of my mouth. Lord, teach me your ordinances.

7922.text: My soul is continually in my hand, yet I won't forget your Law.

7923.text: The wicked have laid a snare for me, yet I haven't gone astray from your precepts.

7924.text: I have taken your testimonies as a heritage forever, for they are the joy of my heart.

7925.text: I have set my heart to perform your statutes forever, even to the end.

7926.text: I hate double-minded men, but I love your Law.

7927.text: You are my hiding place and my shield. I hope in your word.

7928.text: Depart from me, you evildoers, that I may keep the commandments of my God.

7929.text: Uphold me according to your word, that I may live. Let me not be ashamed of my hope.

7930.text: Hold me up, and I will be safe, and will have respect for your statutes continually.

7931.text: You reject all those who stray from your statutes, for their deceit is in vain.

7932.text: You put away all the wicked of the earth like dross. Therefore I love your testimonies.

7933.text: My flesh trembles for fear of you. I am afraid of your judgments.

7934.text: I have done what is just and righteous. Do not leave me to my oppressors.

7935.text: Ensure your servant's well-being. Do not let the proud oppress me.

7936.text: My eyes fail looking for your salvation, for your righteous word.

7937.text: Deal with your servant according to your loving kindness. Teach me your statutes.

7938.text: I am your servant. Give me understanding, that I may know your testimonies.

7939.text: It is time to act, Lord, for they break your Law.

7940.text: Therefore I love your commandments more than gold, yes, more than pure gold.

7941.text: Therefore I consider all of your precepts to be right. I hate every false way.

7942.text: Your testimonies are wonderful, therefore my soul keeps them.

7943.text: The entrance of your words gives light. It gives understanding to the simple.

7944.text: I opened my mouth wide and panted, for I longed for your commandments.

7945.text: Turn to me, and have mercy on me, as you always do to those who love your name.

7946.text: Establish my footsteps in your word. Do not let any iniquity have dominion over me.

7947.text: Redeem me from the oppression of man, so I will observe your precepts.

7948.text: Make your face shine on your servant. Teach me your statutes.

7949.text: Streams of tears run down my eyes, because they do not observe your Law.

7950.text: You are righteous, Lord. Your judgments are upright.

7951.text: You have commanded your statutes in righteousness. They are fully trustworthy.

7952.text: My zeal wears me out, because my enemies ignore your words.

7953.text: Your promises have been thoroughly tested, and your servant loves them.

7954.text: I am small and despised. I do not forget your precepts.

7955.text: Your righteousness is an everlasting righteousness. Your Law is truth.

7956.text: Trouble and anguish have taken hold of me. Your commandments are my delight.

7957.text: Your testimonies are righteous forever. Give me understanding, that I may live.

7958.text: I have called with my whole heart. Answer me, Lord! I will keep your statutes.

7959.text: I have called to you. Save me! I will obey your statutes.

7960.text: I rise before dawn and cry for help. I put my hope in your words.

7961.text: My eyes stay open through the night watches, that I might meditate on your word.

7962.text: Hear my voice according to your loving kindness. Revive me, Lord, according to your ordinances.

7963.text: They draw near who follow after wickedness. They are far from your Law.

7964.text: You are near, Lord. All your commandments are truth.

7965.text: Of old I have known from your testimonies, that you have founded them forever.

7966.text: Consider my affliction, and deliver me, for I do not forget your Law.

7967.text: Plead my cause, and redeem me! Revive me according to your promise.

7968.text: Salvation is far from the wicked, for they do not seek your statutes.

7969.text: Great are your tender mercies, Lord. Revive me according to your ordinances.

7970.text: Many are my persecutors and my adversaries. I haven't swerved from your testimonies.

7971.text: I look at the faithless with loathing, because they do not observe your word.

7972.text: Consider how I love your precepts. Revive me, Lord, according to your loving kindness.

7973.text: All of your words are truth. Every one of your righteous ordinances endures forever.

7974.text: Princes have persecuted me without a cause, but my heart stands in awe of your words.

7975.text: I rejoice at your word, as one who finds great spoil.

7976.text: I hate and abhor falsehood. I love your Law.

7977.text: Seven times a day, I praise you, because of your righteous ordinances.

7978.text: Those who love your Law have great peace. Nothing causes them to stumble.

7979.text: I have hoped for your salvation, Lord. I have done your commandments.

7980.text: My soul has observed your testimonies. I love them exceedingly.

7981.text: I have obeyed your precepts and your testimonies, for all my ways are before you.

7982.text: Let my cry come before you, Lord. Give me understanding according to your word.

7983.text: Let my supplication come before you. Deliver me according to your word.

7984.text: Let my lips utter praise, for you teach me your statutes.

7985.text: Let my tongue sing of your word, for all your commandments are righteousness.

7986.text: Let your hand be ready to help me, for I have chosen your precepts.

7987.text: I have longed for your salvation, Lord. Your Law is my delight.

7988.text: Let my soul live, that I may praise you. Let your ordinances help me.

7989.text: I have gone astray like a lost sheep. Seek your servant, for I do not forget your commandments.

7990.text: In my distress, I cried to the Lord. He answered me.

7991.text: Deliver my soul, Lord, from lying lips, from a deceitful tongue.

7992.text: What will be given to you, and what will be done more to you, you deceitful tongue?

7993.text: Sharp arrows of the mighty, with coals of juniper.

7994.text: Woe is me, that I live in Meshech, that I dwell among the tents of Kedar!

7995.text: My soul has had her dwelling too long with him who hates peace.

7996.text: I am for peace, but when I speak, they are for war.

7997.text: I will lift up my eyes to the hills. Where does my help come from?

7998.text: My help comes from the Lord, who made heaven and earth.

7999.text: He will not allow your foot to be moved. He who keeps you will not slumber.

8000.text: Behold, he who keeps Israel will neither slumber nor sleep.

8001.text: The Lord is your keeper. The Lord is your shade on your right hand.

8002.text: The sun will not harm you by day, nor the moon by night.

8003.text: The Lord will keep you from all evil. He will keep your soul.

8004.text: The Lord will keep your going out and your coming in, from this time forth, and forevermore.

8005.text: I was glad when they said to me, "Let's go to the Lord's house!"

8006.text: Our feet are standing within your gates, Jerusalem;

8007.text: Jerusalem, that is built as a city that is compact together;

8008.text: where the tribes go up, even the tribes of Yah, according to an ordinance for Israel, to give thanks to the name of the Lord.

8009.text: For there are set thrones for judgment, the thrones of David's house.

8010.text: Pray for the peace of Jerusalem. Those who love you will prosper.

8011.text: Peace be within your walls, and prosperity within your palaces.

8012.text: For my brothers' and companions' sakes, I will now say, "Peace be within you."

8013.text: For the sake of the house of the Lord our God, I will seek your good.

8014.text: To you I do lift up my eyes, you who sit in the heavens.

8015.text: Behold, as the eyes of servants look to the hand of their master, as the eyes of a maid to the hand of her mistress; so our eyes look to the Lord, our God, until he has mercy on us.

8016.text: Have mercy on us, Lord, have mercy on us, for we have endured much contempt.

8017.text: Our soul is exceedingly filled with the scoffing of those who are at ease, with the contempt of the proud.

8018.text: If it had not been the Lord who was on our side, let Israel now say,

8019.text: if it had not been the Lord who was on our side, when men rose up against us;

8020.text: then they would have swallowed us up alive, when their wrath was kindled against us;

8021.text: then the waters would have overwhelmed us, the stream would have gone over our soul;

8022.text: then the proud waters would have gone over our soul.

8023.text: Blessed be the Lord, who has not given us as a prey to their teeth.

8024.text: Our soul has escaped like a bird out of the fowler's snare. The snare is broken, and we have escaped.

8025.text: Our help is in the name of the Lord, who made heaven and earth.

8026.text: Those who trust in the Lord are as Mount Zion, which can't be moved, but remains forever.

8027.text: As the mountains surround Jerusalem, so the Lord surrounds his people from this time forth and forevermore.

8028.text: For the scepter of wickedness won't remain over the allotment of the righteous; so that the righteous won't use their hands to do evil.

8029.text: Do good, Lord, to those who are good, to those who are upright in their hearts.

8030.text: But as for those who turn aside to their crooked ways, The Lord will lead them away with the workers of iniquity. Peace be on Israel.

8031.text: When the Lord brought back those who returned to Zion, we were like those who dream.

8032.text: Then our mouth was filled with laughter, and our tongue with singing. Then they said among the nations, "The Lord has done great things for them."

8033.text: The Lord has done great things for us, and we are glad.

8034.text: Restore our fortunes again, Lord, like the streams in the Negev.

8035.text: Those who sow in tears will reap in joy.

8036.text: He who goes out weeping, carrying seed for sowing, will certainly come again with joy, carrying his sheaves.

8037.text: Unless the Lord builds the house, they labor in vain who build it. Unless the Lord watches over the city, the watchman guards it in vain.

8038.text: It is vain for you to rise up early, to stay up late, eating the bread of toil; for he gives sleep to his loved ones.

8039.text: Behold, children are a heritage of the Lord. The fruit of the womb is his reward.

8040.text: As arrows in the hand of a mighty man, so are the children of youth.

8041.text: Happy is the man who has his quiver full of them. They won't be disappointed when they speak with their enemies in the gate.

8042.text: Blessed is everyone who fears the Lord, who walks in his ways.

8043.text: For you will eat the labor of your hands. You will be happy, and it will be well with you.

8044.text: Your wife will be as a fruitful vine, in the innermost parts of your house; your children like olive plants, around your table.

8045.text: Behold, thus is the man blessed who fears the Lord.

8046.text: May the Lord bless you out of Zion, and may you see the good of Jerusalem all the days of your life.

8047.text: Yes, may you see your children's children. Peace be upon Israel.

8048.text: Many times they have afflicted me from my youth up. Let Israel now say,

8050.text: The plowers plowed on my back. They made their furrows long.

8051.text: The Lord is righteous. He has cut apart the cords of the wicked.

8052.text: Let them be disappointed and turned backward, all those who hate Zion.

8058.text: If you, Yah, kept a record of sins, Lord, who could stand?

8059.text: But there is forgiveness with you, therefore you are feared.

8060.text: I wait for the Lord. My soul waits. I hope in his word.

8061.text: My soul longs for the Lord more than watchmen long for the morning; more than watchmen for the morning.

8062.text: Israel, hope in the Lord, for with the Lord there is loving kindness. With him is abundant redemption.

8063.text: He will redeem Israel from all their sins.

8065.text: Surely I have stilled and quieted my soul, like a weaned child with his mother, like a weaned child is my soul within me.

8066.text: Israel, hope in the Lord, from this time forth and forevermore.

8070.text: I will not give sleep to my eyes, or slumber to my eyelids;

8079.text: For the Lord has chosen Zion. He has desired it for his habitation.

8082.text: Her priests I will also clothe with salvation. Her holy ones will shout aloud for joy.

8117.text: To him who spread out the earth above the waters; for his loving kindness endures forever:

8138.text: By the rivers of Babylon, there we sat down. Yes, we wept, when we remembered Zion.

8139.text: On the willows in its midst, we hung up our harps.

8141.text: How can we sing the Lord's song in a foreign land?

8142.text: If I forget you, Jerusalem, let my right hand forget its skill.

8143.text: Let my tongue stick to the roof of my mouth if I do not remember you; if I do not prefer Jerusalem above my chief joy.

8144.text: Remember, Lord, against the children of Edom, the day of Jerusalem; who said, "Raze it! Raze it even to its foundation!"

8145.text: Daughter of Babylon, doomed to destruction, he will be happy who rewards you, as you have served us.

8146.text: Happy shall he be, who takes and dashes your little ones against the rock.

8147.text: I will give you thanks with my whole heart. Before the angels, I will sing praises to you.

8148.text: I will bow down toward your holy temple, and give thanks to your Name for your loving kindness and for your truth; for you have exalted your Name and your Word above all.

8149.text: In the day that I called, you answered me. You encouraged me with strength in my soul.

8150.text: All the kings of the earth will give you thanks, Lord, for they have heard the words of your mouth.

8151.text: Yes, they will sing of the ways of the Lord; for great is the Lord's glory.

8152.text: For though the Lord is high, yet he looks after the lowly; but the proud, he knows from afar.

8153.text: Though I walk in the midst of trouble, you will revive me. You will stretch forth your hand against the wrath of my enemies. Your right hand will save me.

8154.text: The Lord will fulfill that which concerns me; your loving kindness, Lord, endures forever. Do not forsake the works of your own hands.

8155.text: Lord, you have searched me, and you know me.

8156.text: You know my sitting down and my rising up. You perceive my thoughts from afar.

8157.text: You search out my path and my lying down, and are acquainted with all my ways.

8158.text: For there is not a word on my tongue, but, behold, Lord, you know it altogether.

8159.text: You hem me in behind and before. You laid your hand on me.

8160.text: This knowledge is beyond me. It's lofty. I can't attain it.

8161.text: Where could I go from your Spirit? Or where could I flee from your presence?

8162.text: If I ascend up into heaven, you are there. If I make my bed in Sheol, behold, you are there!

8163.text: If I take the wings of the dawn, and settle in the uttermost parts of the sea;

8164.text: Even there your hand will lead me, and your right hand will hold me.

8165.text: If I say, "Surely the darkness will overwhelm me; the light around me will be night;"

8166.text: even the darkness doesn't hide from you, but the night shines as the day. The darkness is like light to you.

8167.text: For you formed my inmost being. You knit me together in my mother's womb.

8168.text: I will give thanks to you, for I am fearfully and wonderfully made. Your works are wonderful. My soul knows that very well.

8169.text: My frame wasn't hidden from you, when I was made in secret, woven together in the depths of the earth.

8170.text: Your eyes saw my body. In your book they were all written, the days that were ordained for me, when as yet there were none of them.

8171.text: How precious to me are your thoughts, God! How vast is the sum of them!

8172.text: If I would count them, they are more in number than the sand. When I wake up, I am still with you.

8173.text: If only you, God, would kill the wicked. Get away from me, you bloodthirsty men!

8174.text: For they speak against you wickedly. Your enemies take your name in vain.

8175.text: Lord, do I not hate those who hate you? Am I not grieved with those who rise up against you?

8176.text: I hate them with perfect hatred. They have become my enemies.

8177.text: Search me, God, and know my heart. Try me, and know my thoughts.

8178.text: See if there is any wicked way in me, and lead me in the everlasting way.

8179.text: Deliver me, Lord, from the evil man. Preserve me from the violent man;

8180.text: those who devise mischief in their hearts. They continually gather themselves together for war.

8181.text: They have sharpened their tongues like a serpent. Viper's poison is under their lips. Selah.

8182.text: Lord, keep me from the hands of the wicked. Preserve me from the violent men who have determined to trip my feet.

8183.text: The proud have hidden a snare for me, they have spread the cords of a net by the path. They have set traps for me. Selah.

8184.text: I said to the Lord, "You are my God." Listen to the cry of my petitions, Lord.

8185.text: Lord, the Lord, the strength of my salvation, you have covered my head in the day of battle.

8186.text: Lord, do not grant the desires of the wicked. Do not let their evil plans succeed, or they will become proud. Selah.

8187.text: As for the head of those who surround me, let the mischief of their own lips cover them.

8188.text: Let burning coals fall on them. Let them be thrown into the fire, into miry pits, from where they never rise.

8189.text: An evil speaker won't be established in the earth. Evil will hunt the violent man to overthrow him.

8190.text: I know that the Lord will maintain the cause of the afflicted, and justice for the needy.

8191.text: Surely the righteous will give thanks to your name. The upright will dwell in your presence.

8192.text: Lord, I have called on you. Come to me quickly! Listen to my voice when I call to you.

8193.text: Let my prayer be set before you like incense; the lifting up of my hands like the evening sacrifice.

8194.text: Set a watch, Lord, before my mouth. Keep the door of my lips.

8195.text: Do not incline my heart to any evil thing, to practice deeds of wickedness with men who work iniquity. Do not let me eat of their delicacies.

8196.text: Let the righteous strike me, it is kindness; let him reprove me, it is like oil on the head; do not let my head refuse it; Yet my prayer is always against evil deeds.

8197.text: Their judges are thrown down by the sides of the rock. They will hear my words, for they are well spoken.

8198.text: "As when one plows and breaks up the earth, our bones are scattered at the mouth of Sheol."

8199.text: For my eyes are on you, Lord, the Lord. In you, I take refuge. Do not leave my soul destitute.

8200.text: Keep me from the snare which they have laid for me, from the traps of the workers of iniquity.

8201.text: Let the wicked fall together into their own nets, while I pass by.

8202.text: I cry with my voice to the Lord. With my voice, I ask the Lord for mercy.

8203.text: I pour out my complaint before him. I tell him my troubles.

8204.text: When my spirit was overwhelmed within me, you knew my path. In the way in which I walk, they have hidden a snare for me.

8205.text: Look on my right, and see; for there is no one who is concerned for me. Refuge has fled from me. No one cares for my soul.

8206.text: I cried to you, Lord. I said, "You are my refuge, my portion in the land of the living."

8207.text: Listen to my cry, for I am in desperate need. Deliver me from my persecutors, for they are stronger than me.

8208.text: Bring my soul out of prison, that I may give thanks to your name. The righteous will surround me, for you will be good to me.

8209.text: Hear my prayer, Lord. Listen to my petitions. In your faithfulness and righteousness, relieve me.

8210.text: Do not enter into judgment with your servant, for in your sight no man living is righteous.

8212.text: Therefore my spirit is overwhelmed within me. My heart within me is desolate.

8213.text: I remember the days of old. I meditate on all your doings. I contemplate the work of your hands.

8214.text: I spread forth my hands to you. My soul thirsts for you, like a parched land. Selah.

8215.text: Hurry to answer me, Lord. My spirit fails. Do not hide your face from me, so that I do not become like those who go down into the pit.

8216.text: Cause me to hear your loving kindness in the morning, for I trust in you. Cause me to know the way in which I should walk, for I lift up my soul to you.

8217.text: Deliver me, Lord, from my enemies. I flee to you to hide me.

8218.text: Teach me to do your will, for you are my God. Your Spirit is good. Lead me in the land of uprightness.

8219.text: Revive me, Lord, for your name's sake. In your righteousness, bring my soul out of trouble.

8220.text: In your loving kindness, cut off my enemies, and destroy all those who afflict my soul, For I am your servant.

8221.text: Blessed be the Lord, my rock, who teaches my hands to war, and my fingers to battle:

8222.text: my loving kindness, my fortress, my high tower, my deliverer, my shield, and he in whom I take refuge; who subdues my people under me.

8223.text: Lord, what is man, that you care for him? Or the son of man, that you think of him?

8231.text: Rescue me, and deliver me out of the hands of foreigners, whose mouths speak deceit, whose right hand is a right hand of falsehood.

8238.text: Great is the Lord, and greatly to be praised! His greatness is unsearchable.

8242.text: They will utter the memory of your great goodness, and will sing of your righteousness.

8243.text: The Lord is gracious, merciful, slow to anger, and of great loving kindness.

8251.text: You open your hand, and satisfy the desire of every living thing.

8261.text: Happy is he who has the God of Jacob for his help, whose hope is in the Lord, his God:

8262.text: who made heaven and earth, the sea, and all that is in them; who keeps truth forever;

8263.text: who executes justice for the oppressed; who gives food to the hungry. The Lord frees the prisoners.

8264.text: The Lord opens the eyes of the blind. The Lord raises up those who are bowed down. The Lord loves the righteous.

8265.text: The Lord preserves the foreigners. He upholds the fatherless and widow, but the way of the wicked he turns upside down.

8266.text: The Lord will reign forever; your God, O Zion, to all generations. Praise Yah!

8267.text: Praise Yah, for it is good to sing praises to our God; for it is pleasant and fitting to praise him.

8268.text: The Lord builds up Jerusalem. He gathers together the outcasts of Israel.

8269.text: He heals the broken in heart, and binds up their wounds.

8270.text: He counts the number of the stars. He calls them all by their names.

8271.text: Great is our Lord, and mighty in power. His understanding is infinite.

8272.text: The Lord upholds the humble. He brings the wicked down to the ground.

8273.text: Sing to the Lord with thanksgiving. Sing praises on the harp to our God,

8274.text: who covers the sky with clouds, who prepares rain for the earth, who makes grass grow on the mountains.

8275.text: He provides food for the livestock, and for the young ravens when they call.

8276.text: He doesn't delight in the strength of the horse. He takes no pleasure in the legs of a man.

8277.text: The Lord takes pleasure in those who fear him, in those who hope in his loving kindness.

8278.text: Praise the Lord, Jerusalem! Praise your God, Zion!

8279.text: For he has strengthened the bars of your gates. He has blessed your children within you.

8280.text: He makes peace in your borders. He fills you with the finest of the wheat.

8281.text: He sends out his commandment to the earth. His word runs very swiftly.

8282.text: He gives snow like wool, and scatters frost like ashes.

8283.text: He hurls down his hail like pebbles. Who can stand before his cold?

8284.text: He sends out his word, and melts them. He causes his wind to blow, and the waters flow.

8285.text: He shows his word to Jacob; his statutes and his ordinances to Israel.

8286.text: He has not done this for just any nation. They do not know his ordinances. Praise Yah!

8287.text: Praise Yah! Praise the Lord from the heavens! Praise him in the heights!

8288.text: Praise him, all his angels! Praise him, all his army!

8289.text: Praise him, sun and moon! Praise him, all you shining stars!

8290.text: Praise him, you heavens of heavens, You waters that are above the heavens.

8291.text: Let them praise the name of the Lord, For he commanded, and they were created.

8292.text: He has also established them forever and ever. He has made a decree which will not pass away.

8293.text: Praise the Lord from the earth, you great sea creatures, and all depths!

8294.text: Lightning and hail, snow and clouds; stormy wind, fulfilling his word;

8295.text: mountains and all hills; fruit trees and all cedars;

8296.text: wild animals and all livestock; small creatures and flying birds;

8297.text: kings of the earth and all peoples; princes and all judges of the earth;

8298.text: both young men and maidens; old men and children:

8299.text: let them praise the name of the Lord, for his name alone is exalted. His glory is above the earth and the heavens.

8300.text: He has lifted up the horn of his people, the praise of all his holy ones; even of the children of Israel, a people near to him. Praise Yah!

8301.text: Praise Yah! Sing to the Lord a new song, his praise in the assembly of the holy ones.

8302.text: Let Israel rejoice in him who made them. Let the children of Zion be joyful in their King.

8303.text: Let them praise his name in the dance! Let them sing praises to him with tambourine and harp!

8304.text: For the Lord takes pleasure in his people. He crowns the humble with salvation.

8305.text: Let the holy ones rejoice in honor. Let them sing for joy on their beds.

8306.text: May the high praises of God be in their mouths, and a two-edged sword in their hand;

8307.text: To execute vengeance on the nations, and punishments on the peoples;

8308.text: To bind their kings with chains, and their nobles with fetters of iron;

8309.text: to execute on them the written judgment. All his holy ones have this honor. Praise Yah!

8310.text: Praise Yah! Praise God in his sanctuary! Praise him in his heavens for his acts of power!

8311.text: Praise him for his mighty acts! Praise him according to his excellent greatness!

8312.text: Praise him with the sounding of the trumpet! Praise him with harp and lyre!

8313.text: Praise him with tambourine and dancing! Praise him with stringed instruments and flute!

8314.text: Praise him with loud cymbals! Praise him with resounding cymbals!

8315.text: Let everything that has breath praise Yah! Praise Yah!

8316.text: The proverbs of Solomon, the son of David, king of Israel:

8317.text: to know wisdom and instruction; to discern the words of understanding;

8318.text: to receive instruction in wise dealing, in righteousness, justice, and equity;

8319.text: to give prudence to the simple, knowledge and discretion to the young man:

8320.text: that the wise man may hear, and increase in learning; that the man of understanding may attain to sound counsel:

8321.text: to understand a proverb, and parables, the words and riddles of the wise.

8322.text: The fear of the Lord is the beginning of knowledge; but the foolish despise wisdom and instruction.

8323.text: My son, listen to your father's instruction, and do not forsake your mother's teaching:

8324.text: for they will be a garland to grace your head, and chains around your neck.

8325.text: My son, if sinners entice you, do not consent.

8326.text: If they say, "Come with us, Let's lie in wait for blood; let's lurk secretly for the innocent without cause;

8327.text: let's swallow them up alive like Sheol, and whole, like those who go down into the pit.

8328.text: We'll find all valuable wealth. We'll fill our houses with spoil.

8329.text: You shall cast your lot among us. We'll all have one purse."

8330.text: My son, do not walk in the way with them. Keep your foot from their path,

8331.text: for their feet run to evil. They hurry to shed blood.

8332.text: For in vain is the net spread in the sight of any bird:

8333.text: but these lie in wait for their own blood. They lurk secretly for their own lives.

8334.text: So are the ways of everyone who is greedy for gain. It takes away the life of its owners.

8335.text: Wisdom calls aloud in the street. She utters her voice in the public squares.

8336.text: She calls at the head of noisy places. At the entrance of the city gates, she utters her words:

8337.text: "How long, you simple ones, will you love simplicity? How long will mockers delight themselves in mockery, and fools hate knowledge?

8338.text: Turn at my reproof. Behold, I will pour out my spirit on you. I will make known my words to you.

8339.text: Because I have called, and you have refused; I have stretched out my hand, and no one has paid attention;

8340.text: but you have ignored all my counsel, and wanted none of my reproof;

8341.text: I also will laugh at your disaster. I will mock when calamity overtakes you;

8342.text: when calamity overtakes you like a storm, when your disaster comes on like a whirlwind; when distress and anguish come on you.

8343.text: Then will they call on me, but I will not answer. They will seek me diligently, but they will not find me;

8344.text: because they hated knowledge, and did not choose the fear of the Lord.

8345.text: They wanted none of my counsel. They despised all my reproof.

8346.text: Therefore they will eat of the fruit of their own way, and be filled with their own schemes.

8347.text: For the backsliding of the simple will kill them. The careless ease of fools will destroy them.

8348.text: But whoever listens to me will dwell securely, and will be at ease, without fear of harm."

8349.text: My son, if you will receive my words, and store up my commandments within you;

8350.text: So as to turn your ear to wisdom, and apply your heart to understanding;

8351.text: Yes, if you call out for discernment, and lift up your voice for understanding;

8352.text: If you seek her as silver, and search for her as for hidden treasures:

8353.text: then you will understand the fear of the Lord, and find the knowledge of God.

8354.text: For the Lord gives wisdom. Out of his mouth comes knowledge and understanding.

8355.text: He lays up sound wisdom for the upright. He is a shield to those who walk in integrity;

8356.text: that he may guard the paths of justice, and preserve the way of his holy ones.

8357.text: Then you will understand righteousness and justice, equity and every good path.

8358.text: For wisdom will enter into your heart. Knowledge will be pleasant to your soul.

8359.text: Discretion will watch over you. Understanding will keep you,

8360.text: to deliver you from the way of evil, from the men who speak perverse things;

8361.text: who forsake the paths of uprightness, to walk in the ways of darkness;

8362.text: who rejoice to do evil, and delight in the perverseness of evil;

8363.text: who are crooked in their ways, and wayward in their paths:

8364.text: To deliver you from the strange woman, even from the foreigner who flatters with her words;

8365.text: who forsakes the friend of her youth, and forgets the covenant of her God:

8366.text: for her house leads down to death, her paths to the dead.

8367.text: None who go to her return again, neither do they attain to the paths of life:

8368.text: that you may walk in the way of good men, and keep the paths of the righteous.

8369.text: For the upright will dwell in the land. The perfect will remain in it.

8370.text: But the wicked will be cut off from the land. The treacherous will be rooted out of it.

8371.text: My son, do not forget my teaching; but let your heart keep my commandments:

8372.text: for length of days, and years of life, and peace, will they add to you.

8373.text: Do not let kindness and truth forsake you. Bind them around your neck. Write them on the tablet of your heart.

8374.text: So you will find favor, and good understanding in the sight of God and man.

8375.text: Trust in the Lord with all your heart, and do not lean on your own understanding.

8376.text: In all your ways acknowledge him, and he will make your paths straight.

8377.text: Do not be wise in your own eyes. Fear the Lord, and depart from evil.

8378.text: It will be health to your body, and nourishment to your bones.

8379.text: Honor the Lord with your substance, with the first fruits of all your increase:

8380.text: so your barns will be filled with plenty, and your vats will overflow with new wine.

8381.text: My son, do not despise the Lord's discipline, neither be weary of his reproof:

8382.text: for whom the Lord loves, he reproves; even as a father reproves the son in whom he delights.

8383.text: Happy is the man who finds wisdom, the man who gets understanding.

8384.text: For her good profit is better than getting silver, and her return is better than fine gold.

8385.text: She is more precious than rubies. None of the things you can desire are to be compared to her.

8386.text: Length of days is in her right hand. In her left hand are riches and honor.

8387.text: Her ways are ways of pleasantness. All her paths are peace.

8388.text: She is a tree of life to those who lay hold of her. Happy is everyone who retains her.

8389.text: By wisdom the Lord founded the earth. By understanding, he established the heavens.

8390.text: By his knowledge, the depths were broken up, and the skies drop down the dew.

8391.text: My son, let them not depart from your eyes. Keep sound wisdom and discretion:

8392.text: so they will be life to your soul, and grace for your neck.

8393.text: Then you shall walk in your way securely. Your foot won't stumble.

8394.text: When you lie down, you will not be afraid. Yes, you will lie down, and your sleep will be sweet.

8395.text: Do not be afraid of sudden fear, neither of the desolation of the wicked, when it comes:

8396.text: for the Lord will be your confidence, and will keep your foot from being taken.

8397.text: Do not withhold good from those to whom it is due, when it is in the power of your hand to do it.

8398.text: Do not say to your neighbor, "Go, and come again; tomorrow I will give it to you," when you have it by you.

8399.text: Do not devise evil against your neighbor, seeing he dwells securely by you.

8400.text: Do not strive with a man without cause, if he has done you no harm.

8401.text: Do not envy the man of violence. Choose none of his ways.

8402.text: For the perverse is an abomination to the Lord, but his friendship is with the upright.

8403.text: The Lord's curse is in the house of the wicked, but he blesses the habitation of the righteous.

8404.text: Surely he is scornful to scoffers, but he gives grace to the humble.

8405.text: The wise will inherit glory, but shame will be the promotion of fools.

8406.text: Listen, sons, to a father's instruction. Pay attention and know understanding;

8407.text: for I give you sound learning. Do not forsake my law.

8408.text: For I was a son to my father, tender and an only child in the sight of my mother.

8409.text: He taught me, and said to me: "Let your heart retain my words. Keep my commandments, and live.

8410.text: Get wisdom. Get understanding. Do not forget, neither swerve from the words of my mouth.

8411.text: Do not forsake her, and she will preserve you. Love her, and she will keep you.

8412.text: Wisdom is supreme. Get wisdom. Yes, though it costs all your possessions, get understanding.

8413.text: Esteem her, and she will exalt you. She will bring you to honor, when you embrace her.

8414.text: She will give to your head a garland of grace. She will deliver a crown of splendor to you."

8415.text: Listen, my son, and receive my sayings. The years of your life will be many.

8416.text: I have taught you in the way of wisdom. I have led you in straight paths.

8417.text: When you go, your steps will not be hampered. When you run, you will not stumble.

8418.text: Take firm hold of instruction. Do not let her go. Keep her, for she is your life.

8419.text: Do not enter into the path of the wicked. Do not walk in the way of evil men.

8420.text: Avoid it, and do not pass by it. Turn from it, and pass on.

8421.text: For they do not sleep, unless they do evil. Their sleep is taken away, unless they make someone fall.

8422.text: For they eat the bread of wickedness, and drink the wine of violence.

8423.text: But the path of the righteous is like the dawning light, that shines more and more until the perfect day.

8424.text: The way of the wicked is like darkness. They do not know what they stumble over.

8425.text: My son, attend to my words. Turn your ear to my sayings.

8426.text: Let them not depart from your eyes. Keep them in the midst of your heart.

8427.text: For they are life to those who find them, and health to their whole body.

8428.text: Keep your heart with all diligence, for out of it is the wellspring of life.

8429.text: Put away from yourself a perverse mouth. Put corrupt lips far from you.

8430.text: Let your eyes look straight ahead. Fix your gaze directly before you.

8431.text: Make the path of your feet level. Let all of your ways be established.

8432.text: Do not turn to the right hand nor to the left. Remove your foot from evil.

8433.text: My son, pay attention to my wisdom. Turn your ear to my understanding:

8434.text: that you may maintain discretion, that your lips may preserve knowledge.

8435.text: For the lips of an adulteress drip honey. Her mouth is smoother than oil,

8436.text: But in the end she is as bitter as wormwood, and as sharp as a two-edged sword.

8437.text: Her feet go down to death. Her steps lead straight to Sheol.

8438.text: She gives no thought to the way of life. Her ways are crooked, and she doesn't know it.

8439.text: Now therefore, my sons, listen to me. Do not depart from the words of my mouth.

8440.text: Remove your way far from her. Do not come near the door of her house,

8441.text: lest you give your honor to others, and your years to the cruel one;

8442.text: lest strangers feast on your wealth, and your labors enrich another man's house.

8443.text: You will groan at your latter end, when your flesh and your body are consumed,

8444.text: and say, "How I have hated instruction, and my heart despised reproof;

8445.text: neither have I obeyed the voice of my teachers, nor turned my ear to those who instructed me!

8446.text: I have come to the brink of utter ruin, in the midst of the gathered assembly."

8447.text: Drink water out of your own cistern, running water out of your own well.

8448.text: Should your springs overflow in the streets, streams of water in the public squares?

8449.text: Let them be for yourself alone, not for strangers with you.

8450.text: Let your spring be blessed. Rejoice in the wife of your youth.

8451.text: A loving doe and a graceful deer- let her breasts satisfy you at all times. Be captivated always with her love.

8452.text: For why should you, my son, be captivated with an adulteress? Why embrace the bosom of another?

8453.text: For the ways of man are before the eyes of the Lord. He examines all his paths.

8454.text: The evil deeds of the wicked ensnare him. The cords of his sin hold him firmly.

8455.text: He will die for lack of instruction. In the greatness of his folly, he will go astray.

8456.text: My son, if you have become collateral for your neighbor, if you have struck your hands in pledge for a stranger;

8457.text: You are trapped by the words of your mouth. You are ensnared with the words of your mouth.

8458.text: Do this now, my son, and deliver yourself, seeing you have come into the hand of your neighbor. Go, humble yourself. Press your plea with your neighbor.

8459.text: Give no sleep to your eyes, nor slumber to your eyelids.

8460.text: Free yourself, like a gazelle from the hand of the hunter, like a bird from the snare of the fowler.

8461.text: Go to the ant, you sluggard. Consider her ways, and be wise;

8462.text: which having no chief, overseer, or ruler,

8463.text: provides her bread in the summer, and gathers her food in the harvest.

8464.text: How long will you sleep, sluggard? When will you arise out of your sleep?

8465.text: A little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to sleep:

8466.text: so your poverty will come as a robber, and your scarcity as an armed man.

8467.text: A worthless person, a man of iniquity, is he who walks with a perverse mouth;

8468.text: who winks with his eyes, who signals with his feet, who motions with his fingers;

8469.text: in whose heart is perverseness, who devises evil continually, who always sows discord.

8470.text: Therefore his calamity will come suddenly. He will be broken suddenly, and that without remedy.

8471.text: There are six things which the Lord hates; yes, seven which are an abomination to him:

8472.text: haughty eyes, a lying tongue, hands that shed innocent blood;

8473.text: a heart that devises wicked schemes, feet that are swift in running to mischief,

8474.text: a false witness who utters lies, and he who sows discord among brothers.

8475.text: My son, keep your father's commandment, and do not forsake your mother's teaching.

8476.text: Bind them continually on your heart. Tie them around your neck.

8477.text: When you walk, it will lead you. When you sleep, it will watch over you. When you awake, it will talk with you.

8478.text: For the commandment is a lamp, and the Law is light. Reproofs of instruction are the way of life,

8479.text: to keep you from the immoral woman, from the flattery of the wayward wife's tongue.

8480.text: Do not lust after her beauty in your heart, neither let her captivate you with her eyelids.

8481.text: For a prostitute reduces you to a piece of bread. The adulteress hunts for your precious life.

8482.text: Can a man scoop fire into his lap, and his clothes not be burned?

8483.text: Or can one walk on hot coals, and his feet not be scorched?

8484.text: So is he who goes in to his neighbor's wife. Whoever touches her will not be unpunished.

8485.text: Men do not despise a thief, if he steals to satisfy himself when he is hungry:

8486.text: but if he is found, he shall restore seven times. He shall give all the wealth of his house.

8487.text: He who commits adultery with a woman is void of understanding. He who does it destroys his own soul.

8488.text: He will get wounds and dishonor. His reproach will not be wiped away.

8489.text: For jealousy arouses the fury of the husband. He won't spare in the day of vengeance.

8490.text: He won't regard any ransom, neither will he rest content, though you give many gifts.

8491.text: My son, keep my words. Lay up my commandments within you.

8492.text: Keep my commandments and live! Guard my teaching as the apple of your eye.

8493.text: Bind them on your fingers. Write them on the tablet of your heart.

8494.text: Tell wisdom, "You are my sister." Call understanding your relative,

8495.text: that they may keep you from the strange woman, from the foreigner who flatters with her words.

8496.text: For at the window of my house, I looked out through my lattice.

8497.text: I saw among the simple ones. I discerned among the youths a young man void of understanding,

8498.text: passing through the street near her corner, he went the way to her house,

8499.text: in the twilight, in the evening of the day, in the middle of the night and in the darkness.

8500.text: Behold, there a woman met him with the attire of a prostitute, and with crafty intent.

8501.text: She is loud and defiant. Her feet do not stay in her house.

8502.text: Now she is in the streets, now in the squares, and lurking at every corner.

8503.text: So she caught him, and kissed him. With an impudent face she said to him:

8504.text: "Sacrifices of peace offerings are with me. This day I have paid my vows.

8505.text: Therefore I came out to meet you, to diligently seek your face, and I have found you.

8506.text: I have spread my couch with carpets of tapestry, with striped cloths of the yarn of Egypt.

8507.text: I have perfumed my bed with myrrh, aloes, and cinnamon.

8508.text: Come, let's take our fill of loving until the morning. Let's solace ourselves with loving.

8509.text: For my husband isn't at home. He has gone on a long journey.

8510.text: He has taken a bag of money with him. He will come home at the full moon."

8511.text: With persuasive words, she led him astray. With the flattering of her lips, she seduced him.

8512.text: He followed her immediately, as an ox goes to the slaughter, as a fool stepping into a noose.

8513.text: Until an arrow strikes through his liver, as a bird hurries to the snare, and doesn't know that it will cost his life.

8514.text: Now therefore, sons, listen to me. Pay attention to the words of my mouth.

8515.text: Do not let your heart turn to her ways. Do not go astray in her paths,

8516.text: for she has thrown down many wounded. Yes, all her slain are a mighty army.

8517.text: Her house is the way to Sheol, going down to the chambers of death.

8518.text: Doesn't wisdom cry out? Doesn't understanding raise her voice?

8519.text: On the top of high places by the way, where the paths meet, she stands.

8520.text: Beside the gates, at the entry of the city, at the entry doors, she cries aloud:

8521.text: "To you men, I call! I send my voice to the sons of mankind.

8522.text: You simple, understand prudence. You fools, be of an understanding heart.

8523.text: Hear, for I will speak excellent things. The opening of my lips is for right things.

8524.text: For my mouth speaks truth. Wickedness is an abomination to my lips.

8525.text: All the words of my mouth are in righteousness. There is nothing crooked or perverse in them.

8526.text: They are all plain to him who understands, right to those who find knowledge.

8527.text: Receive my instruction rather than silver; knowledge rather than choice gold.

8528.text: For wisdom is better than rubies. All the things that may be desired can't be compared to it.

8529.text: "I, wisdom, have made prudence my dwelling. Find out knowledge and discretion.

8530.text: The fear of the Lord is to hate evil. I hate pride, arrogance, the evil way, and the perverse mouth.

8531.text: Counsel and sound knowledge are mine. I have understanding and power.

8532.text: By me kings reign, and princes decree justice.

8533.text: By me princes rule; nobles, and all the righteous rulers of the earth.

8534.text: I love those who love me. Those who seek me diligently will find me.

8535.text: With me are riches, honor, enduring wealth, and prosperity.

8536.text: My fruit is better than gold, yes, than fine gold; my yield than choice silver.

8537.text: I walk in the way of righteousness, in the midst of the paths of justice;

8538.text: That I may give wealth to those who love me. I fill their treasuries.

8539.text: "The Lord possessed me in the beginning of his work, before his deeds of old.

8540.text: I was set up from everlasting, from the beginning, before the earth existed.

8541.text: When there were no depths, I was brought forth, when there were no springs abounding with water.

8542.text: Before the mountains were settled in place, before the hills, I was brought forth;

8543.text: while as yet he had not made the earth, nor the fields, nor the beginning of the dust of the world.

8544.text: When he established the heavens, I was there; when he set a circle on the surface of the deep,

8545.text: when he established the clouds above, when the springs of the deep became strong,

8546.text: when he gave to the sea its boundary, that the waters should not violate his commandment, when he marked out the foundations of the earth;

8547.text: then I was the craftsman by his side. I was a delight day by day, always rejoicing before him,

8548.text: Rejoicing in his whole world. My delight was with the sons of men.

8549.text: "Now therefore, my sons, listen to me, for blessed are those who keep my ways.

8550.text: Hear instruction, and be wise. Do not refuse it.

8551.text: Blessed is the man who hears me, watching daily at my gates, waiting at my door posts.

8552.text: For whoever finds me, finds life, and will obtain favor from the Lord.

8553.text: But he who sins against me wrongs his own soul. All those who hate me love death."

8554.text: Wisdom has built her house. She has carved out her seven pillars.

8555.text: She has prepared her meat. She has mixed her wine. She has also set her table.

8556.text: She has sent out her maidens. She cries from the highest places of the city:

8557.text: "Whoever is simple, let him turn in here!" As for him who is void of understanding, she says to him,

8558.text: "Come, eat some of my bread, Drink some of the wine which I have mixed!

8559.text: Leave your simple ways, and live. Walk in the way of understanding."

8560.text: He who corrects a mocker invites insult. He who reproves a wicked man invites abuse.

8561.text: Do not reprove a scoffer, lest he hate you. Reprove a wise man, and he will love you.

8562.text: Instruct a wise man, and he will be still wiser. Teach a righteous man, and he will increase in learning.

8563.text: The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom. The knowledge of the Holy One is understanding.

8564.text: For by me your days will be multiplied. The years of your life will be increased.

8565.text: If you are wise, you are wise for yourself. If you mock, you alone will bear it.

8566.text: The foolish woman is loud, Undisciplined, and knows nothing.

8567.text: She sits at the door of her house, on a seat in the high places of the city,

8568.text: To call to those who pass by, who go straight on their ways,

8569.text: "Whoever is simple, let him turn in here." as for him who is void of understanding, she says to him,

8570.text: "Stolen water is sweet. Food eaten in secret is pleasant."

8571.text: But he doesn't know that the dead are there, that her guests are in the depths of Sheol.

8572.text: The proverbs of Solomon. A wise son makes a glad father; but a foolish son brings grief to his mother.

8573.text: Treasures of wickedness profit nothing, but righteousness delivers from death.

8574.text: The Lord will not allow the soul of the righteous to go hungry, but he thrusts away the desire of the wicked.

8575.text: He becomes poor who works with a lazy hand, but the hand of the diligent brings wealth.

8576.text: He who gathers in summer is a wise son, but he who sleeps during the harvest is a son who causes shame.

8577.text: Blessings are on the head of the righteous, but violence covers the mouth of the wicked.

8578.text: The memory of the righteous is blessed, but the name of the wicked will rot.

8579.text: The wise in heart accept commandments, but a chattering fool will fall.

8580.text: He who walks blamelessly walks surely, but he who perverts his ways will be found out.

8581.text: One winking with the eye causes sorrow, but a chattering fool will fall.

8582.text: The mouth of the righteous is a spring of life, but violence covers the mouth of the wicked.

8583.text: Hatred stirs up strife, but love covers all wrongs.

8584.text: Wisdom is found on the lips of him who has discernment, but a rod is for the back of him who is void of understanding.

8585.text: Wise men lay up knowledge, but the mouth of the foolish is near ruin.

8586.text: The rich man's wealth is his strong city. The destruction of the poor is their poverty.

8587.text: The labor of the righteous leads to life. The increase of the wicked leads to sin.

8588.text: He is in the way of life who heeds correction, but he who forsakes reproof leads others astray.

8589.text: He who hides hatred has lying lips. He who utters a slander is a fool.

8590.text: In the multitude of words there is no lack of disobedience, but he who restrains his lips does wisely.

8591.text: The tongue of the righteous is like choice silver. The heart of the wicked is of little worth.

8592.text: The lips of the righteous feed many, but the foolish die for lack of understanding.

8593.text: The Lord's blessing brings wealth, and he adds no trouble to it.

8594.text: It is a fool's pleasure to do wickedness, but wisdom is a man of understanding's pleasure.

8595.text: What the wicked fear, will overtake them, but the desire of the righteous will be granted.

8596.text: When the whirlwind passes, the wicked is no more; but the righteous stand firm forever.

8597.text: As vinegar to the teeth, and as smoke to the eyes, so is the sluggard to those who send him.

8598.text: The fear of the Lord prolongs days, but the years of the wicked shall be shortened.

8599.text: The prospect of the righteous is joy, but the hope of the wicked will perish.

8600.text: The way of the Lord is a stronghold to the upright, but it is a destruction to the workers of iniquity.

8601.text: The righteous will never be removed, but the wicked will not dwell in the land.

8602.text: The mouth of the righteous brings forth wisdom, but the perverse tongue will be cut off.

8603.text: The lips of the righteous know what is acceptable, but the mouth of the wicked is perverse.

8604.text: A false balance is an abomination to the Lord, but accurate weights are his delight.

8605.text: When pride comes, then comes shame, but with humility comes wisdom.

8606.text: The integrity of the upright shall guide them, but the perverseness of the treacherous shall destroy them.

8607.text: Riches do not profit in the day of wrath, but righteousness delivers from death.

8608.text: The righteousness of the blameless will direct his way, but the wicked shall fall by his own wickedness.

8609.text: The righteousness of the upright shall deliver them, but the unfaithful will be trapped by evil desires.

8610.text: When a wicked man dies, hope perishes, and expectation of power comes to nothing.

8611.text: A righteous person is delivered out of trouble, and the wicked takes his place.

8612.text: With his mouth the godless man destroys his neighbor, but the righteous will be delivered through knowledge.

8613.text: When it goes well with the righteous, the city rejoices. When the wicked perish, there is shouting.

8614.text: By the blessing of the upright, the city is exalted, but it is overthrown by the mouth of the wicked.

8615.text: One who despises his neighbor is void of wisdom, but a man of understanding holds his peace.

8616.text: One who brings gossip betrays a confidence, but one who is of a trustworthy spirit is one who keeps a secret.

8617.text: Where there is no wise guidance, the nation falls, but in the multitude of counselors there is victory.

8618.text: He who is collateral for a stranger will suffer for it, but he who refuses pledges of collateral is secure.

8619.text: A gracious woman obtains honor, but violent men obtain riches.

8620.text: The merciful man does good to his own soul, but he who is cruel troubles his own flesh.

8621.text: Wicked people earn deceitful wages, but one who sows righteousness reaps a sure reward.

8622.text: He who is truly righteous gets life. He who pursues evil gets death.

8623.text: Those who are perverse in heart are an abomination to the Lord, but those whose ways are blameless are his delight.

8624.text: Most certainly, the evil man will not be unpunished, but the seed of the righteous will be delivered.

8625.text: Like a gold ring in a pig's snout, is a beautiful woman who lacks discretion.

8626.text: The desire of the righteous is only good. The expectation of the wicked is wrath.

8627.text: There is one who scatters, and increases yet more. There is one who withholds more than is appropriate, but gains poverty.

8628.text: The liberal soul shall be made fat. He who waters shall be watered also himself.

8629.text: People curse someone who withholds grain, but blessing will be on the head of him who sells it.

8630.text: He who diligently seeks good seeks favor, but he who searches after evil, it shall come to him.

8631.text: He who trusts in his riches will fall, but the righteous shall flourish as the green leaf.

8632.text: He who troubles his own house shall inherit the wind. The foolish shall be servant to the wise of heart.

8633.text: The fruit of the righteous is a tree of life. He who is wise wins souls.

8634.text: Behold, the righteous shall be repaid in the earth; how much more the wicked and the sinner!

8635.text: Whoever loves correction loves knowledge, but he who hates reproof is stupid.

8636.text: A good man shall obtain favor from the Lord, but he will condemn a man of wicked devices.

8637.text: A man shall not be established by wickedness, but the root of the righteous shall not be moved.

8638.text: A worthy woman is the crown of her husband, but a disgraceful wife is as rottenness in his bones.

8639.text: The thoughts of the righteous are just, but the advice of the wicked is deceitful.

8640.text: The words of the wicked are about lying in wait for blood, but the speech of the upright rescues them.

8641.text: The wicked are overthrown, and are no more, but the house of the righteous shall stand.

8642.text: A man shall be commended according to his wisdom, but he who has a warped mind shall be despised.

8643.text: Better is he who is lightly esteemed, and has a servant, than he who honors himself, and lacks bread.

8644.text: A righteous man regards the life of his animal, but the tender mercies of the wicked are cruel.

8645.text: He who tills his land shall have plenty of bread, but he who chases fantasies is void of understanding.

8646.text: The wicked desires the plunder of evil men, but the root of the righteous flourishes.

8647.text: An evil man is trapped by sinfulness of lips, but the righteous shall come out of trouble.

8648.text: A man shall be satisfied with good by the fruit of his mouth. The work of a man's hands shall be rewarded to him.

8649.text: The way of a fool is right in his own eyes, but he who is wise listens to counsel.

8650.text: A fool shows his annoyance the same day, but one who overlooks an insult is prudent.

8651.text: He who is truthful testifies honestly, but a false witness lies.

8652.text: There is one who speaks rashly like the piercing of a sword, but the tongue of the wise heals.

8653.text: Truth's lips will be established forever, but a lying tongue is only momentary.

8654.text: Deceit is in the heart of those who plot evil, but joy comes to the promoters of peace.

8655.text: No mischief shall happen to the righteous, but the wicked shall be filled with evil.

8656.text: Lying lips are an abomination to the Lord, but those who do the truth are his delight.

8657.text: A prudent man keeps his knowledge, but the hearts of fools proclaim foolishness.

8658.text: The hands of the diligent ones shall rule, but laziness ends in slave labor.

8659.text: Anxiety in a man's heart weighs it down, but a kind word makes it glad.

8660.text: A righteous person is cautious in friendship, but the way of the wicked leads them astray.

8661.text: The slothful man doesn't roast his game, but the possessions of diligent men are prized.

8662.text: In the way of righteousness is life; in its path there is no death.

8663.text: A wise son listens to his father's instruction, but a scoffer doesn't listen to rebuke.

8664.text: By the fruit of his lips, a man enjoys good things; but the unfaithful crave violence.

8665.text: He who guards his mouth guards his soul. One who opens wide his lips comes to ruin.

8666.text: The soul of the sluggard desires, and has nothing, but the desire of the diligent shall be fully satisfied.

8667.text: A righteous man hates lies, but a wicked man brings shame and disgrace.

8668.text: Righteousness guards the way of integrity, but wickedness overthrows the sinner.

8669.text: There are some who pretend to be rich, yet have nothing. There are some who pretend to be poor, yet have great wealth.

8670.text: The ransom of a man's life is his riches, but the poor hear no threats.

8671.text: The light of the righteous shines brightly, but the lamp of the wicked is snuffed out.

8672.text: Pride only breeds quarrels, but with ones who take advice is wisdom.

8673.text: Wealth gained dishonestly dwindles away, but he who gathers by hand makes it grow.

8674.text: Hope deferred makes the heart sick, but when longing is fulfilled, it is a tree of life.

8675.text: Whoever despises instruction will pay for it, but he who respects a command will be rewarded.

8676.text: The teaching of the wise is a spring of life, to turn from the snares of death.

8677.text: Good understanding wins favor; but the way of the unfaithful is hard.

8678.text: Every prudent man acts from knowledge, but a fool exposes folly.

8679.text: A wicked messenger falls into trouble, but a trustworthy envoy gains healing.

8680.text: Poverty and shame come to him who refuses discipline, but he who heeds correction shall be honored.

8681.text: Longing fulfilled is sweet to the soul, but fools detest turning from evil.

8682.text: One who walks with wise men grows wise, but a companion of fools suffers harm.

8683.text: Misfortune pursues sinners, but prosperity rewards the righteous.

8684.text: A good man leaves an inheritance to his children's children, but the wealth of the sinner is stored for the righteous.

8685.text: An abundance of food is in poor people's fields, but injustice sweeps it away.

8686.text: One who spares the rod hates his son, but one who loves him is careful to discipline him.

8687.text: The righteous one eats to the satisfying of his soul, but the belly of the wicked goes hungry.

8688.text: Every wise woman builds her house, but the foolish one tears it down with her own hands.

8689.text: He who walks in his uprightness fears the Lord, but he who is perverse in his ways despises him.

8690.text: The fool's talk brings a rod to his back, but the lips of the wise protect them.

8691.text: Where no oxen are, the crib is clean, but much increase is by the strength of the ox.

8692.text: A truthful witness will not lie, but a false witness pours out lies.

8693.text: A scoffer seeks wisdom, and doesn't find it, but knowledge comes easily to a discerning person.

8694.text: Stay away from a foolish man, for you won't find knowledge on his lips.

8695.text: The wisdom of the prudent is to think about his way, but the folly of fools is deceit.

8696.text: Fools mock at making atonement for sins, but among the upright there is good will.

8697.text: The heart knows its own bitterness and joy; he will not share these with a stranger.

8698.text: The house of the wicked will be overthrown, but the tent of the upright will flourish.

8699.text: There is a way which seems right to a man, but in the end it leads to death.

8700.text: Even in laughter the heart may be sorrowful, and mirth may end in heaviness.

8701.text: The unfaithful will be repaid for his own ways; likewise a good man will be rewarded for his ways.

8702.text: A simple man believes everything, but the prudent man carefully considers his ways.

8703.text: A wise man fears, and shuns evil, but the fool is hotheaded and reckless.

8704.text: He who is quick to become angry will commit folly, and a crafty man is hated.

8705.text: The simple inherit folly, but the prudent are crowned with knowledge.

8706.text: The evil bow down before the good, and the wicked at the gates of the righteous.

8707.text: The poor person is shunned even by his own neighbor, but the rich person has many friends.

8708.text: He who despises his neighbor sins, but blessed is he who has pity on the poor.

8709.text: Do they not go astray who plot evil? But love and faithfulness belong to those who plan good.

8710.text: In all hard work there is profit, but the talk of the lips leads only to poverty.

8711.text: The crown of the wise is their riches, but the folly of fools crowns them with folly.

8712.text: A truthful witness saves souls, but a false witness is deceitful.

8713.text: In the fear of the Lord is a secure fortress, and he will be a refuge for his children.

8714.text: The fear of the Lord is a fountain of life, turning people from the snares of death.

8715.text: In the multitude of people is the king's glory, but in the lack of people is the destruction of the prince.

8716.text: He who is slow to anger has great understanding, but he who has a quick temper displays folly.

8717.text: The life of the body is a heart at peace, but envy rots the bones.

8718.text: He who oppresses the poor shows contempt for his Maker, but he who is kind to the needy honors him.

8719.text: The wicked is brought down in his calamity, but in death, the righteous has a refuge.

8720.text: Wisdom rests in the heart of one who has understanding, and is even made known in the inward part of fools.

8721.text: Righteousness exalts a nation, but sin is a disgrace to any people.

8722.text: The king's favor is toward a servant who deals wisely, but his wrath is toward one who causes shame.

8723.text: A gentle answer turns away wrath, but a harsh word stirs up anger.

8724.text: The tongue of the wise commends knowledge, but the mouth of fools gush out folly.

8725.text: The Lord's eyes are everywhere, keeping watch on the evil and the good.

8726.text: A gentle tongue is a tree of life, but deceit in it crushes the spirit.

8727.text: A fool despises his father's correction, but he who heeds reproof shows prudence.

8728.text: In the house of the righteous is much treasure, but the income of the wicked brings trouble.

8729.text: The lips of the wise spread knowledge; not so with the heart of fools.

8730.text: The sacrifice made by the wicked is an abomination to the Lord, but the prayer of the upright is his delight.

8731.text: The way of the wicked is an abomination to the Lord, but he loves him who follows after righteousness.

8732.text: There is stern discipline for one who forsakes the way: whoever hates reproof shall die.

8733.text: Sheol and Abaddon are before the Lord- how much more then the hearts of the children of men!

8734.text: A scoffer doesn't love to be reproved; he will not go to the wise.

8735.text: A glad heart makes a cheerful face; but an aching heart breaks the spirit.

8736.text: The heart of one who has understanding seeks knowledge, but the mouths of fools feed on folly.

8737.text: All the days of the afflicted are wretched, but one who has a cheerful heart enjoys a continual feast.

8738.text: Better is little, with the fear of the Lord, than great treasure with trouble.

8739.text: Better is a dinner of herbs, where love is, than a fattened calf with hatred.

8740.text: A wrathful man stirs up contention, but one who is slow to anger appeases strife.

8741.text: The way of the sluggard is like a thorn patch, but the path of the upright is a highway.

8742.text: A wise son makes a father glad, but a foolish man despises his mother.

8743.text: Folly is joy to one who is void of wisdom, but a man of understanding keeps his way straight.

8744.text: Where there is no counsel, plans fail; but in a multitude of counselors they are established.

8745.text: Joy comes to a man with the reply of his mouth. How good is a word at the right time!

8746.text: The path of life leads upward for the wise, to keep him from going downward to Sheol.

8747.text: The Lord will uproot the house of the proud, but he will keep the widow's borders intact.

8748.text: The Lord detests the thoughts of the wicked, but the thoughts of the pure are pleasing.

8749.text: He who is greedy for gain troubles his own house, but he who hates bribes will live.

8750.text: The heart of the righteous weighs answers, but the mouth of the wicked gushes out evil.

8751.text: The Lord is far from the wicked, but he hears the prayer of the righteous.

8752.text: The light of the eyes rejoices the heart. Good news gives health to the bones.

8753.text: The ear that listens to reproof lives, and will be at home among the wise.

8754.text: He who refuses correction despises his own soul, but he who listens to reproof gets understanding.

8755.text: The fear of the Lord teaches wisdom. Before honor is humility.

8756.text: The plans of the heart belong to man, but the answer of the tongue is from the Lord.

8757.text: All the ways of a man are clean in his own eyes; but the Lord weighs the motives.

8758.text: Commit your deeds to the Lord, and your plans shall succeed.

8759.text: The Lord has made everything for its own end- yes, even the wicked for the day of evil.

8760.text: Everyone who is proud in heart is an abomination to the Lord: they shall certainly not be unpunished.

8761.text: By mercy and truth iniquity is atoned for. By the fear of the Lord men depart from evil.

8762.text: When a man's ways please the Lord, he makes even his enemies to be at peace with him.

8763.text: Better is a little with righteousness, than great revenues with injustice.

8764.text: A man's heart plans his course, but the Lord directs his steps.

8765.text: Inspired judgments are on the lips of the king. He shall not betray his mouth.

8766.text: Honest balances and scales are the Lord's; all the weights in the bag are his work.

8767.text: It is an abomination for kings to do wrong, for the throne is established by righteousness.

8768.text: Righteous lips are the delight of kings. They value one who speaks the truth.

8769.text: The king's wrath is a messenger of death, but a wise man will pacify it.

8770.text: In the light of the king's face is life. His favor is like a cloud of the spring rain.

8771.text: How much better it is to get wisdom than gold! Yes, to get understanding is to be chosen rather than silver.

8772.text: The highway of the upright is to depart from evil. He who keeps his way preserves his soul.

8773.text: Pride goes before destruction, and a haughty spirit before a fall.

8774.text: It is better to be of a lowly spirit with the poor, than to divide the plunder with the proud.

8775.text: He who heeds the Word finds prosperity. Whoever trusts in the Lord is blessed.

8776.text: The wise in heart shall be called prudent. Pleasantness of the lips promotes instruction.

8777.text: Understanding is a fountain of life to one who has it, but the punishment of fools is their folly.

8778.text: The heart of the wise instructs his mouth, and adds learning to his lips.

8779.text: Pleasant words are a honeycomb, sweet to the soul, and health to the bones.

8780.text: There is a way which seems right to a man, but in the end it leads to death.

8781.text: The appetite of the laboring man labors for him; for his mouth urges him on.

8782.text: A worthless man devises mischief. His speech is like a scorching fire.

8783.text: A perverse man stirs up strife. A whisperer separates close friends.

8784.text: A man of violence entices his neighbor, and leads him in a way that is not good.

8785.text: One who winks his eyes to plot perversities, one who compresses his lips, is bent on evil.

8786.text: Gray hair is a crown of glory. It is attained by a life of righteousness.

8787.text: One who is slow to anger is better than the mighty; one who rules his spirit, than he who takes a city.

8788.text: The lot is cast into the lap, but its every decision is from the Lord.

8789.text: Better is a dry morsel with quietness, than a house full of feasting with strife.

8790.text: A servant who deals wisely will rule over a son who causes shame, and shall have a part in the inheritance among the brothers.

8791.text: The refining pot is for silver, and the furnace for gold, but the Lord tests the hearts.

8792.text: An evildoer heeds wicked lips. A liar gives ear to a mischievous tongue.

8793.text: Whoever mocks the poor reproaches his Maker. He who is glad at calamity shall not be unpunished.
